Had the suite been read quickly they would have looked like noise; they were four assertions checking nothing. (2) **`test_the_flag_gating_is_marked_observation_only` passed against the mutation that deleted the marker**, because the pre-existing sentence below already ends *"...not a failed call (INV-149)"*. A **403** is reachable on the bootcamp's most likely path — Python is the language most Bootcampers pick, the module tells the guide to fetch *"in whatever language the Bootcamper chose"*, and `urllib.request` is the zero-dependency client a guide reaches for first — and it had no next step, so collection simply stopped while a working route sat in the same response. **Criteria walk.** **(1) ✅** `SKILL.md:469` states the `download_url` preference **with its reason** (served to programmatic clients; needs only `mcp.senzing.com`, which is what survives restricted egress) — the reason is asserted separately, because a bare preference gets dropped by the next editor as arbitrary. **(2) ✅** Check 1 gains a 403 branch at `:500` that says retrying cannot help and routes to the other URL from the same citation; `test_403_routes_to_the_other_url_rather_than_retrying` asserts the instruction, not the digits. **(3) ⚠️ Implemented, NOT runtime-verified end to end.** The route now documented was measured **200** today from this machine, but "a Python guide can collect every source by following the module as written" is a claim about a live walk; it **needs a `dry-run` phase 3 pass collecting a CORD-backed generated scenario** — the run that found this. **(4) ✅** dated, client-named, marked *"Observation, not an MCP-sourced fact (INV-080/INV-149)"*. **(5) ✅** No shipped file instructs setting a User-Agent — scanned across all shipped markdown, with the prohibition self-pinned. **(6) ✅** 429 backoff and all three checks asserted intact. **(7) ✅** Nothing platform-specific: the rule is about which URL to use, in any language. **Guard:** 10 tests, stdlib-only (INV-108). Fixed by scoping every assertion to the acquisition **section** and to the blockquote itself, and by requiring the real-data sentence **in place** at every site with no delegation. **This is the fourth guard in this run weakened by matching a neighborhood instead of the claim**, and the second where only the negative control exposed it. ⚠️ **Two existing guards caught me**, which is the system working: `test_new_hard_rules_are_cited_or_deferred` failed until the deferral above was written, and `test_truthset_acquisition_call` rejected a bare `get_sample_data` reference I had put next to the word "requires" rather than "required" — reworded to name the sample-data tool without the bare call token, rather than touching the guard.

- **MCP re-check:** server **1.35.1**, 2026-09-01 — **confirmed, and re-measured from the live source rather than taken from the spec.** `get_sample_data(dataset='las-vegas', source='GLEIF')` and a full fetch of its 1,952 records return twelve root keys, four of them arrays of objects: `COUNTRIES` holds `REGISTRATION_COUNTRY`, `DATES` holds `REGISTRATION_DATE`, `RELATIONSHIPS` holds `REL_ANCHOR_*`/`REL_POINTER_*` — all resolving — while **`RISKS` holds `TOPIC` on 547 of the 1,952 records**. Checked against the served Entity Specification (`/resources/senzing_entity_specification.md`, fetched today): `TOPIC` appears in **no** feature table, while `NAME_ORG`, `ADDR_FULL`, `REGISTRATION_COUNTRY`, `REGISTRATION_DATE` and `LEI_NUMBER` all do. Attribute names were read from the **plain first column** of the feature tables, not by scanning for backticked tokens (INV-115) — a backtick-tuned parse returns **0** of them.
- **Summary:** The coverage check gates Step 5a's fast-path offer — the offer to skip the entire mapping module — and it partitioned only **root keys**, listing the structural set as four record-level keys plus "the legacy per-feature root sub-lists (`NAMES`, `ADDRESSES`, `IDENTIFIERS`, …)". On the legacy-flat shape the dispositionable content is one level down, and that ellipsis invited membership by resemblance: plural, uppercase, an array of objects — which is exactly what an *un*recognized array looks like. The structural set is now **closed and decided by contents**, the partition **recurses one level**, and the discriminator is stated outright. **Criterion walk, 6 of 6 hold.** (1) *The check examines the contents of root arrays* — asserted, and asserted as an **instruction** rather than as vocabulary. (2) *A source carrying a non-resolving root array is not fast-path eligible* — follows from counting its contained keys as unrecognized, which the unrecognized-keys bullet now says explicitly. (3) *Applied to GLEIF, `RISKS` is reported via `TOPIC`* — the worked case is recorded with its figures. (4) *Genuine sub-lists still classify as structural* — the three that resolve are named alongside the one that does not, and asserted, so the rule cannot be read as "distrust root arrays". (5) *The structural set is stated as closed with the contents test as its membership rule* — asserted. (6) *Cross-platform, language-agnostic* — prose.
- ⚠️ **I made this exact error while walking the step, which is how it was found.** The `/dry-run` coverage check filed `RISKS` as structural on the first pass and it surfaced only when the profiler printed the nested attribute inventory. GLEIF escaped a wrong fast-path offer by two unrelated root scalars (`LAST_CHANGE`, `URL`); a source without them would have been offered it with 547 records' worth of undispositioned content.
- ⚠️ **Four mutations, each verified to land** — open-ended structural set restored (1 failure); recursion instruction removed (1); provenance stripped from the worked case (1); worked case removed entirely (3). File verified byte-identical afterwards, `__pycache__` cleared.
- ⛔ **A guard weakness caught by negative control, and it is the SECOND of this shape in this run.** `test_the_partition_recurses_one_level` first matched `one level|contained keys` and **passed with the recursion sentence deleted**, because the unrecognized-keys bullet three lines above also says "contained keys". It now asserts the instruction (`partition one level down` / `same three-way test on the contained`). Together with the `merge-histogram` entry's comment-satisfies-the-assertion case and this run's own marker-value case, that is three instances of one pattern: **an assertion a neighboring sentence can satisfy is not an assertion about the claim.** Worth a standing rule if a fourth appears.

    - ⛔ **A root array is a per-feature sub-list only if its CONTENTS are spec attributes — decide it by looking inside, never by the key's shape.** — in `module-05-data-quality-mapping/phase1-quality-assessment.md`, Step 5a's coverage check.

    Drafted wording, to be minted at the next free id:

    **INV-NNN** — *(written as NNN deliberately: a literal id here would cite an invariant that does not exist and turn `citations.py verify` red. Mint at the next free id — read it off `INVARIANTS.md` rather than trusting a number written here, since several deferrals are pending and only the first one minted gets the id any of them would have named.)* Where a check classifies a source key as *structure* rather than as *content*, that classification MUST be decided by the key's **contents**, never by its name or shape, and any set of structural keys stated in the plugin MUST be closed rather than open-ended. A container whose contained keys do not resolve is unrecognized content, and its contents count toward the source's unrecognized set. ⚠️ **An open-ended list of examples is read as an invitation to add members by resemblance**, which is precisely how a gate that decides whether a whole module may be skipped comes to be satisfied by an array nobody dispositioned. Enforced by `tests/test_coverage_check_looks_inside_root_arrays.py`.

- **MCP re-check:** **n/a (no Senzing fact).** The defect is an internal contradiction between two sentences of the plugin's own instructions; the fix restates one of them and asserts nothing about Senzing. The spec's supporting context — that the environment script must export `PYTHONPATH` and `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` on `linux_apt`/Python — is already stated and cited at Step 3 and was not restated here, so no fact was copied out of the spec (INV-080).
- **Summary:** Step 1's fallback conclusion said *"skip Steps 2 and 3 entirely"* while the V4.0+ branch 27 lines below said *"Not Step 3 entirely"*. The first is what a guide reads at the moment the library check succeeds, is phrased as a complete instruction, and comes first — so it is the one that gets followed. It now says to skip the **installation** (Step 2, and Step 3's install commands) and states that Step 3's environment-script work still runs, pointing at the "Required stops" block. **Criterion walk, 5 of 5 hold.** (1) *No line in Step 1 instructs skipping Step 3 in full* — asserted corpus-wide by a scan that flags "skip … Steps 2 and 3" unless the sentence narrows it to the install. (2) *The fallback path alone still routes through the environment script* — asserted by reading the fallback paragraph in isolation and requiring it to name the environment script, which is the reader the defect actually caught. (3) *The "Required stops" block is unchanged* — asserted directly. (4) *`grep -rn "skip Steps 2 and 3 entirely" plugins/` returns nothing* — run, clean. (5) *Cross-platform, language-agnostic* — prose; the sentence names no platform, path separator or binding.
- ⚠️ **Why the failure was severe out of proportion to the edit.** Skipping Step 3 wholesale leaves a healthy install with no environment, and the first symptom is `libSz.so: cannot open shared object file` **in a later module** — where it reads as a broken SDK rather than a routing decision three steps back. Step 1's own filesystem fallback exists because the import check fails on a working install when those paths are unset, so this instruction routed the guide past the step that fixes the very condition the fallback had just detected. Observed live during the `/dry-run` walk that filed the spec: the library was present at `/opt/senzing/er/lib/libSz.so` and the Python import failed for exactly that reason.
- ⚠️ **Negative-controlled by restoring the historical sentence verbatim** — both assertions in `NoShippedTextLicensesSkippingStep3Wholesale` and `Step1StillRoutesAnExistingInstallThroughTheEnvironmentScript` fail (2 failures), and the file was verified byte-identical to the fix afterwards. The guard also pins its own pattern against that sentence, so a future edit that stops matching it fails rather than passing vacuously.
- **Establishes no invariant.** The change restores a rule the module already states — the "Required stops" block and its ⛔ are unchanged and were always correct; this removes a contradicting sentence rather than creating a guarantee. The one ⛔ added is a restatement of that existing rule at the point the wrong turn was taken (INV-183's reasoning), and `conformance.py since`/`per-rule --uncited` confirm it is not among the uncited set.
- **Commit:** `ff266df`

The guard derives its site set by scanning and caught what the reasoning missed; a guard listing the spec's two paths would have certified the defect.

Fixed by stripping inline-code spans before asserting, the same shape as the merge-histogram guard's comment-stripping. (b) The write-site scan matched "record count across the mentioned sources" — *record* as a **noun** — flagging `module-01-business-problem/phase1-discovery.md`, a file whose entire point is that it must never write the field. The verb list was tightened; all three real write sites still match.

Discarded and re-run clean — a red run whose cause nobody chases is how a genuine regression gets waved through as "that was just the mutation testing". (ii) Fixing an escaping error in this entry, a blanket replace of backslash-backtick across the whole ledger **altered four pre-existing summaries** that were quoting literal escape sequences. Requiring one there is ceremony that teaches the marker means nothing. Tied to the condition the rule's own next sentence already names. All six rules below are now cited. This implementation ships five hard rules citing no invariant at their line. Confirmed by the INV-282 set difference between `conformance.py since --since-last-audit` and `per-rule --uncited`, not by grepping for phrases I expected. The rules, verbatim:
    - ⛔ **This reading is PROVISIONAL, and Step 8a re-takes it — `get_license()` resolves the license from the settings it is handed, and the settings here do not yet carry `CONFIGPATH`.** — in `module-02-sdk-setup/SKILL.md`, Step 5a.

    - ⛔ **A figure whose `_measured_at` marker says provisional, or which carries no marker, is re-measured here before any branch below reads it** — in `module-04-data-collection/SKILL.md`, Step 8a sub-step 1.
    - ⛔ **One exception, and it is the reason `license_record_limit_measured_at` exists: a reading marked provisional (or carrying no marker) takes the absent branch, not this one.** — in `module-06-data-processing/phaseA-build-loading.md`.
    - ⛔ **Read `license_record_limit_measured_at` alongside it, and treat a reading marked provisional — or carrying no marker — as the absent case below.** — in `module-06-data-processing/phaseB-load-first-source.md`.

    All five state one guarantee. Drafted wording, next free id:

    **INV-NNN** — *(written as NNN deliberately: a literal id here would cite an invariant that does not exist and turn `citations.py verify` red. Mint at the next free id — read it off `INVARIANTS.md` rather than trusting a number written here, since several deferrals are pending and only the first one minted gets the id any of them would have named.)* A bootcamp state field measured from the environment **whose result can change once configuration a later step writes exists** MUST record **when** the measurement was taken alongside the value, and a step branching on it MUST NOT treat a reading taken before its inputs were complete as authoritative. ⚠️ **Scope, stated because the unqualified form is ceremony at two of the three fields it would bind**: a field whose value cannot move that way — `platform`, `database_type` — needs no marker, and requiring one there teaches that the marker means nothing, which is how a signal stops being read at the field where it does mean something. Where a measurement's result depends on configuration a later step writes, the earlier reading is **provisional**: it MUST say so, a later step MUST re-take it once that configuration exists, and a superseded figure MUST be named aloud when it is replaced — including when the correction *raises* a limit, which is the direction most likely to be swallowed. ⚠️ **A measured-but-incomplete value is worse than an absent one**, because absence triggers a re-measure and presence suppresses it. (**Extends INV-278** on a new axis: INV-244 forbids reading *absence* as a finding, INV-278 forbids reading *presence* as a measurement, and this forbids reading a *measurement* as a complete one.) Enforced by `tests/test_license_limit_reading_is_complete.py`.

## capture-screenshots-cannot-tell-whether-the-tab-actually-changed

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-31
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/capture_screenshots.py` (`_supports_deep_linking`, `_identical_groups`, a `--url` pre-flight in `main()`, a duplicate check after capture, and `write_manifest(failed_reason=…)`), `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03b-truthset-visualization/phase1-visualization.md` (the deep-linking requirement named at the build step), **added** `tests/test_capture_verifies_tab_activation.py`, `specs/capture-screenshots-cannot-tell-whether-the-tab-actually-changed.md` (deviation note), `specs/IMPLEMENTED.md` (this entry).
- **MCP re-check:** **n/a (no Senzing fact).** The defect is entirely in a bundled script and the module's own verification chain. `get_capabilities` dated the session: server **1.35.1**, 2026-08-31.
- **Summary:** A live server that cannot select a tab now fails the capture instead of naming six PNGs after tabs they do not show. **Criterion walk, 5 items: 4 hold, 1 NOT met and disclosed rather than ticked.** (1) ⛔ **Not met as written — see the deviation note.** The spec asks for a **rendered readback** of the active tab; no backend available to this plugin can do that on the `--url` path (details below). What shipped is a **source-level pre-flight**, `_supports_deep_linking`, which refuses the run before any file is written. (2) *Byte-identical captures reported as an error* — `_identical_groups` hashes every written PNG; an identical group is **deleted** rather than kept, since at most one of the pair can show the tab it is named for and nothing here can determine which, and the run exits non-zero. (3) *A page with no `?tab=` support produces a non-zero exit naming activation* — held, and **verified end to end** against a real localhost stub server carrying every marker the older pre-flights look for (nav ids, section ids, an `activate()`) and no query-string reading: exit 1, zero PNGs, a message naming `?tab=` and deep-linking, and a manifest whose `failed` reason says so instead of the generic "no image written by any backend" (INV-122 requires the reported reason to be the actual one). (4) *`phase1-visualization.md` Step 2 names the requirement* — added to the "server MUST reproduce" list with the contract section quoted, why it matters at capture time, and the 2026-08-28 measurement. (5) *Cross-platform, language-agnostic* — stdlib `hashlib`/`re`/`urllib`; the check reads the served source and names no language.
- ⛔ **Why criterion 1 could not be met, stated rather than worked around.** Playwright and Selenium can evaluate script against a live page; **neither is installed here and neither is a bootcamp requirement** (both are optional imports returning `False` when absent). The backend that actually captures on this machine — and the one the 2026-08-28 walk used — is the **headless-Chrome CLI**, which cannot evaluate an expression for us: `_measure_chrome_cli` has to patch a local copy of the HTML to read **one number**, and its own docstring records that a remote URL cannot be patched. So a rendered readback would be unavailable in exactly the configuration where the defect occurs. The pre-flight that shipped instead cannot prove a page honors `tab` *correctly* — its docstring says so — but it cannot produce a false failure on a conforming server either, since honoring the contract requires reading the query string. **Proposed change 3 (give `--url` the snapshot path's click fallback) is deliberately not implemented** for the same reason, and because a fallback would silently compensate for a missing contract feature instead of reporting it.
- ⚠️ **The spec's INV-122 reading is corrected, and that is why no invariant was minted.** The spec calls this "adjacent to INV-122 but outside it", reasoning from that invariant's *absent-tab* clause. INV-122's **first** clause already forbids the outcome outright — screenshots "MUST be captured as one image per tab, **never as several views of one tab**, and each file MUST be named after the tab it shows". Six files showing one tab is exactly that. The guarantee was registered all along; only the enforcement was missing for this mechanism, so the new rule at the build step **cites INV-122** rather than minting an ID. **Establishes no invariant.**
- **Commit:** `b826db5`

## dry-run-2026-08-28

**Not a spec** — a dated record of a dry-run, following the `dry-run-*` precedent. **Phase 3 only.**

⚠️ **Written retroactively on 2026-08-31**, from the four spec files the run left in the working tree. The walk ended without writing a ledger entry, so for three days its entire record was four **untracked** files — a tree loss would have erased a full live walk. Nothing below is recalled: every fact is carried from those four specs, which were written *during* the walk. Where they are silent — turn count, the start-to-stop sequence, what was exercised and found correct — **this entry is silent too**. That silence is the cost of the missing entry, not something a retroactive record can repair, and it is the reason the run's "verified correct, so a later run need not re-derive it" half is simply **absent** here where every prior `dry-run-*` entry carries one.

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-28 (**4 findings recorded as specs; nothing fixed** — report-before-change)
- **Files changed:** four new spec files (named below), `specs/IMPLEMENTED.md` (this entry). **No plugin file, script or test was modified by the run** — verified 2026-08-31 by `git status`, which showed the four spec files as the working tree's only content, all untracked.
- **MCP re-check:** **server 1.33.0**, 2026-08-28 — `get_capabilities` called at the start of the run to date it. Tools the specs record as called during the walk: `get_capabilities`; `sdk_guide(topic='install', platform='linux_apt', language='java')` and `sdk_guide(topic='install', platform='macos_arm', language='java')`, fetched **as a pair** so the Linux response's missing Java content became visible by comparison; `sdk_guide(topic='load', language='java', platform='linux_apt', record_count=10000)`; and the Entity Specification retrieval, verified live at **73,051 bytes**, matching the recorded `size_bytes`. ⛔ `submit_feedback` **never invoked**, per the skill's absolute rule.
- **Summary:** **The first phase-3 walk with a real Senzing install carrying a non-default license, the first ever to reach Truth Set visualization and build the chosen-language server for real, and the first to reach Data Quality, Mapping, and Transformation with a generated dataset.** Environment, as the specs record it: Linux, **Senzing 4.3.4-26210**, **OpenJDK 21.0.12**, a Java-language bootcamp, the Truth Set loaded at **159 records → 84 entities**, and an installed license reading `licenseType: EVAL (Solely for non-productive use)` with **`recordLimit: 0`** — uncapped. Started at **SDK setup**, the maintainer-chosen start module. **Four findings, each written to `specs/` during the walk.** ⛔ `sdk-setup-step5a-reads-absence-as-the-built-in-license` (**High**) — Step 5a branches on `license_record_limit` and reads **absence** as *"only the built-in evaluation license is active"*, then pins a note limiting the Bootcamper to **500 records**. Absence is the *normal* state there: the field's only writer is Module 4's Step 8a gate, which has not run. So a Bootcamper with an uncapped license is told a false figure at a decision point, and it propagates into Module 4's only volume-gated prompt. **This is the exact inference INV-244 forbids, documented with this exact scenario** — an unguarded recurrence of a known defect, not a new judgment call, and it surfaced only because this walk had a non-default license: with the built-in one the assumed and measured figures agree and the branch looks correct. ⛔ `java-classpath-guidance-is-macos-sourced-and-unusable-on-linux` (**High**) — `SKILL.md:807-810` gives `java -cp "${SENZING_ROOT}/sdk/java/sz-sdk.jar:…"`, but `SENZING_ROOT` is **unset on Linux** and returned by no `linux_apt` route, so the example expands to `-cp "/sdk/java/sz-sdk.jar"` and fails to compile against the real jar at `/opt/senzing/er/sdk/java/sz-sdk.jar`. **Owner-checked:** `sdk_guide(topic='install', platform='linux_apt', language='java')` *is* the route that would carry it, and returns a response **identical to the same call without `language`**. It blocks a documented path rather than degrading it, and the plugin's own seeded-preferences fixture (`path: core`, `programming_language: Java`) is exactly this configuration. ⚠️ `capture-screenshots-cannot-tell-whether-the-tab-actually-changed` (**Medium**) — a chosen-language server that implements the tab set but omits `?tab=` deep-linking makes `capture_screenshots.py --url` write **six correctly-named PNGs holding five distinct images**, report success for every one, and pass the module's completion gate; two files were **byte-identical** by `md5sum`. The file names, the success lines, the manifest and the gate were all consistent with a correct capture — it was caught only by **opening the images**. The corrupted artifact is the keepsake. ⚠️ `the-quality-gates-improve-option-has-no-procedure-and-is-incoherent-on-a-generated-scenario` (**Medium**) — both quality gates offer "improve the data first" and **no step in the plugin defines what the guide does when it is chosen**: no procedure, no loop-back, no re-score, no re-entry. Hit live at **CRM_EXPORT scoring 75.1** (the 70-79 band), the gate presented as pinned, the maintainer answering **1**, and nothing to execute — and on a bootcamp-*generated* scenario the option asks the Bootcamper to undo work the previous module's invariant required. **Coverage limits, from the specs rather than inferred:** all four findings were made in the walk's **analysis stretch**, and no spec records how far the walk got beyond the three modules named above, so **the run's overall coverage is unknown and must be treated as unestablished** — a later run cannot subtract this one from its own sweep. Linux only; one language (Java); one dataset shape per module. ⛔ **One action is still OWED and is not discharged by this record:** the inert `language='java'` parameter on `linux_apt` is a genuine **server-side coverage gap** worth reporting upstream, and `/dry-run` forbids `submit_feedback` under any category, so nothing was sent. It needs the maintainer's approval and an explicit send outside a run. **Establishes no invariant** — a dry run reports; all four findings propose plugin-side fixes and none proposes a new rule.

## the-writer-count-matcher-enumerates-phrasings-not-the-concept

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-28
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-06-data-processing/phaseA-build-loading.md`,
  `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-04-data-collection/SKILL.md`,
  `tests/test_license_limit_is_written_only_from_a_measurement.py` (matcher rewritten against the
  claim), `specs/the-writer-count-matcher-enumerates-phrasings-not-the-concept.md` (deviation note).
  `specs/INVARIANTS.md` — predicted by the spec, **deliberately unchanged**: the invariant it asks for
  is deferred for sign-off, below.
- **MCP re-check:** **n/a (no Senzing fact)** — re-confirmed as n/a rather than assumed.
  `get_capabilities` dated the run: server **1.33.0**, 2026-08-28.
- **Summary:** Cycle 5 of the second unattended loop, and its cap. Two writer-count sites survived the
  guard written to remove them, because that matcher required the field name adjacent to the claim
  while both sentences used an **anaphor** — *"its only writer"*, *"the field's only writer"* — whose
  subject was established a line earlier. Both corrected keeping their own point; a corpus grep for
  the concept now returns nothing outside one legitimate compound adjective. The matcher is rewritten
  against the **claim**: scoping by file rather than by proximity, with all **six** phrasings that
  have actually shipped pinned as fixtures and each planted at a real site to confirm it fails.
  ⛔ **The rewrite immediately produced a false positive, which is the other half of the lesson:** the
  first concept-level pattern fired on *"a stdlib-only writer"*, a real string that states no count.
  A guard that flags correct prose gets relaxed, so the pattern carries a negative lookbehind and
  that string is pinned in the must-pass set — **widening a matcher and tightening it are the same
  edit**. ⚠️ `since` reports **0** rules added and the cycle-2 cited-or-deferred guard **skips** with
  *"no hard rules added"* — both correct, since this change removed false claims rather than adding
  rules, and the skip is that guard saying so rather than passing silently (INV-265), its first time
  on that branch.
- **Invariant established: INV-282** — registered 2026-08-28 on the maintainer's sign-off, from
  the wording drafted below and carried over **unchanged**. Cited at the shipped sites it
  governs and cross-referenced from the spec's `## Invariants introduced`; the enforcing test
  cites it back, so `test_invariant_enforcer_citations.py`'s bidirectional pair count rose from
  90 to 97 across this pass (six invariants, seven pairs — INV-282 names two enforcers).
  ⚠️ The deferral text is kept below rather than deleted, so the record shows what was drafted
  while the maintainer was unavailable and that nothing changed between drafting and signing.
- **DEFERRED INVARIANT (resolved INV-282, 2026-08-28) — the draft as it stood.** ⛔ This is the half worth
  more than either site fix, and it now has **four instances in one day**: the count was wrong; the
  correction minted a new count; the guard against counts enumerated the phrasings already seen; the
  concept-level rewrite then over-matched. INV-246 states this for a guard's set of **files** and
  nothing states it for its set of **phrasings**. Drafted wording (highest id currently INV-276 —
  written as `INV-NNN` deliberately, because spelling an unminted id creates a citation of an
  undefined invariant and turns `citations.py verify` red):
  *"**INV-NNN** — A guard enforcing a rule across shipped prose MUST derive its matcher from the
  CLAIM being made, not from the phrasings observed at the sites it was written to fix. Where the
  claim can be made about a subject established in an earlier sentence, the matcher MUST NOT require
  that subject adjacent to it; scope by file instead. Every phrasing that has actually shipped MUST
  be pinned as a fixture, and every construction the matcher must NOT flag MUST be pinned beside it —
  a guard that flags correct prose is relaxed rather than fixed. (**Extends INV-246** from a guard's
  set of FILES to its set of PHRASINGS: both fail by inheriting the blind spot of whoever last fixed
  the instances.)"*
  Already enforced in practice by `tests/test_license_limit_is_written_only_from_a_measurement.py`'s
  fixture sets; registering it costs one edit to `specs/INVARIANTS.md` plus a citation in that guard.

Under the do-not-persist reading, `config/bootcamp_progress.json` keeps the false `100000`, and Module 4's Step 8a volume-skip (*"If the collected total is at or below the effective limit … **Do not ask for a License Key**"*, `module-04-data-collection/SKILL.md:807-809`) skips the gate on a ~94,000-record collection — **the exact suppression the fix was written to prevent, surviving the fix**. Under the persist reading, two shipped files become false: `phase1-discovery.md:312` and `phaseA-build-loading.md:190` each call Module 4 Step 8a the **only writer** of the field, and each uses that as the premise for an INV-244 absence branch. ⚠️ **Those conclusions survive** — reconciliation fires only on a value already present, so "absent means not yet measured" still holds — which is exactly why the sentences need correcting rather than shrugging at: the conclusion is right and the stated reason is not, and a rule whose reason is wrong is one a later edit simplifies incorrectly. ## applicability-and-attribute-catalog-are-authored-by-hand-and-fail-silently

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-28
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-05-data-quality-mapping/phase1-quality-assessment.md`,
  `tests/test_quality_score_inputs_are_checked_before_scoring.py` (new),
  `specs/applicability-and-attribute-catalog-are-authored-by-hand-and-fail-silently.md` (deviation note)
- **MCP re-check:** **server 1.33.0, 2026-08-28 — confirmed at triage, figures reproduce exactly.**
  The served `senzing_entity_specification.md` yields 102 plain-text first-column attribute names, 21
  backticked ALL-CAPS tokens anywhere and 110 in the union, with `NAME_ORG`, `ADDR_LINE1` and
  `PHONE_NUMBER` never backticked — the report's own numbers.
  `search_docs(query='entity specification attribute names feature tables NAME_ORG ADDR_LINE1
  PHONE_NUMBER', category='data_mapping')` returns the same tables **backticked**, establishing the
  two-rendering trap the report did not name. Per-type presence percentages stay observation-only
  (INV-080/INV-149).
- **Summary:** Two hand-authored inputs to the quality score, each of which produced a wrong number
  that looked like a data finding. **(1) Applicability:** four fields on a 72,799-record source were
  marked "applies to both" while measuring 100%/91.5%/42.3%/100% on ORGANIZATION and **0%** on
  PERSON, scoring 70.5% into the remediation band against a corrected 85.7%. Step 6 now requires a
  per-`RECORD_TYPE` presence breakdown for **every** field marked as applying to both, **before** the
  score is reported, and treats a 100%/0% split as an applicability error that **stops the score**.
  ⚠️ This is a **precondition**, not another heuristic: the existing NAME/ADDRESS check fires after a
  low score exists and keys on the output, while the applicability set is the input that was wrong.
  The existing check and the 0%/100% uniformity sanity-check are both preserved and test-asserted as
  such. **(2) The catalog:** the specification's feature tables write attribute names as **plain text
  in the first column**, so a backtick-tuned parse under-collects by roughly four fifths — and
  `search_docs` renders the same names backticked, which is why a parse tuned on an excerpt works
  there and fails here. Stated at the save step, which already warns that a bad fetch surfaces later
  as "attribute names that are merely absent". ⛔ **No attribute count ships**, per criterion 4 — and
  enforcing that caught two of my own violations, including a bullet *forbidding* a pinned count that
  stated one. Guarded by `tests/test_quality_score_inputs_are_checked_before_scoring.py` (9 tests,
  stdlib only, no `plugins/` import — INV-108), site sets derived by scanning (INV-246).
  ⚠️ **The guard's matcher was wrong in both directions before it was right** — too narrow, then too
  broad (flagging an unrelated `MCP-NEGATIVE` marker) — found by the negative controls, not by
  reading; it now pins three phrasings that must match and three that must not. Negative-controlled
  six ways. ⚠️ **Both halves are text-asserted only** and need a phase-3 walk on a mixed
  person/organization source. **Establishes no invariant** — the applicability precondition is INV-174
  and INV-264 applied at the step that feeds them, and the parse rule is INV-115's
  confirm-the-shape-before-parsing discipline applied to a fetched document; all four hard-rule lines
  cite one of those at the line, and `conformance.py rules` reports **0** sections citing no
  invariant. ⚠️ **Correction, made by `production-readiness-audit-2026-08-28c` the same day: that
  claim was wrong.** Two of the four — the `Do not pin an attribute count` sub-bullet and the
  `The applicability set is authored by hand` rationale clause — carry **no** invariant at their own
  line; `per-rule --uncited` lists both. Their parent rules are cited, so nothing is unregistered,
  but INV-183 is about the line a reader is on. Recorded in
  `specs/three-hard-rules-from-the-2026-08-28-loop-carry-no-citation-at-the-line.md`; the claim
  above is left in place rather than rewritten, per the ledger's append-or-correct rule.
- **Commit:** 2859243

## macos-protected-launchers-strip-dyld-from-a-backgrounded-server

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-28
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03b-truthset-visualization/visualization-api-reference.md`
  (the canonical rule, in "Server lifetime"),
  `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03b-truthset-visualization/phase1-visualization.md`,
  `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-07-query-visualize-discover/phase1-query-visualize.md`,
  `tests/test_server_launch_warns_about_protected_launchers.py` (new),
  `specs/macos-protected-launchers-strip-dyld-from-a-backgrounded-server.md` (deviation note)
- **MCP re-check:** **n/a (no Senzing fact).** The subject is macOS SIP behavior and this plugin's
  launch guidance; no Senzing behavior, SDK surface or server claim is asserted. `get_capabilities`
  dated the run: server **1.33.0**, 2026-08-28.
- **Summary:** macOS SIP strips `DYLD_*` whenever a **protected** binary execs a child, and
  `/usr/bin/nohup`, `/usr/bin/env` and `/bin/bash` are all protected — so a backgrounded server fails
  with `UnsatisfiedLinkError: no Sz in java.library.path` although the parent shell has the variable
  set. The plugin was already right about the hard part (module-02 states that
  `-Djava.library.path` alone is insufficient) but `DYLD` appeared in **exactly one** shipped file,
  several modules from the two steps that start a server, and nothing named the launcher. The rule
  now lives once in the **"Server lifetime"** contract both launching modules read — demonstration,
  symptom, the "the JVM flag does not fix it" pointer to module-02 (INV-179), and the explicit note
  that it is silent on Linux and Windows so a non-macOS reader does not skip it (INV-001), with the
  JVM error marked as illustration (INV-002) — and each launch site carries a pointer. ⚠️ **The spec
  predicted two files; the derived set is three** (the contract is itself a site), and
  `phase2-close.md` is deliberately excluded as teardown-only. Guarded by
  `tests/test_server_launch_warns_about_protected_launchers.py` (7 tests, stdlib only, no `plugins/`
  import — INV-108), site set derived by launch instruction and launch-handle capture (INV-246). ⛔ **A
  negative control caught a vacuous assertion:** the guard matched the bare word `env`, which is a
  substring of "environment" and "senzing-env.sh", so deleting `/usr/bin/env` from the contract
  **passed**. It now matches backticked tokens and fails on any deletion — found by running the
  control, not by reading the test. Negative-controlled six ways in total. ⚠️ **The SIP behavior was
  NOT reproduced** — this machine is Linux, where `DYLD_*` does not exist — so it is marked
  observation-only (INV-080/INV-149) in the shipped text and needs re-confirming on macOS.
  **Establishes no invariant** — the rule is a platform hazard note stated once and cited from its
  sites, governed by INV-001 (all three platforms first-class), INV-002 (stated as behavior, not per
  binding) and INV-179 (stated once, cited elsewhere); all three new hard-rule lines cite one of them
  at the line, and `conformance.py rules` reports **0** sections citing no invariant.
- **Commit:** e6c1df2

## a-non-utf8-recap-crashes-three-hooks-and-the-obvious-fix-destroys-it

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-27
- **Files changed:** `specs/INVARIANTS.md` (INV-276 + index entry), `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/recap_checkpoint.py` (`UNREADABLE` sentinel, `_read`, `checkpoint_state`, `fold_checkpoint`), `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/generate_recap_pdf.py` (source read guard), `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/generate_discoveries_pdf.py` (source read guard), `tests/test_undecodable_recap_is_never_overwritten.py` (new, 10 tests), `specs/a-non-utf8-recap-crashes-three-hooks-and-the-obvious-fix-destroys-it.md` (new), `specs/IMPLEMENTED.md` (this entry).
- **MCP re-check:** n/a (no Senzing fact). The defect is entirely in the plugin's own scripts, hooks and artifacts — no Senzing behavior, SDK surface or entity-specification claim is involved, so there is no server fact to re-verify and no absence claim to substantiate. `get_capabilities` was called once at the start of the `/dry-run` that found this, to date the run: server **1.33.0**, 2026-08-27.
- **Summary:** Found by `/dry-run` phase 2. A `docs/bootcamp_recap.md` that is not valid UTF-8 — what a Windows editor saving cp1252/ANSI produces as soon as the prose contains a smart quote or an en dash — crashed **three of the seven hook entries** (`precompact-recap.py`, `session-start.py`, `session-end.py`) and **both keepsake PDF generators** with an unhandled `UnicodeDecodeError` traceback. Root cause was a single choke point, `recap_checkpoint._read`, catching `OSError` only; `UnicodeDecodeError` derives from `ValueError`, so it escaped. ⚠️ **The severity is not the crash.** `fold()` reads the recap and then rewrites it in `"w"` mode, so the natural one-line patch — widening that `except` to return `None` — converts a loud crash into **silent destruction**: the recap is treated as empty and replaced by the current checkpoint block alone. Measured on the real scripts with only that patch applied, outside the repo: a 279-byte recap holding **two completed module sections became 98 bytes holding none**, while the hook printed `folded … (97 characters)` — a success line. The fix therefore makes `_read` return a distinct `UNREADABLE` sentinel so callers cannot conflate *absent* (safe to create) with *unreadable* (never write here); `fold_checkpoint` and `checkpoint_state` refuse and report in the shape `normalize_docs_markdown.py` already used, naming the file, the cause and that both files were left untouched; the two generators guard their own reads, exit 1 and write no PDF. ⛔ The bootcamper's file is never "repaired" — no `errors="replace"`, because silently mangling a document they are invited to keep and share is not ours to do. **Acceptance criteria all satisfied**, verified by execution rather than by reading: no hook emits a traceback; the recap is **byte-identical** after all three folding hooks (sha256 compared); both completed sections survive; both generators exit non-zero with a relayable message and no PDF; `normalize_docs_markdown.py` unchanged (it already handled this correctly, which is what made the omission a gap rather than an accepted limit); and the healthy path is intact — the fold is still byte-identical across three runs at the same md5 as the pre-fix baseline, the recap PDF still reports `renderer: fpdf2`, and an **absent** recap is still created. ⛔ **Negative-controlled twice, because one control was not enough.** Control A reintroduced the original `except OSError` — 6 of 10 tests failed. Control B applied the destructive widening patch — 5 failed, `test_the_recap_is_byte_identical_after_every_folding_hook` and `test_completed_module_sections_survive` among them. A guard that only asserted "no traceback" would have **passed** against Control B, which is precisely the certification-of-a-worse-bug this repo has been bitten by before; the byte-identity assertion is the point of the file and its docstring says so. Both controls reverted and `__pycache__` cleared. **Test is stdlib-only and drives the hooks as subprocesses, importing nothing under `plugins/` (INV-108).** ⚠️ **My own error, reported:** while probing, a backup `cp` fell through to a path that did not exist with its failure hidden by `2>/dev/null`, so a later "utf8" backup captured an already-mutated fixture and I briefly read healthy hooks as crashing. Caught by checking each fixture's actual encoding rather than trusting the restore; the scratch project was re-scaffolded and the UTF-8 baseline re-established before any conclusion was drawn. This is the second time in this skill's history that a silent restore failure cost work, and it happened despite the rule that warns about it.
- **Invariant established: INV-276** — registered 2026-08-27 on the maintainer's sign-off, from the wording drafted in this entry and carried over unchanged. Indexed under *Generator behavior: rendering, encoding, reporting*; enforced by `tests/test_undecodable_recap_is_never_overwritten.py`, which now cites it back per the bidirectional guard. **Registered wording:** *A helper that reads a bootcamper-owned artifact MUST distinguish **absent** from **present but unreadable**, and MUST NOT collapse the two into one falsy result. Any caller that goes on to WRITE that artifact MUST refuse and report when the read was unreadable, never proceed on a value that merely looks empty — a rewrite of a file whose existing content could not be read destroys it. The refusal MUST name the file and the cause, and MUST leave the artifact byte-identical; the plugin MUST NOT silently transcode or lossily re-read a document the bootcamper owns. Enforced by `tests/test_undecodable_recap_is_never_overwritten.py`, whose byte-identity assertion — not its no-traceback assertion — is what distinguishes a correct fix from a data-destroying one.* Scope note for the reviewer: the rule is about the **absent-vs-unreadable conflation**, not about UTF-8 specifically; `current_module()` in the same file already honored it (catching `(OSError, ValueError)`, documented against INV-048) eleven lines above the function that did not, which is the argument that the guarantee wants an address of its own rather than living as a comment.
- **Commit:** 26dcf1a

## the-packager-secret-scan-skips-the-files-most-likely-to-be-secrets

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-26
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/package_bootcamp.py` (`TEXT_SUFFIXES` **deleted**; `_scan()` rewritten to a three-outcome contract with a chunked full-content read; the `UNEXAMINED` branch at the call site in `collect()`), `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/bootcamp-onboarding/packaging.md` (the Step 4 summary of what the scan covers), `specs/the-bootcamp-cannot-leave-the-machine-it-was-built-on.md` (the drafted invariant's secret-scan clause), `tests/test_package_bootcamp.py` (the `.pem`/extensionless/`.crt` fixtures, the PNG pair, the boundary and unreadable cases, the docstring), `tests/test_secret_patterns_are_shared.py` (what it proves; the no-allowlist assertions)
- **MCP re-check:** n/a (no Senzing fact). The secret patterns are the plugin's own (INV-109) and the defect was in how they were applied; no SDK method, flag, response shape or server behavior is asserted, and no absence is claimed.
- **Summary:** **Criterion walk, all eight met.** (1) A PEM private key is now excluded regardless of extension — asserted over `.pem`, an **extensionless** `id_rsa`, and `.crt`, the three the old allowlist skipped. (2) A member that cannot be read is excluded and named; `_scan()` returns a distinct `UNEXAMINED` sentinel and the call site fails **closed**. (3) A genuine PNG still travels, asserted — the fix must not exclude the visualizations `share` exists to carry. ⚠️ **And a key pasted *into* a PNG is excluded**, which is correct: a credential does not stop being one because of the file it was pasted into. (4) `TEXT_SUFFIXES` is deleted, not lengthened — a longer allowlist is the same defect with a later trigger, and the removal rationale is in the module with a test asserting it survives (never cut the reason). (5) All three over-claiming docstrings now state what is asserted, and `test_secret_patterns_are_shared` says plainly that **pattern equality does not establish equal application** — the general lesson being that a sync test on a shared constant says nothing about how each consumer uses it. (6) That file additionally asserts the packager's scan is not gated on an extension, that the `UNEXAMINED` distinction exists, and that `write-gate.py` still has no suffix filter — the baseline the packager is measured against, asserted rather than assumed. (7) Negative-controlled. (8) stdlib only, no `file(1)`, cross-platform. ⛔ **Verified by re-running the hostile fixture that found it**: before, `src/keys/server.pem` and `src/keys/id_rsa` were packaged; after, both are excluded and named alongside `creds.cfg`, `loader.py` and the key-bearing PNG, while the clean PNG is still included. ⚠️ ⛔ **THREE of five negative controls escaped on the first pass, and closing them is the most valuable part of this entry.** Reintroducing the allowlist was caught (8 failures) and deleting the rationale was caught — but collapsing `UNEXAMINED` into `None`, including an unexamined member, and **dropping the block overlap** all changed nothing any test could see, because no fixture had an unreadable member and every fixture was smaller than one 1 MiB scan block. **A guard that claims boundary-safe scanning and a three-outcome contract while exercising neither is precisely the Step 7 class 3 defect this spec was written about** — reproduced inside the fix for it. Two tests were added: a >1 MiB member with the armor line **straddling** the block boundary, and a `chmod 000` member (skipped rather than faked where the filesystem allows root to read anyway). All three controls now fail. ⚠️ **One escaped control taught something extra:** collapsing `UNEXAMINED` surfaces as an *error* rather than a failure, because `sha256_of` then raises on the unreadable member during manifest build — so failing open on the scan also crashes the packager, which makes the fail-closed branch load-bearing twice. Suite green at **3,654 passed, 3 skipped**; `citations.py verify` clean at 266; `conformance.py rules` **0** sections citing no invariant. **Establishes no invariant of its own** — the guarantee is INV-109's, and the drafted packaging invariant's secret-scan clause was corrected to describe the fixed behavior rather than the shipped defect; that draft remains unminted pending sign-off.
- **Commit:** 632f422

- **Summary:** Baseline green — **3,640 passed, 3 skipped, 3,145 subtests**. `since --since-last-audit` reports **0** hard-rule lines added by iteration 3's implement round (documentation fixes plus guards), the second consecutive zero. ⛔ **THE FINDING — `the-packager-secret-scan-skips-the-files-most-likely-to-be-secrets` (High).** `package_bootcamp.py`'s secret scan is gated on an extension allowlist (`TEXT_SUFFIXES`), which carries `.md`/`.py`/`.json`/`.csv` and **not** `.pem`, `.key`, `.crt`, or the empty extension. Measured on a fixture with `--profile transfer`: `src/keys/server.pem` and an extensionless `src/keys/id_rsa`, **both carrying real PEM armor lines, were PACKAGED**, while the identical key embedded in `src/loader.py` was correctly excluded and named. The scan skips exactly the file types whose purpose is to hold a credential, in an archive whose reason to exist is being handed to someone else — and `OPEN_ME_FIRST.md` tells the recipient that anything matching a secret pattern was excluded, which is then false. **Root cause:** an allowlist written to answer *"is this worth reading as text?"* is used to answer *"can this contain a secret?"*, and `_scan()` returns `None` — indistinguishable from a clean result — for every unlisted suffix. ⚠️ **The same module fails CLOSED one screen away**, in the `find_secret` ImportError fallback, so the intent was fail-closed on a missing scanner and fail-open on the suffix, in one file. ⛔ **And this is why the sync test was misleading rather than merely incomplete.** `write-gate.py` has **no** suffix filter — it scans every payload — so `tests/test_secret_patterns_are_shared.py` asserting the two **pattern strings** byte-identical, and reporting that the packager cannot "protect less than the gate", was true of the constants and false of the behavior. The patterns were never the difference; the *application* is. **Three places over-claim on the strength of that test** — both new test docstrings and the drafted invariant's *"MUST exclude and name any member matching the INV-109 secret patterns"* — and the packager's own test passed because its fixture used a `.py`. This is Step 7 class 3 exactly, found by applying it to my own work rather than to inherited code. **Verdict by property, separately.** **Consistent — pass in scope.** **Coherent — one defect: the finding, whose three docstrings assert more than the code does.** **Complete — pass in scope**, and the outcome blocks **INV-033–INV-049 were swept this pass** (the rotation slot the two previous audits declared unfilled): INV-035/037/039–045/049 are honored by the modules that own them; INV-047's shipped banner is `🎓🎓🎓 BOOTCAMP GRADUATION 🎓🎓🎓`, which satisfies INV-079's name-in-caps form and is **not** a discrepancy with INV-047's looser quoted string; INV-048's non-blocking guarantee survives iteration 1's tab-coverage change and is test-asserted; INV-033/034/046's *offered* semantics are conversational and route to `dry-run` phase 3. `coverage_reports.py affected` was run for the first time in this loop — **489 ledgered specs examined, 38 with a gap, and none of this session's 15 specs is among them**; the report's own preamble calls a gap often legitimate and never a gate. `citations.py verify` clean at **266**; `shipped` clean; `negatives` clean with no unmarked dated absence claim. **Concise — flat.** **45 files / 176,448 words**, unchanged from iteration 2; duplication unchanged at **163 across 100 pairs**; `per-rule --uncited` unchanged at **344 of 541**. Iteration 3's edits were to `README.md` and `docs/README.md`, which the shipped-markdown scan does not count. ⛔ **Coverage limits, explicitly.** **No full forward sweep** — 266 invariants; this pass took INV-033–INV-049, the `affected` report, and Step 7 class 3 against the new feature. **INV-050–INV-266 were not swept this pass** beyond what the generators flagged. **The 45 enumerating invariants were again not individually re-read**; the 33 comma-series members remain unchecked across all three iterations. **`per-rule --uncited`'s 344-line worklist was not worked.** **The conversational invariants remain untested and cannot be tested by reading** — INV-251, INV-005/006/008/009/012/014, INV-033/034/046/047 and every gate-ordering rule need `dry-run` phase 3, including the packaging flow's consent ordering. **Nothing in the packaging feature has run in a live bootcamp.** ⚠️ **The finding above is the strongest argument in this session for running `dry-run`**: it was found by *executing* the packager against a fixture designed to be hostile, not by reading it, and reading had already passed it twice. **This audit established no invariant and modified no shipped file.**

(9) One top-level directory, both orientation files at its root, and the manifest records profile, plugin version, date, `modules_completed`, per-file SHA-256 and size, and the exclusion rules — all asserted. ## a-composite-flag-is-a-set-in-java-and-cannot-be-listed-among-enum-constants

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-26
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-07-query-visualize-discover/phase1-query-visualize.md` (the binding-shape rule at `:156`, the `MCP-NEGATIVE` marker and routing caveat at `:177`, the worked Java example at `:184`, the plural-class stop sign at `:211`), `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-07-query-visualize-discover/phase2-discover.md` (`:196-208` — the misattributed claim corrected), `tests/test_why_key_details_flag_claim_is_withdrawn.py` (the guard that pinned the retracted claim, rewritten)

The spec never asked that route (its `MCP re-check` field carried no `owner-checked:` clause because it claimed no absence — the absence was in the Root cause instead). So the general fact **is** served, and the implementation became a **routing pointer** to `topic='parameters'` rather than a hardcoded Java assertion. The residual unserved fact is narrower: that a composite *constant* is itself a collection. Recorded as a routing `MCP-NEGATIVE` marker at `phase1-query-visualize.md:177`, owner `topic='parameters'`; it appears in `coverage_reports.py negatives` and is not reported malformed.
- **Summary:** **Criterion walk — five of six met, one deferred (named below).** (1) **Facts re-verified before any prose landed** — 1.33.0, 2026-08-26; every new citation carries that version and date. (2) **Module 7's flag-composition guidance now states the representation rule** at `phase1-query-visualize.md:156`, directly after the `composite_members` block, with the two shapes a binding can take (scalar/bitmask → OR it in; collection → the composite may be a member *or itself a collection*, in which case it is merged) and the Java `addAll`-not-`EnumSet.of` case as the worked example at `:184`. (3) **Stated as binding-shape guidance, Java as illustration only** (INV-002) — the rule is expressed over parameter *types*, and the Java block is explicitly labeled a worked example. (4) ⛔ **Not met — invariant deferred, see the deferral below.** (5) **Upstream report explicitly deferred, with the reason** — and the re-check changed what it would say: the original finding (no route names the binding type) is false, so the fileable residue is only that `topic='flags'` rows carry no representation hint and no cross-reference to `topic='parameters'`. `submit_feedback` requires the exact message be shown and confirmed before sending, and the maintainer is away; **not sent, and never under `category='license_request'`** (INV-135). Draft, for approval: *category `feature`* — "`get_sdk_reference(topic='flags')` returns composite and single flags in one shape; a one-line binding-representation note, or a pointer to `topic='parameters'`, would close the gap for callers following the production caution in a collection-typed binding." (6) **Cross-platform and language-agnostic** — markdown guidance only. ⚠️ **Better than the criterion asked: the compile behavior IS runtime-verified.** The criterion said it was confirmable only with a live Java SDK; this machine has one (`/opt/senzing/er/sdk/java/sz-sdk.jar` + `javac`), so it was compiled both ways: `EnumSet.of(..., SzFlag.SZ_ENTITY_INCLUDE_ALL_RELATIONS)` fails with `no suitable method found for of(SzFlag,SzFlag,Set<SzFlag>)`, and the `addAll` form compiles and prints six flags — the two named flags plus the composite's four members, independently confirming the server's `composite_members`. ⛔ **This corrected a defect in shipped guidance that the spec did not know about, and which its own premise would have entrenched.** `phase2-discover.md` already stated the rule (2026-08-14) and stated it **wrong**: *"the composite is a `long` bitmask"*. `javap` on the installed jar settles it — `com.senzing.sdk.SzFlag` is an enum **and** declares `public static final Set<SzFlag>` fields for the composites, so `SzFlag.SZ_ENTITY_INCLUDE_ALL_RELATIONS` is a `Set` and **not** an enum constant; the `long` of the same name lives in the *separate plural class* `SzFlags` (value `960`), which cannot be passed to a `Set<SzFlag>` parameter at all. The old note therefore sent the reader to the one class that does not fit the argument. ## stop-hook-ran-bare-python3-and-executed-its-own-payload

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-21
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/hooks/hooks.json`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/hooks/README.md`, `specs/INVARIANTS.md` (INV-052), `tests/test_hook_entries_name_a_script.py`, `tests/test_recap_checkpoint_writer.py`, and the invocation docstrings in `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/session-start.py`, `checkpoint-tick.py`, `session-end.py`, `precompact-recap.py`, `feedback-capture.py`, `write-gate.py`, `stop-nudge.py`, `docker_lifecycle.py`, `recap_checkpoint.py`
- **MCP re-check:** n/a (no Senzing fact) — the defect is in Claude Code hook invocation, which the Senzing server does not serve.
- **Summary:** ⛔ **Every one of the seven hooks had been running bare `python3` and never ran its script.** `/dry-run` phase 2 settled the question the 2026-08-21 static pass left open: **`args` is not part of the `type: command` hook schema.** Evidence, all documentary so it needed no enabled plugin — Anthropic's own `plugin-dev` plugin documents a command hook as "Execute bash commands" with the script inside `command` (`hook-development/SKILL.md:44-51`) and `grep -rn '\bargs\b'` across that entire skill returns nothing; seventeen `hooks.json` files across `claude-plugins-official`, `claude-code-plugins` and `every-marketplace` use `args` **zero** times, including the fixture that enumerates 15 events and every hook variant, and `security-guidance`, which passes a second argument *inside* the command string; every `"args"` key on the machine belongs to an `.mcp.json`, where it genuinely is the schema — the likely origin of the error. **Why three audits and 3,277 tests missed it:** bare `python3` fed each real payload exits **0 with no output on six of the seven events** (a payload that is a valid Python expression evaluates and exits), which is indistinguishable from this plugin's own documented "no-op outside a bootcamp" gating; only `Stop` fails visibly, because `stop_hook_active`'s JSON `false` is the one payload token that is not a Python name — which is exactly the bootcamper's 0.5.1 traceback. The fix moves each script into the `command` string, quoted so a plugin root containing a space survives. **Verified by side effect, not by silence** (the trap the previous pass documented): from a gate-satisfied project on Claude Code **2.1.239**, all seven now run — `session-start`/`precompact-recap`/`session-end` fold the checkpoint, `feedback-capture` injects its `additionalContext`, and **`write-gate.py` returns exit 2 and "Write blocked" on a `/tmp` path it had been passing silently**. **Establishes no new invariant; it CORRECTS INV-052 in place,** whose required exec form was the defect and whose stated rationale does not survive — command hooks *are* shell commands, so there was never a shell-free form to choose, and the quoting requirement now carries the cross-platform concern. Guard: `tests/test_hook_entries_name_a_script.py`, now 5 tests, negative-controlled with four mutations, all verified to land and all caught: the original defect (script moved back into `args`) → caught by the new `test_no_entry_relies_on_an_args_array`; a bare interpreter with no script anywhere → 2 tests; an unresolvable script path → 1; the file gutted to one entry → 3. ⚠️ **Two existing assertions had gone vacuous and one was silently blind, which is the transferable lesson:** `test_every_named_script_exists` and `test_no_hook_parses_its_payload_as_source` keyed off `resolved_args()`, so moving the scripts emptied their input and they passed while asserting nothing — the tell was a 0.000s run that spawned no subprocess. Both now read either channel, both carry anti-vacuity floors, and the behavioral one launches via the shell the way the host does. `test_recap_checkpoint_writer.py`'s wiring check read `args` only and failed honestly; it now reads both. ⛔ **Still not verified, and deliberately not claimed:** Claude Code has not been observed firing these hooks — that needs the plugin in `enabledPlugins` and a new session, which is the maintainer's call. **Windows is unverified** from a Linux suite. Criterion 2's second half therefore stays open in the spec even though the fix is shipped.
- **Commit:** 4fb1107

- **Not a spec** — a dated record of an audit run, per the `deep-dive-audit-*` precedent. Fourth run of 2026-08-21 and the first with the maintainer present, so the skill's **report-before-changing** guardrail applied: findings are recorded here and in one spec, and **nothing was fixed**.

- **Summary:** **The finding is that the negatives worklist was never worked.** `coverage_reports.py negatives` lists 23 `MCP-NEGATIVE` markers; **21 are dated `server 1.32.9`** (2026-08-13 to -17) while the live server is **1.33.0**, and none had been re-asked. Three audit iterations earlier the same day each read that report as clean, because it answers "is every marker well-formed?" and not "has any expired" — so a marker eight days stale is indistinguishable in its output from one re-asked this morning. Sampling four found **one already false**: `module-05-data-quality-mapping/SKILL.md:82` claims `search_docs(query='globalization')` returns no UTF-8 or supported-languages answer, and against 1.33.0 the `globalization` **category** returns the Globalization Guide's "What languages does Senzing support?" section answering it directly. It is also a route problem, not only staleness: the `owner:` clause named `search_docs` itself, recording an absence for a fact served under a filter the marker never used. ## the-teardown-contract-assumes-a-host-shell-and-the-container-has-neither-tool

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-21
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03b-truthset-visualization/visualization-api-reference.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03b-truthset-visualization/phase2-close.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-07-query-visualize-discover/phase1-query-visualize.md`, `tests/test_container_teardown_has_a_route_and_a_failure_report.py`
- **MCP re-check:** n/a (no Senzing fact) — the missing executables are a property of the Debian slim base image the **plugin itself** prescribes (`module-02-sdk-setup/SKILL.md:435`, `debian:bookworm-slim`), and the teardown contract is entirely the plugin's. No Senzing route owns either claim, so no `owner-checked:` clause applies; `get_capabilities` was called this session for the two Senzing facts recorded under other entries. `module-02-sdk-setup/SKILL.md` is **untouched**: change 3 decided against adding `procps`, so the container build needed no edit.
- **Summary:** All five proposed changes are in. The canonical contract now states that both its pid and port routes are host-shell routes unavailable inside the container, gives a route needing neither missing tool — signal the recorded pid through the shell builtin (`docker exec <c> sh -c 'kill <pid>'`, since `/bin/kill` is a `procps` binary and absent while `kill` as a builtin is not) and probe the port with the `python3` the SDK install brings — forbids treating the kill's exit status as evidence the server stopped, and says what the Bootcamper is told when the port still answers: name the port, say something is still listening, say the records may still be loaded, and **continue without the purge** rather than purging on an unverified stop. The ⛔ on `pkill -f` is unchanged. Both parallel sites (`phase2-close.md`, `phase1-query-visualize.md`) gained the container branch and link the full rule rather than restating it (INV-179). **Establishes no invariant, and this was checked rather than assumed: INV-223 already governs all of it** — it requires capturing the pid, terminating by it, falling back to the port, and states *"the port being free is the exit condition"*, which forecloses trusting an exit status by construction. Every rule added cites INV-223 at the rule, and `conformance.py rules` holds at **0** in a section citing no invariant with `per-rule` showing none of the three new rules uncited at itself. **Criteria not runtime-verified, both needing a reachable Docker daemon:** criterion 6 (verify on the Docker path with a real container — `docker info` fails here, so the route is written and test-asserted but not shown to work end to end) and criterion 7 (confirm the absences against the actual base image — **not done**; they rest on the field observation `exec: "…": executable file not found in $PATH`, which is real evidence and not the evidence the criterion asked for). **Beyond the spec:** the pid's **namespace** is now addressed — a `docker exec` launch yields a container-namespace pid, the only kind `docker exec … kill` can signal, while a host pid from `docker run` identifies the container so signaling it stops everything. Guard: `tests/test_container_teardown_has_a_route_and_a_failure_report.py`, 8 tests, deriving the teardown site set by scanning for the host-route commands rather than listing paths (INV-246). Negative-controlled with five mutations, all verified to land: four caught first time, and **the fifth escaped twice before the check was right** — a file-scoped string search passed with the cross-reference replaced by `nowhere.md` because these files name the contract more than once inside the window, so the assertion was changed to resolve path-shaped references instead, then narrowed again after a bare `name.md` used as prose triggered a false positive.

Reading the 37 individually against `INVARIANTS.md` by subject found **three** durable guarantees the ruleset mentions nowhere — the datastore mount-crossing measurement, registration re-runnability-by-construction (five sites, two statement and three referring), and the Poor band's three-outcome routing — plus **two** capture blocks stating a rule **INV-122** governs while citing INV-185/INV-252/INV-179 instead. Only **4 of 15** ledger entries recorded the deferral Step 5 requires; eleven said "Establishes no invariant", and for three subjects that was wrong. **Second finding, and the mechanism behind the first:** `conformance.py rules` is **section-scoped**, so a new unregistered rule is invisible whenever it lands beside any existing citation — and it reads clean *more* reliably as citations get denser. - **Summary:** Module 4 required the generated data to put a source in the 70-79% band and illustrated it with rates that score ~96.5. **Criterion walk.** (1) The requirement is now a completeness/slot-emptiness target — leave **30-43% of applicable field slots empty**, mean per-record completeness **57-70%** — and no longer offers per-field absence rates as the route — **met**. (2) The shipped worked table recomputes exactly: every row's `m`, completeness and score satisfy `0.70 × C + 0.25 × 100 + 0.05 × 100`, asserted by a guard that **parses the table and recomputes it** rather than grepping for the figures — **met**. (3) The `quality_intent` sample's gaps now reach its `target_band`: five rates summing to **2.20** of seven fields → completeness **68.6%** → score **78.0**, inside 70-79, with `measured_score` agreeing — **met**. (4) Module 4 routes to Module 5's Step 6 for the arithmetic rather than restating it (INV-179) — **met**. (5) The generation step must score its own output against the recorded band before the module closes, and **widen the gaps rather than adjust any score** (INV-239's diagnose-don't-grade line) — **met**. (6) A guard asserts the example rates land in the band they claim, negative-controlled twice — **met**, see below. (7) INV-239 still holds: gaps in non-key fields only, keys present and unique, at least one source at ≥80%, `quality_intent` per source — **met**, and the pre-existing `test_synthesized_scenario_has_quality_gaps` still passes. (8) Cross-platform and language-agnostic: prose and arithmetic; the target is a number, not code — **met**. Suite **3205 passed, 3 skipped**.
- ⛔ **DEVIATION — the spec's own worked table is arithmetically wrong in the row that matters, and this implementation does not ship its figures.** The spec instructs completeness **58.9 – 71.8%** for the 70-79 band. Computed: with `format_consistency = 100` and `duplicate_rate = 0` the composite reduces to `score = 0.70·C + 30`, so score 79 ⟹ C = **70.00%** and score 70 ⟹ C = **57.14%**. The correct band is **57.1 – 70.0%**, and the spec's change-1 prose ("roughly 59-72%") inherits the same slip. Every **other** row in its table reproduces exactly (96.5, 90.0, 85.0), and its headline "30% to 43% of slots empty" is right — so the diagnosis is sound and only that one column is off. What shipped is the computed figure. ⚠️ **The guard's second negative control is precisely this:** injecting the spec's own 58.9–71.8% values fails `test_the_band_row_actually_spans_the_band` and `test_every_row_recomputes`. Implementing faithfully would have shipped a wrong number into the file whose whole defect was a wrong number.
- **Also corrected during implementation:** a first draft of the `quality_intent` sample deliberately **missed** the band with a note explaining why, which contradicts criterion 3 outright. Recomputed to land inside it. And a rewording of the requirement broke the literal phrase `at least one source in the 70-79% band` that `test_synthesized_scenario_has_quality_gaps` asserts; the prose was restored to preserve it rather than the guard relaxed.
- **INVARIANTS.md deliberately unchanged.** The spec suggested INV-239 gain the completeness target "if the band figure is to be binding rather than illustrative". That is an invariant amendment, the spec drafts no wording for one, and inventing invariant wording unattended is outside what this run was authorized to do — **flagged as a candidate, not minted.** ⚠️ **Consequence stated:** the 30-43% target is now binding in Module 4's prose and guarded by a test, but INV-239 still describes the band only as a band, so the two could drift if INV-239 is later edited without reference to this.
- **The open design question the spec surfaced is left open, deliberately.** Reaching 70-79 honestly means about a third of all field values absent — heavier degradation than a real CRM or POS export usually carries. ## capture-steps-pass-the-flags-without-naming-the-capture-script

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-21
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-07-query-visualize-discover/phase1-query-visualize.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03b-truthset-visualization/phase1-visualization.md`, `tests/test_bundled_script_and_production_paths.py`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/bootcamp-onboarding/module-completion.md` (confirmed unchanged as the procedure of record), `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03b-truthset-visualization/phase2-close.md` (checked: its pointer still resolves), `specs/IMPLEMENTED.md` (this entry)
- **MCP re-check:** n/a (no Senzing fact) — the defect is that a bundled script was parameterized and never named. Verified in the codebase instead: `capture_screenshots.py` accepts `--url`/`--html`, `--tabs`, `--name`, `--query` and `--single`, and before this change was named in only three places, none of which was a step that requires capture.
- **Summary:** Both requiring steps now name `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/capture_screenshots.py` with its skill-relative fallback (INV-185, INV-252) and carry a runnable invocation with that step's own arguments. **Criterion walk.** (1) Both name the script with both resolution paths and a runnable command — **met**. (2) `module-completion.md` remains the single statement of the procedure; neither step duplicates its backend list, exit-code handling or caption rule — **met**, and the module-07 site says so explicitly (INV-179). (3) Each step's silent-skip path is conditioned on the helper's **exit code**, with the sentence that closes the actual failure: *"no headless capability" is a conclusion the helper reaches and reports, never one you reach first* — **met**. (4) The INV-185 sweep is widened and negative-controlled — **met**, see below. (5) The existing sweep still passes and every added invocation resolves under `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` — **met**. (6) Module 3b's invocation states its live capture cannot be re-taken after teardown, because that module purges its records at close — **met**. (7) Cross-platform and language-agnostic: a bundled `python3` script invoked identically on all three platforms (INV-052), backend discovery is the helper's own concern — **met**. Suite **3173 passed, 3 skipped**.
- **The widened guard, and the false positives it started with.** `AParameterizedInvocationNamesItsScript` sweeps for helper-only flags (`--tabs`, `--single`, `--out-dir`) and requires any use to name a resolved script. This is the generalizable half: the existing INV-185 sweep discovers invocations **by script name**, so it catches a *wrong* resolution and is structurally blind to a *missing* one. First version fired on **five** sites, all false positives — `module-completion.md` explaining what `--single` and `--tabs` mean, and this implementation's own sentence listing `--single` among things stated once elsewhere. It could not distinguish *"run this with `--tabs`"* from *"`--tabs` means X"*. Added a command-vs-prose discriminator: a line counts only inside a fenced block or carrying an interpreter token. Negative-controlled by stripping the script name from Module 3b's invocation (both the fenced path and the prose mention, since either satisfies the window) and confirming the mutation lands.
- **Deviation — the implementation changed under a guard, and the guard was right.** `test_screenshot_retention_and_order.call_sites()` **discovers** every shipped file containing `capture_screenshots` rather than listing them, deliberately (its docstring cites INV-246 for replacing a two-file constant that would have left a third site green). Naming the script therefore converted both requiring steps from *pointers* into *call sites*, and three assertions immediately demanded they carry the retention and tab-order rules — which the spec's change 3 had said not to restate. Resolved in the guard's favor: the spec forbade duplicating the **procedure** (backends, exit codes, `--single`, the caption rule), while what the guard wants is two one-clause **constraints**, and a step carrying a runnable invocation is exactly where a subset capture or a directory-scan embed order can happen. Narrowing the discovery instead would have restored the blindness its docstring exists to prevent. Both sites now also state: embed in the app's tab order, never in capture/append or filename-discovery order, citing the contract's tab table rather than restating the list; and never let a caption imply a result set the image does not show, disclosing an empty or inactive Search / Probe panel (INV-123). **The spec's framing — "the steps gain the identity of the tool, not a copy of its manual" — was almost right: the identity brings two constraints with it.**
- **Establishes no invariant** — the new ⛔s cite INV-185, INV-252, INV-179 and INV-123, all existing; `conformance.py rules` uncited count unchanged at 1.
- **Commit:** `e805e57`
