- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-04-data-collection/SKILL.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-01-business-problem/phase1-discovery.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-05-data-quality-mapping/phase2-data-mapping.md`, `tests/test_shape_claims_precede_mapping_claims.py` (new), `tests/test_data_collection_generated_scenarios.py`, `tests/test_generated_scenario_dataset_eligibility.py`, `tests/test_synthesized_scenario_has_quality_gaps.py`
- **MCP re-check:** **confirmed in substance, with one correction to the spec's quotation.** `search_docs(query='NAME_FULL single name field do not parse NAME_FIRST NAME_LAST', category='data_mapping')` and a follow-up on the rule's own wording, server **1.32.9, 2026-08-17**, return the Entity Specification's *Name > Feature: NAME* section: `NAME_FULL` is documented as the *"Single-field name when type (person vs org) is unknown or only a full name is provided"*, and the rule reads *"Prefer parsed person names (`NAME_FIRST`/`NAME_LAST`/…) when available; use `NAME_ORG` for organizations; use `NAME_FULL` only when the type is unknown or only a single field exists"*. ⚠️ **The spec's quoted sentence is NOT what the indexed corpus returns.** It quotes *"do NOT attempt to parse a single name field—use NAME_FULL … (even if they appear parseable, like \"Smith, Robert\")"*, attributing it to the full 73KB document fetched from the resources URL. That stronger prohibition, and the `"Smith, Robert"` example, appear nowhere in the indexed chunks I could reach this session — so **the shipped guidance quotes the verified wording, not the spec's**. The conclusion is identical (a single name field maps to `NAME_FULL`; "when available" means the source provides separate fields), and I did not launder the unverified phrasing into the plugin (INV-080). The re-check also surfaced three adjacent ❌ rules worth shipping: do not mix `NAME_FULL` with parsed fields in one `NAME` object, do not mix `NAME_ORG` with parsed person fields, and do not split one name across two `NAME` objects.
- **Summary:** Fixed both causes. **Cause 1 (sequencing):** Module 4's synthesized branch now asks for **shape differences** and forbids stating — or inviting — what any field maps to, saying why (the specification is not read until Module 5) and where the claim lands if made (`config/data_sources.yaml` and `docs/data_source_locations.md`, where it reads as settled fact a module before anything can check it), with the wording to use instead. Module 1's Step 4a invariant is restated as **cross-source mapping divergence**, with an explicit ⛔ against the old unqualified "at least one transformation" phrasing and a list of kinds that genuinely qualify (date normalization, code/value standardization, composing a `RECORD_ID`). **Cause 2 — the one the report missed and the more consequential:** the module's two leading examples were **direct mappings** under the specification, not transformations, so the module was teaching that a joined name is a transformation waiting to happen. They are kept as shape differences and the `NAME_FULL` rule is stated where it changes what gets generated, with its route, version and date. **Module 5 now states the rule as a rule** rather than only showing `full_name -> NAME_FULL` in examples — it is the authority the other two modules route to, and an implicit authority is not one. **⚠️ Nothing weakens the branch's other requirements**, asserted directly: quality gaps (INV-239), record-key integrity (INV-180), `quality_intent`, and the license-sizing directive added earlier the same day in the same branch. **Criteria walked one at a time**, plus a corpus-wide scan for the reported claim shape in four phrasings, with a quoted-retraction carve-out and a not-vacuous control. **⚠️ Three existing tests pinned the old wording and were updated, not loosened:** two asserted `mapping-complexity-rich (needs at least one transformation` and one asserted `Generate the mapping complexity the scenario promised`. Their intent — that the requirement is carried through, and that `truthset` cannot satisfy it — is unchanged and still asserted; the Truth Set is pre-mapped and uniform, so it fails the reworded requirement exactly as it failed the old one. Each carries a note recording the rewording and why. **⚠️ Not runtime-verified:** no scenario was generated and no data mapped — these are assertions about shipped guidance (INV-108). **This implementation established no invariant** — the spec drafts none, though it *reworded* one of Module 1's Step 4a validation conditions, which is prose in a skill file rather than an entry in `INVARIANTS.md`. **Suite: 3124 passed, 3 skipped, 2585 subtests, 0 failed** (pytest exit 0).

## generated-dataset-is-sized-before-anything-measures-the-license

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-17
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-04-data-collection/SKILL.md`, `tests/test_generated_dataset_size_is_a_license_decision.py` (new)
- **MCP re-check:** **n/a for the change; one relied-upon negative re-confirmed.** The fix is a routing directive, so it asserts no Senzing fact of its own — deliberately, since restating the measurement procedure is what the spec forbids. But the file's existing note that `recordLimit` is observation-only was re-asked rather than trusted: `get_sdk_reference(topic='response_schemas', filter='get_license')` on server **1.32.9, 2026-08-17** returns `data: []` — the **signature** is documented for all five bindings (`get_license() -> str` in Python) while the **response shape** is not, so `recordLimit` remains observation-only and the note at `:800` stays accurate (INV-080/INV-149).
- **Summary:** Closed the gap between a correct rule and the site it binds. The `provenance: synthesized` branch — where the record counts are actually chosen and the files written — now states that **how many records to generate is a license-capacity decision**, forbids choosing it before the limit is measured, cites INV-244, and **routes** to the canonical framing block rather than restating its procedure. ⚠️ It says explicitly not to re-derive that procedure, because a copy at the decision site would be the third and a rule stated three times drifts in two of them — which the `inv244-…` implementation had already recorded. The framing's trigger sentence now names **generating** a dataset, not only sampling one down: sizing a dataset into existence and cutting one are the same decision under this rule, and only one of them was recognizable in the old wording. The branch also **resolves** rather than only warning — on a measured `recordLimit: 0`, size by what the scenario needs, with the cost of under-generating named (too little overlap for Modules 6 and 7, INV-150). The reported run is recorded with its figures (538 → 466 to stay under the 500-record built-in limit; the workstation actually carried `recordLimit: 0`) and with **why the miss is natural** — nothing is being cut, so the framing's "sampling" language did not obviously apply, and the measurement sits several steps downstream of the decision. **⛔ The guard's design is the substantive part, and the spec is right about why.** The two prior specs each fixed a site that *reads* `license_record_limit`; this site never reads it — it makes the decision the field exists to inform without consulting it — so a guard derived from "every branch on `license_record_limit`" (INV-246's usual derivation) is **structurally blind** to it. **`tests/test_module06_license_reconciliation.py` was deliberately NOT extended** — the spec offered "extend, or add a sibling", and a sibling is right here: that file's `discover_branches()` derivation enumerates sites that *read* `license_record_limit`, which is exactly the derivation blind to this defect, so folding a non-reading site into it would make its scan look more complete than it is. It is left untouched and passing. The new guard therefore slices the synthesized branch out of the file by its own content and asserts the mechanism *inside that slice*, with three controls proving the approach: the slice is asserted **not** to reach the framing block (or the assertions could pass on the framing's text instead of the decision site), the directive is asserted present within the slice, and the sibling generation directives are asserted undisturbed. **⚠️ Not runtime-verified:** no dataset was generated and no license measured — these are assertions about shipped guidance (INV-108). Whether a live run now measures before sizing is a conversational property needing `dry-run` phase 3, and it is worth saying that this defect was *already* a case of correct text not binding, which is precisely the class an offline suite cannot settle. **This implementation established no invariant** — the spec drafts none; INV-244 already states the rule and this makes it reachable. **Suite: 3044 passed, 3 skipped, 2550 subtests, 0 failed** (pytest exit 0).

- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/senzing_viz_server.py`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03b-truthset-visualization/visualization-api-reference.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-07-query-visualize-discover/phase1-query-visualize.md`, `tests/test_graph_colors_by_source_combination.py` (new), `tests/test_brand_sync.py`

No SDK method, flag or response schema is asserted and no absence is relied on. Server **1.32.9** confirmed reachable this session (`get_capabilities`, 2026-08-16).
- **Summary:** A node is now colored by its **whole source set** — `Model.color_keys()` returns every source plus every observed combination as one list, allocated in a **single** `color_for_sources` pass, and the page's `srcKeyOf(d)` joins an entity's sorted sources into the key that drives **fill, stroke and stroke width** alike. The legend gains combination rows, counted over the nodes actually drawn and labeled as combinations, because a color a viewer cannot name is no improvement on the wrong color. The graph payload is bounded (`GRAPH_NODE_CAP = 1500`) and carries `total` and `capped`, ranking candidates by **source span first** — an entity spanning several sources is exactly what a truncation ordered by id would drop — then connectivity, record count and id for determinism, with edges filtered to surviving nodes. All of it is stated as behavior in the any-language contract (INV-090/INV-104/INV-124), since the Bootcamper's app is built from that contract, and step 3c now warns that **this is the rule the Truth Set cannot test**. **Criteria walked one at a time:** a cross-source entity's rendered appearance is asserted distinct from both its members'; no two keys collide on `(fill, stroke, stroke_width)`; the allocation is asserted to be a **single call site**; all three channels are asserted to read the key and no rendering expression reads `data_sources[0]`; the legend's combination rows and labels are asserted; the cap's total, determinism, span-first ranking and edge consistency are asserted; and both the endpoint and the snapshot are asserted to apply the cap. **⛔ Three deviations recorded on the spec, one of them substantive.** (1) **"Truth Set output is unchanged" is not literally achievable and asserting it would have been asserting the defect** — Truth Set entities that genuinely span sources *should* now change color. The checkable guarantee is asserted instead: single-source entities degenerate to their own source code, and the Truth Set's **preferred** palette assignments are proven unchanged when combination keys join the allocation. (2) The cap value is mine; 1500 sits above the existing 400-entity subgraph threshold, so it bounds payload and snapshot size without changing what any current view draws. (3) ⚠️ **Not verified at production scale** — the spec's ninth criterion — because this environment has no engine and no multi-thousand-entity corpus; everything is verified on synthetic models carrying the reported shape, and **the snapshot-size criterion is implemented but unmeasured**, needing `dry-run`. **⚠️ Two of my own errors, both caught by the repo's guards:** a comment I wrote said "Coloring", failed the US-English guard registered earlier today, and was corrected; and `tests/test_brand_sync.py` pinned the literal `d.data_sources[0]` stroke expression this spec replaces — its criterion (swatch and mark agree for one key) is unchanged and still asserted, only the pinned expression moved. **This implementation established no invariant** — the spec drafts none. **Suite: 2968 passed, 3 skipped, 2523 subtests, 0 failed** (pytest exit 0).

## the-viz-contract-never-states-the-bind-host-so-a-port-conflict-can-succeed

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-17
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03b-truthset-visualization/visualization-api-reference.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/senzing_viz_server.py`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-07-query-visualize-discover/phase1-query-visualize.md`, `tests/test_viz_server_bind_and_identity.py` (new)
- **MCP re-check:** **n/a (no Senzing fact).** The defect is in the plugin's own server contract and in host-OS socket-binding behavior; no SDK, flag, response shape or server behavior is asserted, and no absence about the MCP server is relied on. Server **1.32.9** confirmed reachable this session (`get_capabilities`, 2026-08-16).
- **Summary:** Stated both rules **in the any-language contract**, which is where the defect actually lived: the bundled Python server has always bound `127.0.0.1` explicitly, and the Bootcamper was running their own port of it, so a Java implementation using the idiomatic `InetSocketAddress(port)` — a wildcard bind — was fully conformant and unsafe. That is the INV-002 boundary INV-164 and INV-190 each had to record case by case. **New contract sections:** *Binding the port* requires an explicit loopback bind with the reason attached (a wildcard bind does **not** collide with an existing loopback listener — both succeed, two processes listen, either may answer), names the idiomatic wrong form in Java, Node and C# so a faithful port does not write the shorter thing, and states that **a successful bind is not proof the port was free**. *Confirming the server that answers is yours* requires a post-bind `/api/stats` probe comparing a per-process **nonce**, ⚠️ explicitly **not** the record count — two runs of the same project agree on the count, which is exactly the case where the stale listener is the Bootcamper's own earlier server — and requires a disagreement to **stop**, never to degrade into a warning above a working-looking link, since the whole failure mode is that everything looks fine. It also says why both remedies are needed: loopback binding defeats a colliding *loopback* listener, the probe defeats a *wildcard* one, and only asking which server answered covers both. **In the Python reference:** the loopback address is now the named `BIND_HOST` constant carrying its reason, the bind is wrapped so a genuine collision reports and exits rather than tracebacks, `/api/stats` exposes `server_nonce`, and startup serves on a background thread only long enough to run `confirm_server_identity` **before** the URL is printed — an unanswerable probe counts as failure, because a gate that exists because success looks like success cannot treat silence as permission. Module 7 step 3c's port guidance no longer reads a successful start as proof. **Criteria walked one at a time**, including the two the spec was emphatic about: the bind host is **pinned** (constant, call site, and a scan for `""`/`0.0.0.0` forms) so a future edit cannot widen it; and the probe is **negative-controlled against a constructed two-listener condition** — a real foreign HTTP server is stood up on the port and the probe must reject it, with a fixture control proving our own server is accepted (without which the rejection test would pass for the wrong reason), plus a no-nonce responder and an unanswerable-port case. The contract rules are asserted to be free of Python names, so a Java/C#/TypeScript implementation can satisfy them (INV-002). **⚠️ Disclosure — `main()`'s serve path is NOT runtime-verified**, and cannot be by this suite: it needs a live Senzing engine (INV-108). What *is* runtime-verified is the mechanism it wires — a `ThreadingHTTPServer` served from a background thread, probed, then shut down, which every test here exercises against real sockets — plus the probe itself in four scenarios. The wiring is pinned by **source-order** assertions instead: the probe precedes the URL, a failed probe shuts down and returns non-zero without printing it, and `shutdown()` precedes `server_close()`. ⚠️ **The loopback/wildcard coexistence itself was observed on macOS**; socket rules differ across platforms, which is precisely why the contract makes the *probe* the cross-platform requirement rather than the bind. **⚠️ One of my own errors:** the first source-order test used a fixed 220-character window that overran `return 1` into the success path and asserted about the wrong code; it now slices to the branch's own end. **This implementation established no invariant** — the spec drafts none, and it applies INV-002/INV-090/INV-124 rather than adding a rule. **Suite: 2943 passed, 3 skipped, 2515 subtests, 0 failed** (pytest exit 0).

It now looks the entry up **by tab**; its subject (the slug/filename join between the two scripts) is unchanged, and it additionally asserts exactly one entry per tab, so it now also guards against duplication. Graduation's Step 1a records how to read the new `the manifest undercounts` finding — as too small a denominator rather than a missing image — and says the merge should prevent recurrence while the PNG count is what notices if it is bypassed. **⚠️ Not runtime-verified:** no browser ran and no real capture was performed; `write_manifest` was exercised directly with stub PNGs, which is what makes the merge logic testable offline (INV-108). **This implementation established no invariant** — the spec drafts none, and this repairs an existing mechanism (INV-122's manifest) rather than adding a standing rule. **Suite: 2866 passed, 3 skipped, 2491 subtests, 0 failed** (pytest exit 0); census clean at 257.

- **Summary:** Step 25 now branches **before** it asks: `### 25a.` (bootcamp-generated — states the self-direction and proceeds, asking nothing) and `### 25b.` (real stakeholders — carries the pinned question), so the question is structurally unreachable from the suppressed path rather than twelve lines below its prohibition at the section's outer level. The verbatim wording is unchanged (INV-056, asserted). 25a additionally carries an explicit ⛔ forbidding it from borrowing 25b's question, since manufacturing one there would breach INV-006 in the opposite direction — the spec's fourth proposed-change item, which is easy to get backwards. **⛔ The sweep is the substantive part, and it inverted the expected result.** Scanning every shipped `.md` for the shape — a suppression instruction (`do not ask`/`do not offer`/`never ask`) appearing **before** an outer-level 👉 within 25 lines — matched **8 sections** on the crude scan and **4** once proximity was applied. Three of those four were **already correct**, each by one of the two mechanisms the plugin uses without having named either: per-branch sub-headings (`module-01-business-problem/phase2-document-confirm.md` §9a/9b) or a self-contained precondition immediately above the question (`module-02-sdk-setup/SKILL.md` "Fallback only — when detection is genuinely unavailable…", `module-04-data-collection/SKILL.md` "Only when the source has **no** recorded provenance…"). Four other matches were excluded as unrelated prose in long sections, at 85, 218 and 719 lines' separation, plus one where the 👉 **precedes** its supposed suppressor (`onboarding-flow.md` §4, an unconditional question). **So exactly one site had the defect — but the discriminator it revealed is the durable finding:** the three correct sites state a condition a reader meets *at* the question, while the broken one said only *"Otherwise (a real business problem with stakeholders)"*, which is a **relative** condition — meaningless without the paragraph above it, which is precisely the paragraph a guide arriving at pinned text has not re-read. `tests/test_suppressed_branch_has_no_pinned_question.py` derives its site set by scanning (INV-246) and rejects exactly that shape, so a future step growing it fails without anyone remembering this spec. **Negative-controlled:** with the pre-fix text restored, the class test failed naming `phaseD-validation.md:113` and the section by heading; with the fix, all 7 pass — and the not-vacuous test asserts the scan matches more than one site, so the class assertion cannot quietly become empty. **⚠️ Not runtime-verified:** whether a live guide on a generated scenario now actually asks nothing at step 25 is a conversational property the offline suite cannot judge (INV-108) — it needs `dry-run` phase 3. What is asserted is that the shipped text no longer offers the question on that path. **This implementation established no invariant:** the spec drafts none, and the rule this would state ("a pinned question governed by a suppression instruction must be structurally scoped or carry a self-contained precondition") is my wording rather than the maintainer's — flagged as a candidate instead of minted. **Suite: 2828 passed, 3 skipped, 2490 subtests, 0 failed.**

## bytecode-caching-hides-a-latent-syntax-error-from-the-suite

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-15
- **Files changed:** `tests/test_sdk_update_offer.py` (raw docstring), `tests/test_python_sources_compile_cleanly.py` (new, 7 tests), `specs/bytecode-caching-hides-a-latent-syntax-error-from-the-suite.md` (deviations)
- **MCP re-check:** **n/a (no Senzing fact).** A Python source-syntax defect and a gap in the repo's own checks. No Senzing claim asserted, no absence about the server relied on. Server **1.32.9** (`get_capabilities`, 2026-08-15) recorded earlier this session; no MCP tool called for this implementation.
- **Summary:** `tests/test_sdk_update_offer.py:175` carried an invalid escape `\\\`` in a docstring — a `SyntaxWarning` today, a **`SyntaxError`** in a future Python, at which point the file stops importing and the suite stops running. It was invisible because a `SyntaxWarning` fires at **compile** time, not on import of a cached module, so `__pycache__` silenced it on every run after the first. **Criterion walk — 6 of 7 hold, 1 disclosed.** (1) *Compiles clean, quoted claim unchanged* — fixed with `r"""`, and the claim was verified **byte-identical** by `md5sum` against `d35046d` rather than eyeballed, because INV-219's reasoning depends on that exact wording. (2) *Guard compiles every `.py` under the four roots from source, failing on `SyntaxWarning`/`DeprecationWarning`/`SyntaxError`* — file set derived by scanning (INV-246) with a >100-file floor so a collapsed scan cannot pass vacuously. (3) *Reads source text, never imports, and the docstring says why* — asserted by `test_the_import_blind_spot_is_disclosed`, since "simplifying" it into an import check would silently restore the exact blind spot. (4) **Negative-controlled per root, as the criterion required** — a defect planted separately in `tests/`, `plugins/`, `.claude/` and `scripts/`; all four reddened **and named the offending file**; both docstring disclosures mutated independently; all plants removed and the tree verified clean. (5) *Stdlib-only, imports nothing from `plugins/`* (INV-108). (6) *Cross-platform/language-agnostic* — `pathlib` and `compile()`. (7) ⛔ **NOT runtime-verified:** this proves the files *compile* under the Python running the suite, not that they run correctly, and not their behavior under a future Python that has promoted the warning to an error — it ensures the repo is already clean when that lands. ⚠️ **Two deviations, both my own errors, both caught by the guard being built.** The explanatory note I first added inside the docstring contained a literal `"""`, which **closed the docstring early** and turned the following prose into code — compiling from source caught it in seconds, which is the spec's own thesis demonstrated on itself. And the per-root floor initially asserted every scanned root contains Python; the repo-root `scripts/` holds only `sync-check.sh`, so it was corrected to floor the three Python-bearing roots while keeping `scripts/` scanned, with its emptiness recorded by its own test — a guard that asserts a falsehood gets "fixed" by deleting the assertion. **Suite:** 2722 → **2729 passed, 3 skipped**, verdict `OK`, and the pytest warning line is gone. **Establishes no invariant** — "Python must compile cleanly" is **INV-004** applied rather than a new guarantee, and the guard carries the reasoning; raise it for an ID only if a future run finds the rule being argued about.
- **Commit:** `9dd81e7`

It surfaced only because `d35046d` changed one unrelated docstring line in that file (`:295`) and invalidated the cached bytecode. ⚠️ **It looked like mine and was not** — verified rather than assumed: the escape is present in `d35046d~1` (`grep -c` → 1) and `git show d35046d` changed exactly one line, `:295`. Citing INV-251 at all 37 would be the citation noise this skill's Goldilocks section warns against; the two that genuinely were canonical statements (`ground-rules.md:34` and `:39`) were fixed in `d35046d`. **The gap is closed by disproof, not by edits.** **Concision:** unchanged; no shipped file changed. **Establishes no invariant.** ⛔ **Coverage limits:** ~712 citations of multiply-cited invariants outside `ground-rules.md` remain unread. Conversational invariants remain untested here. Nothing was executed in this run or the seven before it beyond compiling Python from source (`libSz.so` absent; `fpdf2`, poppler, `docker`, Chrome present and unused). ⚠️ **Eight audits this session. This is the first whose finding was NOT in the previous audit's own fix** — it is a genuine latent defect that predates the session and was invisible by construction. **`dry-run` remains owed: seven conversational rules changed today and none has been exercised in a live turn.**

## host-rendered-control-prompt-interrupts-a-pending-question

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-15
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/bootcamp-onboarding/ground-rules.md`, `tests/test_no_host_control_is_offered_as_a_question.py` (15 → 21 tests), `specs/INVARIANTS.md` (INV-247 observation + clarification), `specs/host-rendered-control-prompt-interrupts-a-pending-question.md` (deviations)

- **Summary:** A second bootcamper report of the same onboarding-preface interruption, on a fresh run three hours after the first, quoted the host dialog verbatim — *"Set up auto mode for your environment?"* with "Set it up" / "Not now" / "Don't show again". Those are harness UI affordances, not text a model emits, which settles what the first report left open: **the prompt is host-rendered and the guide originated nothing.** Two consequences, both fixed here. (1) *The uncovered case.* `ground-rules.md:106-115` forbids the guide **originating** a host-control question and `:666-674` handled the bootcamper **asking** about one; a host dialog arriving unbidden over a pending 👉 was neither, and the generic recovery rule at `:677-684` enumerated four interruptions that are all conversational and all guide-visible. (2) *An over-claim in shipped text.* `ground-rules.md:127-132` and the guard docstring both stated a bootcamper "was asked" about auto mode, implying a guide defect **no run has shown**. **Criterion walk — 7 of 8 hold, 1 disclosed as not runtime-verifiable.** (1) *Interruption list names a host-rendered prompt* — `ground-rules.md:680-681`, asserted by `test_the_interruption_list_names_a_host_rendered_prompt`. (2) *Entry fires on "raises", not only "asks"* — the bullet is retitled "A host control the bootcamper raises — in any form" and covers "or tell you that a prompt for one appeared over the bootcamp"; asserted by `test_the_entry_fires_when_a_host_prompt_merely_APPEARS`. (3) *Neither file implies the guide asked* — `test_no_shipped_text_claims_the_GUIDE_asked_about_auto_mode` (an `assertNotRegex` plus a positive anchor) and the new `TheCorrectedAttributionIsDisclosed` class for the docstring. (4) *INV-247's MUST condition byte-identical* — **verified mechanically, not by eye**: the 586-byte condition was extracted from `git show HEAD:specs/INVARIANTS.md` and from the working copy and compared identical. (5) *No file claims the plugin suppresses a host control* — the pre-existing `test_no_shipped_file_claims_the_plugin_suppresses_a_host_control` still passes; nothing was added. (6) *The answer names no dismissal affordance* — per the maintainer's 2026-08-15 decision the guide stays silent on "Don't show again"; `ground-rules.md:672-675` forbids it and `test_the_answer_does_not_name_a_dismissal_affordance` asserts the prohibition ships. (7) *Negative-controlled* — **all 6 mutations landed and reverted cleanly.** ⚠️ **One escaped on the first pass and the assertion was tightened:** the docstring check matched the bare token `host-rendered`, which also occurs in this spec's **own filename** cited two lines below, so gutting the claim still passed — the filename was certifying the sentence. Re-anchored to "that prompt is host-rendered". (8) ⛔ **NOT runtime-verified, and must not be read as covered:** whether a guide actually re-presents the pending 👉 after a host dialog interrupts. It is a live-turn property, and the guide **may never observe the dialog at all** — if the bootcamper dismisses it, nothing enters the conversation, so the recovery fires only on the evidence that does arrive (they mention it, or answer something that does not fit the pending question). Needs `dry-run` phase 3, and even there is reachable only by simulating the mention. **Cross-platform/language-agnostic:** holds — Markdown prose and a stdlib-only guard, no platform or language surface. **Suite:** 2683 → **2689 passed, 3 skipped**, verdict line `OK`. `coverage_reports.py shipped` reports none, so INV-247 remains cited where it binds. **Establishes no new invariant**; see the deviations note for the one judgment call — two requirements registered under INV-247's clarification rather than as new IDs.
- **Commit:** `3d52531`

## inv247-guard-is-narrower-than-the-invariant-it-enforces

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-15
- **Files changed:** `tests/test_no_host_control_is_offered_as_a_question.py` (structural slash-command check, dual disclosure, dated snapshot marker, 4 self-disclosure tests; 10 → 15 tests), `specs/inv247-guard-is-narrower-than-the-invariant-it-enforces.md` (deviations)
- **MCP re-check:** n/a (no Senzing fact) — confirmed, not assumed. Server **1.32.9** (`get_capabilities`, 2026-08-15). Test source and the plugin's conversational layer; no Senzing claim asserted.
- **Summary:** INV-247 governs a **class** ("a session- or host-level control"); its enforcer tested a closed vocabulary of eight literals, so a control phrased outside that list passed while breaching the invariant — and the docstring disclosed the *runtime* limit emphatically while saying nothing about the vocabulary one, which reads as completeness. Both halves fixed. `SLASH_COMMAND` now matches `/<command>` **structurally** inside pinned questions and allows only `model` and `effort`, so a control this repo has never heard of fails the day it appears — no list to extend. The vocabulary check survives only for non-slash phrasings and carries a dated `⚠️ SNAPSHOT, NOT A CLOSED SET` marker; the docstring states both limits and points the reader from the expiring check to the structural one. **Criterion walk: all 6 hold, 1 with a disclosed caveat.** (1)–(3) asserted by a new `ThisGuardDisclosesWhatItCannotSee` class. (4) **Verified with the decisive control:** a planted `👉 **Would you like to enable /thinking …**` — a name in no vocabulary list, which the pre-fix guard passed — now fails. (5) INV-247 unchanged. (6) Linux only; stdlib `re`/`pathlib`. **Negative-controlled: 5 mutations, all landed, all caught** after the correction below; both files restored and verified identical. ⛔ **THREE MUTATIONS ESCAPED FIRST TIME, AND THE CAUSE WAS THE VERY DEFECT THIS SPEC IS ABOUT.** The disclosure assertions read `Path(__file__)` — the test's own source — so each assertion's regex literal was part of the text it searched; gutting the docstring left the pattern strings behind and every check matched its own literal. **A guard that greps the file it is written in cannot fail.** Repointed to the module `__doc__`, which holds the prose and not the patterns; the snapshot-date check still reads source (that marker is a `#` comment) but its `\d{4}` escapes make self-matching impossible. ⚠️ **One escape is inherent, recorded rather than fixed:** widening `SANCTIONED_SLASH` defeats the structural check, as widening any allowlist would. It cannot be closed from inside the guard; what limits it is that the widening is a visible one-line edit beside a comment saying what the set is for — unlike the vocabulary list's silent expiry, which needed no edit at all to go wrong. **The spec's predicted `tests/test_guard_disclosures_survive.py` was deliberately NOT created.** Its `## Affected files` offered it as "new, **or** the assertion added to the file above"; the second branch was taken, because a guard asserting another guard's docstring belongs beside the docstring it protects — split across two files, the disclosure and its enforcement drift independently, and the new file would itself need a third file to guard *its* claims. The four assertions live in `ThisGuardDisclosesWhatItCannotSee` inside the enforcer. ⚠️ **This omission was caught by `test_spec_ledger_invariants.py`, not by me** — the entry originally recorded the work without accounting for the predicted file, which is the INV-097 shape (a spec names a second consumer, only the first is built, the ledger says done). The suite was **red at the moment of commit** and I chained the commit after the test run instead of gating on it; `2c81466` therefore landed on a red suite and this correction follows it. Full suite **`OK (skipped=3)`, 2668 tests**, delta +5 = exactly the tests added; `citations.py verify` clean, run after this entry existed. **Establishes no invariant** — INV-247 was correct as written; only its enforcer moved.

That file enforces INV-243/INV-245 *at step 17*, pinning the counter-scoping hazard and its two resolutions in one bounded step; the new file enforces the same invariants *across their binding surface* by derivation. Merging them would put a swept sweep and a step-scoped assertion in one place and make the step-17 window ambiguous. The prediction is answered here rather than left silent, which is what the affected-files gate asks for — it fired on this entry and this sentence is the response.
- **MCP re-check:** **n/a (no Senzing fact).** Entirely internal consistency between INV-243/INV-245 and the plugin's own steps; no MCP tool was called and no Senzing claim is asserted. Server 1.32.9 was established earlier this session.
- **Summary:** INV-243/INV-245 were cited only in `phaseC`, whose own gate skips the file unless the Bootcamper has 2+ sources, while the paths everyone takes wrote and displayed per-source counts unreconciled. **Criterion walk: all 5 hold.** (1) *Phase B's registry write requires reconciliation and cites both IDs* — and does so more strongly than the spec asked, see below. (2) *Phase C step 12 states the counts shown are reconciled and what is shown when one is not* — `ThePresentationSiteIsCovered` pins the ID and the `unverified` disposition inside the **bounded step**, not the file. (3) *Phase D's per-source statistics carry the requirement* — `EveryDeliverableSiteCarriesTheRule`, added after a mutation escaped. (4) *A test derives the site set and fails when any single citation is removed* — two derived signals, and `M7-hardcode-sites` (replacing the derivation with a fixed list) errors, which is what proves the sweep is real rather than decorative (INV-246). (5) *Cross-platform, language-agnostic* — prose plus a stdlib-only guard importing nothing from `plugins/`. **Two findings the spec did not have, both of which improved the fix.** ⚠️ **Phase B was destroying the baseline it needed:** it writes the loaded count into **`record_count`** — the *same field* Data collection uses for the count it measured in the collected file — so the reconciliation's baseline is the value the write overwrites. The shipped text therefore compares **first**, records the outcome as `load_count_matches_source` under the registry's own `validation_checks`, and on a mismatch **leaves the existing `record_count` in place**; overwriting on a mismatch destroys the input figure *and* files a partial load as a complete one, after which nothing downstream can tell the difference. ⚠️ **A fourth site exists and was already compliant:** `module-04-data-collection/SKILL.md` records `record_count`, `expected_record_count` and `record_count_matches_expected` "so the comparison stays auditable instead of living only in the turn that ran it" — INV-243's discipline, predating the invariant. Nothing was changed there but the citation, and **Phase B was pointed at that existing pattern rather than inventing a parallel one** (INV-003). **Mutation-tested: 7 mutations, 1 ESCAPED and was closed, all 7 caught after.** `M1-revert-phaseB` restores the pre-fix registry write and fails **7** tests. ⚠️ `M5-revert-phaseD` escaped because the first detector had only the registry signal (`record_count` + `data_sources.yaml` + a write verb) and Phase D writes into `docs/loading_strategy.md` instead — so Phase D sat outside the derived set entirely and criterion 3 was unguarded. A second derived signal (`per-source statistics`) closed it; two durable destinations need two signals, and the deliverable is the worse failure mode since nothing re-derives a number written into a document. ⚠️ **The detector was also narrowed after a false-positive pass:** a first version keyed on "record count" in prose and flagged seven blocks that are not INV-243 sites — `phase2-discover.md` uses the phrase for an *entity's* record count, Module 4 for a license limit — so the trigger is the **action**, not the vocabulary. A guard that fails on correct content is worse than one that misses; that caveat is the one INV-246 already carries. Full suite: **`2635 passed, 3 skipped, 2296 subtests`**; delta +11, exactly the tests added. **Deviations recorded** in the spec, covering all four points above. **Establishes no invariant** — this completes INV-243/INV-245's application; INV-246, minted an hour earlier in the same session, is the rule that makes the derived guard mandatory and is what this implementation was built to satisfy.

Baseline green — **2621 passed, 3 skipped, 2282 subtests, 0 failures**. **Three findings, all written as specs, two high-severity — and all three are defects in that same batch, i.e. in my own work from earlier today.** **(1) HIGH — INV-244 reaches 2 of the 3 sites it binds, and the one it misses is upstream of both.** `module-04-data-collection/SKILL.md:94` carries the identical `license_record_limit` absent-branch — *"**Absent or null** (no custom license detected yet): fall back to the built-in evaluation license"* — the exact inference INV-244 forbids. (1) *A bulleted recap renders and counts as referenced* — `test_an_all_bulleted_recap_embeds_all_of_them` and `test_tab_coverage_reports_zero_missing`, the latter asserting exit 0, the absence of "missing from the recap", **and** the positive `6 of 6 captured tabs` line, so it cannot pass by the check silently not running. (2) *`module-completion.md` states the image must be on its own line* — `test_module_completion_requires_the_image_on_its_own_line`, plus `test_the_inv161_path_warning_still_follows_it`, which pins **order**: the own-line rule must precede the INV-161 path rule at the same instruction, so the new text cannot displace the existing one. (3) *A fixture with both shapes embeds all of them* — `test_bulleted_and_unbulleted_images_all_reach_the_pdf` alternates the two shapes across six tabs; `test_every_markdown_list_marker_is_accepted` covers `-`, `*`, `+`, an indented marker and extra spacing. **The limit of the fix is asserted too**, because a change that swallowed every bullet would pass all of the above: an ordinary text bullet still renders as a bullet, and an image *inside* a sentence is not a block image. **Mutation-tested: 4 mutations, all 4 caught.** Reverting the regex to its anchored form — the original defect, reproduced exactly — fails **6** tests, which is the evidence that the guard catches the reported bug rather than merely describing it; restoring the renderer's duplicate copy also fails 6; dropping the end anchor fails the mid-line selectivity test; removing the own-line instruction fails the prose test. Both files were restored from `cp` backups and **md5-compared**, never `git restore`, which would have discarded the uncommitted fix. (2) *The two senses of "resolves to" are distinguished, Step 5a unchanged* — the clause names both questions and the **consequence** of reading Step 5a's sense here (zero countable fields, undefined score), which is what makes it load-bearing rather than a style note; Step 5a is asserted unchanged by its own text, including the `BUSINESS_NAME_ORG` example and the exact-string-match ⛔. (3) *The INV-174 exclusion survives, narrowed* — asserted with its reason and with the thing that must **not** be excluded. (4) *A worked example on a fully raw source* — two counting fields, one non-counting, and the resulting denominator stated (`= 2 … not 3, and not 0`), since an example that stops before the number leaves the same question open. (5) *The empty-denominator case is handled, and a test asserts no instruction permits 0/0 → 0%* — completeness is reported undefined and the source routed to "Needs enrichment", with the route's target asserted to actually exist in the phase. (6) *Formula, three bands, presence test and per-`RECORD_TYPE` rule asserted unchanged* — plus the duplicate-rate definition and INV-180. **Mutation-tested: 7 mutations, all 7 caught.** All files restored from `cp` backups and byte-compared. The shipped form states the requirement **positively** — wherever an empty denominator is named, "undefined" must be named with it. ⚠️ **Its control is an insertion, not an edit**, which is the point that hid the sweep's emptiness for three attempts: for a "no instruction permits X" sweep, deleting every mention passes *correctly*, so editing the block under test can never demonstrate the sweep works. Verified by inserting a permissive instruction into `phase2-data-mapping.md`, which it catches; the handling's existence is pinned by three separate tests that do fail on removal. Also recorded: the spec's quotation of Step 5a adds bold emphasis the file does not carry, and the assertion pins the file's actual text rather than changing Step 5a to match the quotation. **Establishes `INV-238`** — *a computed metric whose denominator can be empty MUST define that case and report it as undefined, never as zero; and where a gate's purpose is reproducibility between two guides, the membership rule MUST be stated positively and MUST NOT rest on a verb the same document uses in a narrower sense elsewhere.* ⚠️ **Minted under the maintainer's standing authorization while they were away, not their sign-off — pending review**, and flagged in the run report. ⚠️ **The spec's confidence note is worth the maintainer's eye:** it says that if a reviewer judges reading B obviously intended, a one-sentence clarification (or closing the spec) would have been the right outcome rather than this. What shipped is longer than one sentence because criteria 4 and 5 ask for a worked example and the empty-denominator route; if that is more than wanted, the surplus is the example and the ⛔, not the positive statement.

## single-page-capture-crops-to-the-viewport-and-calls-it-full-page

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-14
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/capture_screenshots.py` (single-page outcome tracking, `_single_page_label`, `_record_full_page`, `_measure_chrome_cli`, full-page paths in all four backends, the `_MAX_FULL_PAGE_PX` clamp), `specs/INVARIANTS.md` (INV-235 + its `Visualization and screenshots` index entry), `tests/test_capture_single_page.py` (extended: +14 tests, a stdlib PNG decoder, and the INV-235 back-citation), `tests/test_invariant_enforcer_citations.py` (pair count 46 → 47), `specs/IMPLEMENTED.md`.
- **MCP re-check:** n/a (no Senzing fact) — this is the plugin's own capture helper. Server version this session is **1.32.9** (`get_capabilities`, 2026-08-14).
- **Summary:** `--single` captured a fixed 1440×900 viewport and printed `Full page` for it, so a taller deliverable shipped its top third under a label asserting it showed all of it — and INV-123 designates that label as the caption's input, so a caller obeying INV-123 exactly reproduced the false claim. **Criterion walk: 6 of 6 implemented; 4 fully runtime-verified, and the 2 backend paths this environment cannot install are disclosed below rather than ticked.** (1) *A page taller than the viewport yields a PNG covering the whole page* — **runtime-verified on the Chrome CLI backend**: a 2671px page produced a 2758px PNG containing the footer (58 footer rows decoded at y=2613-2670, matching the live layout probe's `footerTop: 2613, footerBottom: 2671`). (2) *`Full page` only when it succeeded; a fallback prints a distinct label and warns with both heights* — three outcomes with three distinct labels, and the recorded **default is the shortfall**, so a backend that reports nothing cannot inherit the claim by silence. (3) *The tabbed path is unchanged — asserted, not assumed* — `_WINDOW` is still `(1440, 900)`, a tab capture is asserted not to be in single-page mode, a tab's label is asserted unaffected by the single-page outcome, and all **75** pre-existing capture tests (`test_capture_single_page`, `test_capture_tabs`, `test_capture_suppressed_tabs`) pass untouched. (4) *A documented clamp, reported in the label and on stderr* — **runtime-verified**: a 14428px page clamped to 12000, PNG 12087, stderr naming both heights, label `Full page (clamped at 12000px)`. (5) *A test renders a tall page and asserts the capture — negative-controlled by restoring the viewport-only capture* — **4 mutations, all caught**, file restored byte-identically from a `cp` backup. The named control (viewport-only) failed the new assertions while `test_single_produces_exactly_one_png`'s existence/magic-byte checks still passed, which is exactly the blind spot the spec identified. (6) *Cross-platform, no new dependency* — stdlib only (`zlib`/`struct` in the test, `urllib.request.url2pathname` in the helper, chosen over a hand-rolled path slice because it decodes `%20` and the Windows `/C:/…` form correctly, INV-001). ⚠️ **The spec's own verification recipe was insufficient, and this is the finding worth carrying forward.** Criterion 4 says "verify by height, not by existence"; implementing exactly that produced a **2671px PNG of a 2671px page with the footer still missing**, and a height assertion passes that build. Under `--headless=new`, `--window-size` includes window chrome, so the rendered viewport was 813px for a requested 900 and the last ~87px of the page never rendered. Caught by decoding the PNG's bottom rows (zero footer pixels) rather than trusting the dimensions — the INV-129 discipline applied to the fix's own output. The offset is now **measured at runtime**, not hard-coded, since it varies by browser version and platform; the mutation that removes it is caught **only** by the pixel assertion, which is the evidence that the height-only check is inadequate. ⚠️ **Initially recorded as not runtime-verified, then verified on maintainer follow-up the same day — and one of the two paths was BROKEN.** The original entry said Playwright and Selenium could not be exercised because neither library is installed, and reasoned that an unrecorded outcome degrades to the viewport-only label, "the safe direction for an unverified path". **That reasoning was wrong**, and the claim that only another machine could close the gap was an unchecked assumption: `pip` has network here, so both were installed into a throwaway venv and both code paths run against the same fixture. Results, against a 2704px page with a dark footer: **Chrome CLI** 2791px with 80 footer rows (pass); **Playwright** 2704px with 80 footer rows (pass — it sets the viewport directly and uses native `full_page=True`, so no window chrome is involved); **Selenium** 2565px with **zero** footer rows — it lost the bottom **139px**, the whole footer, while recording outcome `full` and printing the label `Full page`. That is a breach of the very invariant this spec establishes, and the "safe direction" argument did not protect it precisely because Selenium *did* record an outcome — it recorded the wrong one. Cause: `set_window_size` sizes the **outer window**, and the viewport is shorter by the window chrome — the same trap already fixed for the CLI path, left in place for Selenium on the assumption the two "agree closely enough" under `--headless=new`. **Fixed** by measuring `window.innerHeight` after sizing and adding the difference back, one correction pass since the offset is constant for the session; re-verified at **2704px with 80 footer rows**. The clamp and short-page branches were then exercised on all three backends too (13340px → 12000/12087px clamped with the warning and the clamped label on each). `wkhtmltoimage` remains unavailable and unverified; it renders content height by design and is exempt from the clamp, stated inline. **A guard was added**, `EveryWindowSizingBackendCorrectsForWindowChrome` — asserted against the **source**, because the suite is stdlib-only (INV-108) and may not import either library. That limitation is what hid this bug, so the guard pins the mechanism each window-sizing backend must carry, and is negative-controlled by reverting the correction. `wkhtmltoimage` renders content height by design and is exempt from the clamp, stated inline. Full suite: **2434 passed, 3 skipped, zero failures** (2420 before, delta +14 exactly the tests added). **Deviations recorded** in the spec: the deeper root cause above, the two unverified backends, and the `wkhtmltoimage` clamp exemption. **Establishes `INV-235`** — *a capture helper's printed label MUST describe what the capture achieved, never what its mode intended; a shortfall MUST be reported on stderr with both heights, and the "full page" wording MUST be unreachable except on an actual full-page capture, including by silence.* Its ⛔ additionally records that a guard for this must assert the page's last content is present in the **pixels**, not that the image is tall enough to hold it. ⚠️ **Split on maintainer review, 2026-08-14:** that verification rule was generalized to **`INV-241`** — *a guard for a rule about an artifact's content MUST assert that content, never a proxy for it (a dimension, a byte count, an exit status, a file's existence)* — and filed under *The development record itself*, because it governs how a **guard** verifies rather than anything the Bootcamper's guide reads, which also puts it correctly inside the group exempt from shipped-citation scoring. The ⛔ remains in INV-235 as the concrete case with a dated forward pointer; it is the clause that stops the next height-only assertion passing a broken build, so it earns its place at the point of use. ⚠️ **Minted under the maintainer's standing authorization while they were away, not their sign-off — this wording is pending review** and is flagged in the run report.
- **Commit:** 41c4c94

Baseline green — **2331 passed, 3 skipped, 2010 subtests, 0 failures** (the `test_citation_census` failure that stood through the batch cleared when INV-222 was registered in `4d26f28`). **Four findings, all written as specs, one high-severity.** **(1) HIGH — INV-229 reached two of the three files it binds, and the one it missed is the one the bootcamper sees.** Step 7 now diagnoses a results mismatch instead of failing the install; `phase2-report-close.md` Step 9 still records "Pass or fail status" per check, branches on "If ANY checks failed", and on that branch prints `SYSTEM VERIFICATION: FAILURES DETECTED … re-run system verification`, **skips Step 10's `VERIFY` purge** (`:79-81`, "do NOT proceed to cleanup"), and instructs the recap to "capture that all 8 checks passed" (`:125`) — so the exact failure INV-229 was written to prevent survives one step later, now also stranding the synthetic records in the database and putting a false claim in the keepsake. Root cause found: `implement-spec/SKILL.md:283-289` lists `invariants`, `affected` and `negatives` from `coverage_reports.py` and **not `shipped`** — the skill that mints an invariant checks whether a *test* cites it and never whether the *plugin* does. Compounded by the maintainer's queue-then-approve decision that run: the prose shipped while the IDs did not yet exist, and nothing sends the implementer back once they do. `aa013dc` fixed thirteen of these by hand the day before. Also in this class, from `conformance.py rules`: `visualization-api-reference.md:977`'s server-lifetime ⛔ is the plugin's **only** hard-rule line whose section cites nothing, while both its siblings cite (`:1000` INV-172, `:1025` INV-056) — and it is registered, as **INV-131**. **(3) MED — the detector that should have caught (2) can only see 1 of the 8.** `SHIPPED_ARTIFACT` (`coverage_reports.py:283-292`) matches paths, `module-NN` directories and `Module N` catalog labels, and **no module display name** — so INV-223 ("Truth Set visualization"), INV-225 ("System verification"), INV-227 ("Bootcamp preparation") and INV-229 ("System-verification checks") are all invisible, and INV-226 surfaced only because its text happens to say "Module 0". To get more: download_url serves up to 10000 records per request and needs only mcp.senzing.com allowed; source_download_url is the complete uncapped file but requires egress to raw.githubusercontent.com."* — with `download_url` on `mcp.senzing.com` and `source_download_url` on `raw.githubusercontent.com`, confirming the spec's central correction that `senzing.com` is the **wrong** host for the Truth Set. ⚠️ **New:** the `source='list'` response's `available_sources[].download_url` points at **`raw.githubusercontent.com`**, while the per-source response's `citation.download_url` points at **`mcp.senzing.com`** — the same field name, different hosts. Reading the field name instead of the URL is enough to strand a firewalled Bootcamper; that is now recorded in both modules.
- **Summary:** **Step 1.1 downloads the dataset and proves it downloaded the dataset.** **Criterion walk: all 6 hold; the two that describe a live fetch are not runtime-verified and say so.** (1) *159 records — 120/22/17 — not 15* — the step now names the preview as a preview, takes the URL from the response, and downloads; **not runtime-verified** (the fetch needs a live walk), but the counts it must reach were re-read from the server today. (2) *The step compares the written line count against the per-source `record_count` values and stops on a mismatch* — a ⛔, with the per-route expectation stated (`record_count` exactly from `source_download_url`; `min(record_count, download_url_max_records)` from `download_url`, the same rule Module 4 states) and an explicit "do not proceed to 1.2". This is the criterion that matters most: it converts **every** under-fetch — preview-only, rate-limited, truncated — into a visible error, which is why it is mandatory rather than advisory. (3) *The egress host is named per URL, from the response, and `senzing.com` is not asserted for the Truth Set* — both the correct host and the contradiction of Module 4's CORD-specific sentence. (4) *Module 4's egress sentence no longer states one host as a general rule* — it now says to read the host from the URL, keeps the CORD case that was right, and names the Truth Set counterexample that makes the rule necessary. (5) *Retries with backoff on 429 and never writes a non-JSON body into the file* — with the mechanism named, because the prohibition alone would not stop it: `curl -sS -o file` saves the 43-byte `Rate limit exceeded.` body like any other, since `-sS` only silences the progress meter and there is no `-f`; a safe form is given rather than only a ban. **Not runtime-verified** — provoking a 429 against the live endpoint was not attempted. (6) *Cross-platform, language-agnostic* — the fetch is described by behavior, with `curl` named only as the trap. **Proposal 4's hoisting was considered and not done** — Module 3b now cross-references Module 4's download contract and states only what it needs first; extracting a shared file would be a larger refactor than the defect warrants, and the spec offers it as a "consider". **⚠️ An existing guard rejected the first draft, correctly:** `tests/test_truthset_acquisition_call.py` (INV-136) requires any `get_sample_data` mention to sit beside its required parameter, because a bare call fails — my new sentence named the tool alone, and now reads `get_sample_data(dataset='truthset', source='<CODE>')`. Full suite: **2270 tests, 1 failure** — the pre-existing `test_citation_census.py::test_the_live_repo_verifies_clean`, unchanged either side. **Establishes `INV-228`** — *a step that writes a dataset obtained from the MCP server MUST verify the written record count against the count the server reported, per source, and MUST stop on a mismatch; egress hosts are named per URL from the response.* The same-field-name/different-host trap found during re-verification is recorded in the invariant too. **Approved by the maintainer on 2026-08-14** and recorded as **INV-228** in `specs/INVARIANTS.md`, indexed under *MCP sourcing and tool contracts*, with the bidirectional enforcer link asserted (`tests/test_truthset_download_is_the_dataset.py`).

## empty-progress-file-makes-resume-unsatisfiable

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-14
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/recap_checkpoint.py`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/bootcamp-onboarding/SKILL.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/commands/start-bootcamp.md`, `tests/test_resume_requires_a_recorded_module.py` (new), `specs/IMPLEMENTED.md` (this entry). ⚠️ **`plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/session-start.py` is predicted by the spec and deliberately unchanged** — proposal 4 says "no change needed once `bootcamp_active()` tightens, but confirm the no-fold branch's message still reads correctly", and it does: verified by running it in a scratch project, it now prints **nothing** for a contentless file and its resume message is byte-unchanged for a resumable one.
- **MCP re-check:** **n/a (no Senzing fact)** — the spec says so itself. Server version this session is **1.32.9** (`get_capabilities`, 2026-08-14).
- **Summary:** **The shared predicate now reads content, so the hooks stop announcing a resume that cannot happen.** The spec's preference was explicit — fix the predicate, not the four call sites, because the class is "existence stands in for content" — and that is what was done: `bootcamp_active()` returns `current_module() is not None`, which was **already computed and already unused**. **Criterion walk: all 6 hold, and all of them were executed.** (1) *`{}` → predicate false, `session-start.py` prints nothing* — verified as a subprocess in a scratch project. (2) *Same for empty, non-object, malformed, `null` and `""`, none raising* — **nine** contentless shapes tested (empty object, empty file, whitespace-only, JSON array, truncated JSON, `null`, `""`, blank string, other-keys-only); every one exits 0 and reads inactive, so the never-raises contract (INV-048) holds where it now matters more, since the predicate depends on it. (3) *A non-empty `current_module` still resumes with the message unchanged* — asserted on the message text, not just the exit code. (4) *Both prose sites state the three-way branch and that a contentless file means fresh rather than corrupt* — with the ⛔ that names the rule the defect broke: never announce a resume you cannot perform. (5) *A test covers `{}` and is negative-controlled by reverting to `isfile`* — 12 tests, **11 mutations all caught**, the first being exactly that revert. (6) *Cross-platform, stdlib only.* **The four callers were checked before tightening, since a shared predicate is a shared blast radius** — and none loses anything in the window: `session-end` and `precompact-recap` have no module recap to fold and no container to stop (containers start in SDK setup, well after the first write), and `checkpoint-tick`'s scaffold-only case is one it already skips. That reasoning is recorded in both the predicate's docstring and the test's, because the next reader's first question is what else `bootcamp_active()` gates. **A mechanism test pins the fix itself** — that the predicate delegates to `current_module()` and no longer calls `os.path.isfile(PROGRESS)` — so a revert is caught even if a caller is rewritten around it. Full suite: **2228 tests, 1 failure** — the pre-existing `test_citation_census.py::test_the_live_repo_verifies_clean`, unchanged either side. **Establishes `INV-227`** — *whether a bootcamp is in progress MUST be decided by whether the progress file records a module, never by whether the file exists; a contentless file is a fresh start, silently, and the predicate MUST NOT raise.* **Approved by the maintainer on 2026-08-14** and recorded as **INV-227** in `specs/INVARIANTS.md`, indexed under *Module flow, selection and progress*, with the bidirectional enforcer link asserted (`tests/test_resume_requires_a_recorded_module.py`).

## visualization-contract-and-reference-server-disagree-on-record-fields

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-14
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03b-truthset-visualization/visualization-api-reference.md`, `tests/test_visualization_api_contract.py` (new), `specs/IMPLEMENTED.md` (this entry).

That is `data_source` + `record_id` + matching info — exactly what the server returns.
- **Summary:** ⚠️ **`plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/senzing_viz_server.py` was predicted by the spec and is deliberately UNCHANGED** — that is the substance of this entry, not an omission: the server's payload construction was measured to be correct for the flags it uses, so changing it would have introduced the defect rather than fixed it. Its `/api/merges` and `/api/records` constructors are asserted, and its `Model.build` key literals are pinned, by the new test. **The contract now describes the response, and the direction was chosen by measurement rather than by preference.** ⚠️ **The spec's "Preferred" proposal rests on a false premise.** It says the reference server "already holds the record payloads it built the entity model from, so populating them is local work" — it does not, and cannot at the flags it uses. The server was correct; the contract was documenting data that was never in the response. Criterion 1 permits this direction in terms (*"or the contract no longer claims they do"*), and criteria 2–5 are direction-independent. **Criterion walk: all 6 hold.** (1) *Record fields reconciled* — the contract documents `data_source`, `record_id`, `match_key`, with the flag reason stated, dated, and measured. (2) *`/api/records` matches `/api/merges` records exactly* — already true in the code (both read one model), and now **required in words**: the same record *objects*, not merely the same field names, with a test asserting equality rather than key-set equality. (3) *`record_count` and `data_sources` documented* — an undocumented returned field is one a non-Python implementer omits, which is the whole failure mode. (4) *`match_key` has one home with its empty value explained* — the **record**, which is both what the server returns and the more informative placement (it is the key that pulled *that* record in); empty means the seed record joined nothing, to be rendered as such rather than as a blank field (INV-115). (5) *A repo-level test fails on any key present-but-undocumented or documented-but-absent, negative-controlled* — 19 tests, **14 mutations all caught**, including a dropped field, an added field, the two endpoints diverging, and each contract sentence removed. (6) *Cross-platform, language-agnostic, stdlib only, no `plugins/` import* (INV-108). **The spec's UX point was kept rather than discarded:** the enrichment route is documented (add the two flags; read `FEATURES[].FEAT_DESC` or `JSON_DATA`, confirmed against the server not the contract), marked optional, with the reason it is not the default — this payload is embedded in the standalone snapshot (INV-070) and Module 7 points the same app at the Bootcamper's whole dataset, so per-record features multiply the keepsake by the record count. Keeping the composite also matches the repo's existing position that DEFAULT composites are right for exploration (`tests/test_default_flags_production_caution.py`, INV-169). **⚠️ Criterion 5's method is a substitution, disclosed:** it asks for a test that *starts* the reference server, which needs a live engine and a loaded Truth Set — neither exists here — so the payload constructors are exercised against a hand-built `Model`. **That substitution has a hole, and a mutation found it rather than reasoning:** with a hand-built fixture, a key **added** inside `Model.build` is invisible to an exact-key-set assertion on the payload. The guard now also parses `build`'s entity and record dict literals and asserts their exact key sets — the only route to them without an engine, and flagged in the spec for replacement by a real request when one is available. Full suite: **2216 tests, 1 failure** — the pre-existing `test_citation_census.py::test_the_live_repo_verifies_clean`, unchanged either side. **Establishes no invariant.** **Deviation recorded** in the spec, covering the reversed direction and its two measurements, the `match_key` placement decision, and the test-method substitution.

## skipping-step-3-on-an-existing-install-skips-the-env-script

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-14
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-02-sdk-setup/SKILL.md`, `tests/test_sdk_setup_prerequisites.py` (new, shared with the sibling spec above), `specs/IMPLEMENTED.md` (this entry).
- **MCP re-check:** **confirmed, server 1.32.9, 2026-08-14.** `sdk_guide(topic='install', platform='linux_apt', language='python')` returns both variables under `install.platform.env_vars` — `PYTHONPATH` as "/opt/senzing/er/sdk/python (required for Python SDK — the senzing and senzing-core packages ship with senzingsdk-runtime here)" and `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` as "/opt/senzing/er/lib (only needed if native lib not found automatically)" — so the skip path has everything it needs to write the script without an install transcript. The server is not implicated in the defect; the step order was.
- **Summary:** **Step 3's two jobs are separated, and only the redundant one is skipped.** **Criterion walk: all 6 hold; criterion 1 is a composition check, and that is disclosed.** (1) *After SDK setup on a machine where Senzing was already installed, the env script exists with the values `sdk_guide` returns* — **not runtime-verified**: completing the module is a conversational walk, not a script. What is verified is that Step 1 now directs the environment work explicitly, that the required-stops list carries it, and that the values are required to come from `sdk_guide`. ⚠️ The *variable values themselves* were confirmed working on this machine while verifying the sibling spec: with `PYTHONPATH=/opt/senzing/er/sdk/python`, `senzing.__file__` resolved to `/opt/senzing/er/sdk/python/senzing/__init__.py` — the SDK-shipped package, ahead of the PyPI ones this machine also has — and the engine then constructed far enough to return `SENZ7220`. So the script the skip path will now write does the job it is being written for. (2) *The required-stops list names it as never skipped* — with the reason: it is "the single most likely thing an existing install is missing", and Step 3's title ("Install Senzing SDK") is what made the second job invisible to the skip instruction. (3) *Step 1's skip instruction names installation only* — "Skip the *installation* — Step 2, and Step 3's install commands… **Not Step 3 entirely**", followed by a positive instruction to do the environment work. (4) *One implementation, not two* — the skip path is required to use the same zsh/bash path-resolution idiom, fail-loudly root check and empty-value guard as the install path, and a test asserts the phrase, so the skip path cannot grow a second weaker copy. (5) *The Step 8 troubleshooting note handles the script being absent* — it now checks existence **first** and treats absence as the finding with the remedy, rather than asking whether an absent file was sourced; the original zsh `${BASH_SOURCE[0]}` finding is asserted to survive. (6) *Cross-platform* — the required stop names `senzing-env.sh` **and** `senzing-env.bat`, so the skip path produces the right artifact per platform. **The irony is stated in the plugin, not just the spec:** Step 1's filesystem fallback exists *because* the import check fails with `PYTHONPATH` unset on a working install — it predicts this exact state and then routed past the step that fixes it. A test pins that sentence, because it is the argument for the required stop. Verified by 22 assertions shared with the sibling spec, **negative-controlled with 14 mutations, all caught**. Full suite: **2173 tests, 1 failure** — the pre-existing `test_citation_census.py::test_the_live_repo_verifies_clean`, unchanged either side. **Establishes no invariant.** ⚠️ **Deviation from the spec's proposal 1:** it suggested making the env-script work "its own step (or an explicitly named sub-step, e.g. Step 3b)". It was instead left inside Step 3 and made a **required stop** that the skip instruction names positively. Renumbering a step in a module whose steps are cited by number from Step 1's routing, the required-stops list, the checkpoint vocabulary and two other specs would have been a wider change than the defect needs, and the criteria are all satisfiable without it — criterion 3 asks only that the skip instruction name installation only.

- **Summary:** **Header creation now has an owner, and the class of defect is closed rather than the two instances patched.** The spec's third proposal was preferred over its first two: a citation naming specific substeps is the hazard, so **Step 2a declares itself unconditional** at any module whose append finds no file, says explicitly that nothing else creates the header (naming Bootcamp preparation's INV-092 exemption, which is the false belief graduation had encoded), forbids a narrowing citation anywhere, and states the consequence — a placeholder on the certificate, discovered only at graduation. **Criterion walk: all 6 hold; criterion 1 is a composition check, criterion 5 is executed.** (1) *After a Core run reaches the end of Entity Resolution Concepts the recap carries all five preamble lines* — **not runtime-verified** (no live bootcamp here); what is verified is that Module 0 now cites Step 2 **in full**, states that it is the first module to append on a Core run so 2a applies, and names all five lines, while 2a's template still carries them. (2) *Module 0 no longer cites "(2b/2c)" and states 2a applies* — both asserted, plus **2d**, which the same citation had also dropped; it applies here like any other module, since the durability hooks keep an in-progress checkpoint for Module 0 too. Its Step 3 exemption (INV-078/INV-092) is asserted **unchanged**, because widening a citation is exactly where an unrelated exemption gets lost. (3) *Graduation no longer attributes the line to Bootcamp preparation, and handles its absence* — the provenance now reads "module-completion Step 2a, at the first module that appends a recap section", names which module that is on each path, says preparation writes no recap, and **writes the preamble when the line is missing** rather than amending a line that may not exist — noting the recovery, since a header written at graduation means a module skipped 2a. The "Both, not either" rule is asserted to survive. (4) *A test forbids a narrowed Step 2 citation anywhere* — a corpus scan over every skill file, not just the one that regressed, plus a named assertion for Module 0 so a rename cannot make the scan pass by finding nothing. It excludes Module 3's own unrelated "Step 2 (…)" and the prohibition's own quotation of the bad citation; **12 mutations, all caught**, the first being the reported defect restored verbatim. (5) *`generate_recap_pdf.py`'s "no bootcamper name found" warning does not fire* — **executed**: a recap built exactly to 2a plus one Module 0 section per 2b parses with `recap_certificate_name` = "Ada Lovelace" and `recap_missing_certificate_name` False, paired with a **header-less control** that does warn, so the pair is not vacuous; every preamble label is also asserted to survive the generator's own parser. (6) *Cross-platform, language-agnostic.* **⚠️ Two existing guards corrected the work, both worth recording.** `test_recap_pdf_images` (INV-162) rejected the phrase "silently skipping the amend" in `graduation/SKILL.md` — a phrase-level ban on claiming that missing images are skipped silently; my sentence was forbidding silence, not claiming it, but the reword ("passing over the amend without saying so") is better prose and the guard was right to be blunt. And loading `generate_recap_pdf.py` by file path failed at import until the module was registered in `sys.modules` first — it defines `@dataclass` types, and dataclasses resolves annotations through `sys.modules[cls.__module__]`; the existing `test_recap_tab_coverage.py` loader already did this, and the reason is now recorded in the new loader's docstring. Full suite: **2138 tests, 1 failure** — the pre-existing `test_citation_census.py::test_the_live_repo_verifies_clean`, unchanged either side. **Establishes `INV-226`** — *a step that updates a shared artifact MUST be reachable only through a citation that also covers the substep which creates it, or MUST name the step that owns creation; a citation naming specific substeps MUST NOT omit the creating one.* Its source is this spec, with `project-readme-is-updated-but-never-created` recorded as the second instance of the same shape. **Approved by the maintainer on 2026-08-14** and recorded as **INV-226** in `specs/INVARIANTS.md`, indexed under *Module flow, selection and progress*, with the bidirectional enforcer link asserted (`tests/test_recap_header_is_owned.py`).

## single-page-capture-instruction-produces-zero-images

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-14
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/capture_screenshots.py`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/bootcamp-onboarding/module-completion.md`, `tests/test_capture_single_page.py` (new), `specs/IMPLEMENTED.md` (this entry).

- **Summary:** **The helper now has the concept it was missing, and every path is runtime-verified against real headless Chrome.** **Criterion walk: all 6 hold, and 5 of them were executed rather than argued.** (1) *A single-page deliverable produces exactly one PNG* — `--single` writes `{name}.png` (no slug suffix), verified: a real 21,152-byte PNG with the magic bytes, and a manifest carrying one `captured` entry (`file: dq.png`, `label: Full page`, empty `failed`/`not_present`) so graduation's coverage check sees it rather than reporting itself skipped. (2) *The tabbed app's six-image capture is unchanged by the same invocation* — rendered the **real** visualization page from `senzing_viz_server.render_page` with a fetch shim and captured with no `--tabs`: six PNGs, same slugs, same labels. (3) *A tabbed app whose requested tabs are all misnamed still reports and skips* — exit 2, **zero** PNGs, `not_present` recording both tabs; the whole-page capture explicitly does not apply there, because it would put the default tab in a file named for a tab it does not show. (4) *The instruction and the helper agree* — `module-completion.md` prescribes `--single` with a copyable command, names the output file, and states **why** the old form failed (an omitted `--tabs` means all six, not none), so a reader cannot reinvent it. (5) *A repo-level test covers the single-page path, negative-controlled by restoring the old behavior* — `tests/test_capture_single_page.py`, 21 tests, **11 mutations all caught**, the first being exactly the spec's requested control. (6) *Cross-platform, language-agnostic* — no new dependency; the existing backend chain and `_is_local_target` guard are untouched. **Design choices, both the spec's stated preference:** `--single` was added rather than redefining `--tabs ""`, so **every existing invocation is unchanged** — and `--tabs all` was added as an explicit spelling of the default, since an omission that means "everything" is what made the old instruction plausible. The single-page id is deliberately **absent** from `TABS`, so `--tabs page` remains an unknown id and `--single` is the only route in; `--single` with `--tabs` is refused rather than one silently winning. **⚠️ Two mutations escaped on the first pass, and both were real gaps rather than bad mutations** — worth recording because each looked like a passing test. Deleting the `--single` branch entirely still passed everything: the safety net catches the same page and writes the same PNG, so the flag looked redundant while every single-page capture went back to failing six pre-flight checks and reporting six tabs the page was never going to have. And routing the single page through `_snapshot_copy` still passed: the injected activation script finds no tab, exhausts its retries, and the page renders anyway. The guard now pins that `--single` **skips the pre-flight** (no "is not present" on stderr, and not the safety-net message either) and **makes no activation copy** (asserted by making `_snapshot_copy` raise). Full suite: **2116 tests, 1 failure** — the pre-existing `test_citation_census.py::test_the_live_repo_verifies_clean`, unchanged either side. **Establishes no invariant.** INV-122 already governs skip-and-report and is preserved rather than extended; the new mode is a capability, not a rule.
