## statement-only-step-cannot-satisfy-one-question-per-turn

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-14
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/bootcamp-onboarding/ground-rules.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-01-business-problem/phase1-discovery.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03-system-verification/SKILL.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03-system-verification/phase1-verification.md`, `tests/test_non_yielding_steps.py` (new), `specs/IMPLEMENTED.md` (this entry).
- **MCP re-check:** **n/a (no Senzing fact)** — the spec says so itself. Server version this session is **1.32.9** (`get_capabilities`, 2026-08-14).
- **Summary:** **The plugin now has a name for a step that asks nothing, so its own gate-precedence rule is followable.** **Criterion walk: all 5 hold; criterion 4 is reasoned, not executed, and that is disclosed.** (1) *A non-yielding step is defined and shares a turn* — a new ⛔ in the 👉 protocol: no 👉 means it does not end a turn **and** does not get one of its own; present it with the next step that does ask and let that step's single 👉 end the turn for both. It states why this is not a violation of one-step-at-a-time, and the one-step rule itself now points back at the carve-out, because two rules in separate sections is how this became unfollowable. (2) *No assertion that Step 1 ends on a 👉* — both post-nudge sentences read "the next single 👉 question", and the first names Module 1's Step 1 as exactly the case, so it is not re-derived. (3) *Module 1's step 1 is marked, with a consistent checkpoint* — the heading carries `NON-YIELDING`, the body gives the reason (a turn ending there would end with zero 👉, which INV-005 forbids), and its checkpoint is folded into one write with Step 2's at the end of the shared turn. (4) *A "no" to the switch at Discover the Business Problem yields one turn with the reminder and exactly one 👉* — **this is the criterion that cannot be executed here**: it describes a live conversational walk, and no live bootcamp runs in this environment. What is verified is that every instruction the walk would follow now composes to that outcome, asserted end to end (the post-nudge sentence, step 1's marking, step 2's question still being present as the 👉 the shared turn ends on). Reported as *implemented, not runtime-verified*. (5) *Cross-platform, language-agnostic.* **⚠️ Three files beyond the spec's Affected-files list, and this is the substantive addition.** The spec's Root cause is mostly about `module-03-system-verification`, which contains **exactly one** 👉 in the whole module and whose own instructions therefore describe a mechanism it never provides — yet its Proposed change and Affected files name only the ground rules and Module 1. Naming the concept centrally does not repair a file that says "signal a stop by ending the turn on the single 👉 question" when it has none, so all three of the instructions the spec identifies were fixed in place: `SKILL.md` states the module has one question and that "one at a time" is about order and completeness rather than turns; `phase1-verification.md`'s header says every step in the phase is non-yielding; and agent rule 10's eleven immediate writes became **one write at the end of the turn**, with a partial-turn fallback the spec did not ask for — collapsing writes to the end of a turn loses everything if the turn dies, so a failed turn must still leave resume on the right step. **Also decoupled**: `ground-rules.md`'s "Progress and state" section now says a step boundary is not a turn boundary, since that is where the contradiction was read from. Verified by 20 assertions; **22 mutations across this spec and its README sibling, all caught**, including re-coupling the boundaries, dropping `step_history` entries, and reverting either post-nudge sentence. Full suite: **2095 tests, 1 failure** — the pre-existing `test_citation_census.py::test_the_live_repo_verifies_clean`, unchanged either side. **Establishes `INV-225`** — *a step with no 👉 question is non-yielding: it MUST share the turn of the next step that asks, MUST NOT end a turn, and its checkpoint MUST collapse into one write at the end of that shared turn.* **Approved by the maintainer on 2026-08-14** and recorded as **INV-225** in `specs/INVARIANTS.md`, indexed under *Questions, gates and bootcamper-facing conversation*, with the bidirectional enforcer link asserted (`tests/test_non_yielding_steps.py`). ⚠️ One CommonMark point worth recording: the first draft inserted an HTML comment mid-sentence inside a list item, which the repo's CommonMark hook rejected with the exact reason (a whitespace-only line splitting the item into two paragraphs); the note was moved to the end of the bullet instead.

- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/bootcamp-onboarding/ground-rules.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-01-business-problem/phase1-discovery.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-02-sdk-setup/SKILL.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-05-data-quality-mapping/phase1-quality-assessment.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-05-data-quality-mapping/phase2-data-mapping.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-06-data-processing/phaseA-build-loading.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-06-data-processing/phaseD-validation.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/graduation/SKILL.md`, `tests/test_mcp_freshness_vocabulary.py` (new), `tests/test_sdk_parameter_shapes.py` (a pinned literal), `specs/IMPLEMENTED.md` (this entry).
- **MCP re-check:** **confirmed, server 1.32.9, 2026-08-14.** The spec asserts no Senzing fact, but rewriting the sites surfaced one **shipped claim with no provenance stamp at all**, and it was re-verified live rather than re-worded around: `get_sample_data(dataset='london', source='GLOBALDATA')` returns a `FEATURES` array (with the raw source columns alongside it at the record root) and `get_sample_data(dataset='las-vegas', source='PPP_LOANS')` returns flat root attributes — `BUSINESS_NAME_ORG`, `RECORD_TYPE`, `BUSINESS_ADDR_*` — and no `FEATURES` array. The claim **holds**, and now carries its version and date. The 500-record cutover was re-read from `sdk_guide`'s own `record_count` contract on the same server and also holds.
- **Summary:** **Two rules, two names, defined once.** ⚠️ **Two commits carry this**: `516344f` is the spec's commit, and the `ground-rules.md` half landed a moment earlier inside `129b8ce` (the sibling language-gate spec touched the same file and was staged first). **Criterion walk: all 5 hold.** (1) *Both terms defined, and the relationship stated* — **presentation freshness ("this turn")** is the pre-response checklist, now explicitly tied to the attribution rule as its reason: a turn with no call has nothing to attribute, so it must not present Senzing specifics; **sourcing floor ("from the server, not from this file")** is a floor on *provenance*, not a ceiling on caching. A ⛔ states that a floor **never** relaxes freshness, with a tie-break — when they seem to conflict both apply and the stricter governs. The attribution rule at the other end of the file now points back at the definition instead of restating the turn requirement independently, which is how two vocabularies grew. (2) *`phase1-discovery.md` no longer permits an earlier turn's results* — "returned **on the turn the gallery is presented** — never from memory, and never from an earlier turn's results", with the reason named (the step's own MCP attribution line). (3) *No file uses "this session" as a freshness claim* — **twelve sites rewritten, three more than the spec listed** (`phaseA-build-loading.md:136`, `module-02-sdk-setup/SKILL.md:631`, `graduation/SKILL.md:756` were missing from its inventory; criterion 3 is absolute, so the list was not the authority). Eight are sourcing floors and use the defined term. **Four turned out to be a third category the spec did not name**: provenance claims about facts already written into the file ("Verified this session: …"). In a shipped file "this session" means *the authoring session*, which tells a reader nothing — so those now carry a server version and date instead, and the one with **no stamp at all** was re-verified live (above). (4) *A test fails on a new freshness phrasing, negative-controlled by restoring the `phase1-discovery` wording* — `tests/test_mcp_freshness_vocabulary.py`, 11 tests, **8 mutations all caught**, the first being that exact restoration. The scan pairs "this session" with MCP vocabulary in the same sentence and allowlists the four ordinary-sense uses (ask-once scope, what to review at graduation, when a platform was detected) **by exact wording**, with a test that every allowlisted phrase still exists — so a stale entry fails rather than quietly covering new text. ## source-encoding-collides-past-twenty-four-sources

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-14
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/brand_tokens.py`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/senzing_viz_server.py`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03b-truthset-visualization/visualization-api-reference.md`, `tests/test_brand_sync.py`, `tests/test_source_encoding_renders_distinctly.py` (new), `specs/IMPLEMENTED.md` (this entry).
- **MCP re-check:** **n/a (no Senzing fact).** Entirely local rendering behavior, as the spec states. Server version this session is **1.32.9** (`get_capabilities`, 2026-08-14).
- **Summary:** **The encoding space is now counted as rendered, and the guard checks the canvas rather than a model of it.** The defect reproduced exactly as reported: at 25 sources the pre-fix code drew `SRC_006` and `SRC_024` identically as `('#8b5cf6', '#18160F', 1.5)`, and drew **24** distinct appearances at 25, 60, 64 and 210 sources alike, while the returned map stayed collision-free at every size because each entry carried a distinct `cycle` — which never reaches the canvas. **Criterion walk: all 6 hold, and the central claim is verified in a browser, not only in Python.** (1) *n distinct rendered keys for every n from 2 to ≥64* — the space widens along two further channels (stroke width, then a deterministic lightness perturbation of the fill), giving `SOURCE_ENCODING_CAPACITY` = **210** = 6 fills × 7 rendered stroke states × 5 fill-lightness steps; measured distinct/total is 25/25, 60/60, 64/64, 210/210, with the first collision at **211**. (2) *The guard tests past capacity and computes the rendered key* — `test_every_size_up_to_capacity_stays_distinct_as_rendered` walks 2, 6, 7, 24, 25, 42, 64 and 210 using `(fill, stroke when a width is set, width)`, the same expression the served JS uses; the old `len(FALLBACK_COLORS) + 3` = 9 with `(fill, stroke)` is replaced, and the small-n test the spec asked to keep is kept. (3) *Negative-controlled, naming the colliding sources* — **9 mutations, all caught**; on failure the message reads `n=64: 22 collision(s) as RENDERED — SRC_0000 == SRC_0042 as ('#8b5cf6', None, None); …`. (4) *Determinism, `SIGNAL_GREEN`, and Truth Set fills* — `test_assignment_is_deterministic` still passes, `SIGNAL_GREEN` appears in no assigned fill at capacity (verified across all 30 distinct fills, and a mutation putting it in the palette is caught), and the three Truth Set codes keep their preferred assignment. (5) *Legend and node agree above 24 sources* — both derive from `srcStrokeW`, one expression, asserted textually **and** in the browser. (6) *Cross-platform, language-agnostic* — the rule is stated in `visualization-api-reference.md` → "Data-source colors", which is what every non-Python server is built from (INV-090), including the instruction to define the rendered key, to derive swatch and mark from one expression, and to state a capacity rather than collide silently; the Python reference is cited as an implementation, not as the rule. **⚠️ A property worth recording: rendering is byte-identical to the pre-fix behavior for n = 2..24**, verified by re-deriving the old appearance and comparing (`test_the_rendered_appearance_is_unchanged_where_it_was_already_correct`). The old encoding was correct at that scale, and every realistic bootcamp lives there — the largest CORD dataset has 11 sources — so widening the space must not recolor existing graphs. A mutation that shifts one stroke slot is caught. **Runtime-verified in a real browser:** `tests/test_source_encoding_renders_distinctly.py` renders a 50-source model in headless Chrome (`/usr/bin/google-chrome`) and reads the drawn `<circle>` attributes and the legend dots' computed `box-shadow`: 50 distinct drawn appearances, 50 distinct swatches, both stroke widths present, the bare no-stroke state present, more than six drawn fills (so the shading channel genuinely renders), and equal appearance counts across graph and legend. 50 rather than 30 is deliberate — shading first appears at source 42, and a 30-source render left that channel asserted only in Python, which is the exact gap this file exists to close. The seven pre-existing Chrome-driven tests in `test_viz_tab_consolidation.py` also pass, so the changed JS executes. **⚠️ One vacuity found and fixed while here:** `test_viz_server_inline_fallback_matches_the_token_helper` compared `brand_tokens.color_for_sources` **to itself** — the inline fallback is only bound when the import fails, and it never fails under test — so a mutation gutting the inline copy's encoding space escaped every assertion. It now loads the server with `brand_tokens` blocked, asserts the two functions are not the same object, and compares them at 7, 25, 60 and 210 sources. Full suite: **2022 tests, 1 failure** — the pre-existing `test_citation_census.py::test_the_live_repo_verifies_clean`, unchanged either side. **Establishes no invariant, and `specs/INVARIANTS.md` is deliberately unchanged.** The spec listed it as an affected file *"only if a capacity ceiling is accepted rather than removed"* — that condition is not met. Option 4 (accept a ceiling and record it in INV-127 with the number) would have been a meaning change to a registered invariant, which needs the maintainer's sign-off; the widening route needs no invariant edit, so that is the one taken, and INV-127 stands exactly as written. **Deviation recorded** in the spec: the fix widens the space rather than accepting a ceiling, for that reason, and the capacity is a stated constant with a warning rather than a silent limit.

## visualization-server-teardown-does-not-record-a-pid

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-14
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03b-truthset-visualization/visualization-api-reference.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03b-truthset-visualization/phase1-visualization.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03b-truthset-visualization/phase2-close.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-07-query-visualize-discover/phase1-query-visualize.md`, `tests/test_viz_server_process_handle.py` (new), `tests/test_viz_tab_consolidation.py` (anchor), `specs/IMPLEMENTED.md` (this entry).
- **MCP re-check:** **n/a (no Senzing fact).** The spec asserts nothing about Senzing — it is about process lifetime in the modules that start a visualization server. Server version this session is **1.32.9** (`get_capabilities`, 2026-08-14), recorded because the session's other work cites it.
- **Summary:** **The server now has a handle, and the handle is the pid.** The rule is stated once, in `visualization-api-reference.md` → "Server lifetime" → a new **"Identifying the server process (required)"** subsection, because that file is what every non-Python bootcamp builds from (INV-090) and a rule living only in the Python module is a rule four of five languages never receive. Both modules that start a server then point at it. **Criterion walk: all 5 hold, and the mechanism is runtime-verified.** (1) *Phase 1 2.3 records the pid beside the port* — the start command backgrounds with `&` and captures `VIZ_PID=$!`, and the checkpoint is now `"web_service": {"status": …, "port": <port>, "pid": <pid>}`. (2) *Step 4.3 terminates by pid with a documented port fallback* — it names the field it reads (`truthset_visualization.checks.web_service.pid`) and falls back to `lsof -ti:<port>` / `Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort <port>` when a resumed session has no pid; the fallback is by **port**, never by name, since the port is bound by exactly the process serving it. (3) *`pkill -f <script>` is named unsafe with its reason* — the ban carries the mechanism, which is the load-bearing half: the pattern appears in the matching command's own command line, so the kill signals the caller, and the failure presents as the *next* step crashing. (4) *Termination is confirmed by the port being free, before the purge* — the fixed 5-second wait became a poll whose exit condition is the port, with an explicit ⛔ that step 4 does not start until it is confirmed free or the bootcamper has been warned; a sleep asserts nothing, and the purge is irreversible. (5) *Cross-platform and language-agnostic* — both handles are named (`$!`; PowerShell `Start-Process … -PassThru` → `$proc.Id`) and both port lookups, and the section states the rule as behavior with no dependence on the reference server's filename outside the prohibition, where it is the recorded evidence. **Runtime-verified, not merely written:** backgrounding a real HTTP server gave pid 1769793 from `$!`, `lsof -ti:8099` returned **the same pid** (so the fallback and the handle agree), the kill succeeded, and the port-free poll exited on its first iteration. The hazard reproduced too — `bash -c 'pgrep -af senzing_viz_server.py'` matched **the invoking shell** (`/bin/bash -c … pgrep -af senzing_viz_server.py …`) with nothing of that name running at all; `pkill` in place of `pgrep` is exactly the reported exit-144 kill. **Guard:** `tests/test_viz_server_process_handle.py`, 17 tests, **negative-controlled with 9 mutations, all caught** — dropping the pid from either checkpoint, dropping the `$!` capture, dropping the PowerShell handle, replacing the ban's mechanism with a bare "it is unsafe", turning the port check back into a sleep, reverting Step 4.3 to signaling an unnamed process, dropping the purge's port precondition, and removing module 7's rule. Each was restored from a byte-compared `cp` backup, never `git restore`, which would have discarded the uncommitted fix. It also sweeps **every** shipped instruction file so a ban in one place cannot be undone by a recipe in another: any `pkill` mention must sit inside a prohibition. **One existing guard changed**: `test_viz_tab_consolidation.py`'s teardown-ordering list pinned the literal `3. **Terminate the web service:**`, and the heading now continues "— by process id, per …"; the anchor was trimmed to the step name, since that test pins order rather than punctuation. Full suite: **1993 tests, 1 failure** — the pre-existing `test_citation_census.py::test_the_live_repo_verifies_clean`, red on `main` before this work (baseline: `Ran 1976 tests`, `FAILED (failures=1, skipped=3)`) because the still-unimplemented spec `senzing-python-sdk-must-not-be-pip-installed.md` proposes an INV id that is not minted yet. Same single failure either side; delta is +17 passed, exactly the tests added. **Establishes `INV-223`** — *a module that starts a background server MUST capture its process id at launch and record it beside its port, MUST terminate by that pid (or by a port lookup), and MUST confirm the port is free before any subsequent step; identifying the server by a command-line match is forbidden.* **Approved by the maintainer on 2026-08-14** and recorded as **INV-223** in `specs/INVARIANTS.md`, indexed under *Visualization and screenshots*, with the bidirectional enforcer link asserted (`tests/test_viz_server_process_handle.py`).
- **Commit:** cae1339

## phase3-analysis-start-point-2026-08-14

**Not a spec** — a dated record of a maintainer-requested change to a maintainer tool, at the
maintainer's request. Follows the `concision-pass-2026-08-13` precedent. ⚠️ **No shipped file
changed**; `.claude/` is not propagated to the public repo, so nothing here reaches a bootcamper.

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-14
- **Files changed:** `.claude/skills/dry-run/phase3-conversational.md`, `.claude/skills/dry-run/SKILL.md`, `specs/IMPLEMENTED.md` (this entry).
- **MCP re-check:** **n/a (no Senzing fact).** The change governs when phase 3 asks a question and what it does before the answer; it asserts nothing about the Senzing MCP server.
- **Summary:** **Phase 3 now asks where the *analysis* starts, and fast-forwards to it.** The maintainer reported the failure directly: *"I can never get to the end of Bootcamp in a dry-run because the context fills up with the analysis."* The file's own coverage-limits section already conceded the consequence — "Anything past the SDK … the loads, the live visualization server, and graduation's deliverables are out of reach" — and its Setup section prescribed the cause, stopping every walk at **Onboarding preface → Bootcamp preparation → Module 0 → Module 1**. So the later modules were not merely unwalked, they were unwalkable: the analysis, not the bootcamp, is what consumes the window, and a run that analyzes from the first turn exhausts it before reaching module four of eleven. **The change:** a new `## Where the analysis starts` section, placed before Setup because it must run before scaffolding, requiring phase 3 to present the eleven modules in order and ask for one — sourced from the module table in `bootcamp-preparation/SKILL.md` with an instruction to read that table rather than the local copy, which is marked as a convenience that can go stale. The walk then splits in two. The **fast-forward stretch** (everything before the chosen module) produces bootcamp output only: follow the skill files as written — it is what puts the project into the state the chosen module reads, so improvising through it invalidates the analysis that follows — with no test-notes blocks, no invariant lookups, no pinned-wording comparisons, no specs, and no narration of the fast-forward itself. The **analysis stretch** switches the whole rest of the file back on at the chosen module, announced in one line so the maintainer knows which channel they are reading. ⛔ **The no-fabrication rule is explicitly not relaxed by the fast-forward** — it is stated inside the new section, not left to the reader to carry down from "Why this cannot be self-played", because a stretch described as "run the bootcamp normally with the notes off" is exactly where a reader would infer permission to supply the answers too. **One exception to "no analysis": a blocker** (unsatisfiable instruction, missing file, failed tool call) still gets its spec written immediately, since that is the walk failing rather than an observation. **Three consequences handled rather than left implicit:** (1) the module list is presented **marked with the environment's ceiling** — from SDK setup onward the fast-forward needs a real install, database and license, so a choice past what `Before you start` step 3 found is still the maintainer's to make but not one they make blind; (2) `--seeded` becomes the default fixture when the analysis starts past Bootcamp preparation, because the `--fresh`/`--seeded` pair differs only in what preparation does and `--seeded` is the shorter fast-forward — with an instruction to report that the INV-133 pair went unrun and is still owed; (3) **fast-forwarded modules are named as a coverage limit**, since *walked* is not *tested* and a report of Data-processing findings that omits the seven modules before it reads as a full-bootcamp walk. `Stopping` now requires naming **both ends** of the analysis, which is also the only memory the start-point rotation has — nothing in the repo records the previous run's choice. ⚠️ **Numbering the maintainer-facing list is deliberate and annotated as such**, so a future INV-079 sweep does not "fix" it: INV-079 governs what the *Bootcamper* reads. **Verification:** full suite run, 1972 passed / 3 skipped / 1713 subtests. The single failure, `test_citation_census.py::test_the_live_repo_verifies_clean`, is pre-existing and unrelated — the untracked spec `senzing-python-sdk-must-not-be-pip-installed.md:138` proposes an invariant id that is not registered yet, and the id is deliberately not repeated here: writing it out would make this entry a *second* citation of an undefined invariant, which is the hazard `tests/test_spec_ledger_invariants.py::TestTheLedgerIsVerifiedAfterItIsWritten` exists to describe. (It did exactly that on the first draft of this entry, taking the census from 1 dangling reference to 2.) **Establishes no invariant.** ⚠️ **If the start-point question is ever to be gated rather than instructed, that needs an invariant and the maintainer's sign-off** — this is a maintainer-tool workflow rule, and reading one in unasked is the over-reach `production-readiness-audit` warns against.
- **Commit:** f6ed0ce

## concision-pass-2026-08-13

**Not a spec** — a dated record of the concision pass, at the maintainer's request. Follows the
`deep-dive-audit-*` precedent. ⚠️ Concision is **not** an invariant (INV-003 says consistent,
coherent, complete); it is audited because the maintainer asks for it.

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-13
- **Files changed:** `specs/anti-rationalization-clause-lives-in-four-modules-and-no-contract.md` (new spec, unimplemented by design), `specs/IMPLEMENTED.md` (this entry). **No shipped file changed** — the pass produced a finding, and shipped conversational text is not something to edit on a static pass (see below).
- **MCP re-check:** **n/a (no Senzing fact).** The pass measured this repo's own prose; no MCP tool was called.
- **Summary:** **Measured, then hunted drift rather than length. One real finding; nothing cut.** Baseline: **42 shipped markdown files, 129,607 words**, heaviest `module-02-sdk-setup/SKILL.md` (11,739) and `graduation/SKILL.md` (11,376); `conformance.py duplication` reports **131 verbatim repeats across 92 file pairs**. ⛔ **No word count was reduced and no rationale was touched** — the sanctioned direction is merging duplicated statements and moving a rule to where it is used, never deleting why (`deep-dive-audit-2026-07-28b`: a corrected example with its reason stripped got "helpfully" corrected back). **Method:** verbatim duplication is structurally blind to the defect that matters — the same rule stated in two places that no longer agree — so the near-duplicate scan from `production-readiness-audit-2026-08-12` was rebuilt (1,550 passages ≥22 words, cross-file pairs at 0.82–0.965 similarity, 39 hits, ranked by whether the delta contains a number or an ID). The top band proved to be legitimate per-step restatement (INV-183) differing only by relative path (`ground-rules.md` vs `../bootcamp-onboarding/ground-rules.md`); **the drift lives in the middle band**, which is where the 2026-08-12 port defect was also found (0.894). **The finding, written up as `anti-rationalization-clause-lives-in-four-modules-and-no-contract`:** the clause stating that a 👉 step has absolute precedence and that **the guide's own internal reasoning may not override it** appears in **4 of 9** module `SKILL.md` files, in **three phrasings** (module-02 "or token-budget concern", module-03 and module-03b "session length, context", module-05 "can override it"), and is **absent from `ground-rules.md`**, whose only "absolute precedence" is the MCP-first invariant at `:92` — a different subject. So five modules never state it. Corroborating, weaker: the `current_step` resume instruction is in 6 of 10 module skills and phrased differently again in module-02. The proposed fix **reduces** total words while **increasing** coverage — one contract statement plus four short citations replacing four divergent copies — and explicitly forbids copy-pasting the clause into the five silent modules or deleting any module's local hazard clause. ⚠️ **Not fixed inline, deliberately:** it is shipped conversational text whose behavioral half is INV-005–INV-009, which only `dry-run` phase 3 can exercise, and the audit discipline is report-before-change. ⚠️ **Method note, third instance today:** the first per-module table this pass produced was **wrong** — a `grep … | head -1` for one phrasing reported module-02 as lacking the clause and module-03/03b as having a weaker form, when all three carry it in different words. Corrected by grepping the distinctive phrase instead of the sentence frame. Hasty greps against this corpus have now produced a wrong table three times in one day; each was caught by re-reading, none reached a spec. **Establishes no invariant.** ⚠️ **If concision defects are ever to be gated rather than audited on request, that needs an invariant and the maintainer's sign-off** — INV-003's "consistent, coherent, complete" does not cover it, and reading one in would be exactly the over-reach `production-readiness-audit` warns against.
- **Commit:** 0315af4

## production-readiness-audit-2026-08-13b

**Not a spec** — the two follow-ups from `production-readiness-audit-2026-08-13`, actioned at the
maintainer's direction. Follows the `production-readiness-audit-2026-08-11b` precedent.

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-13
- **Files changed:** `tests/test_dated_negatives_are_marked.py` (a `_diagnose_malformed()` helper plus 2 new tests; the malformed assertion now carries a per-row diagnosis), `.claude/skills/dry-run/coverage_reports.py` (`find_malformed_negatives` docstring and the `negatives` report header — **strings only, no logic changed**), `specs/no-report-for-invariants-the-shipped-plugin-never-cites.md` (new spec, unimplemented by design), `specs/IMPLEMENTED.md` (this entry).
- **MCP re-check:** **n/a (no Senzing fact).** Both items concern this repo's own tooling and reference graph. No MCP tool was called; server 1.32.9 was established earlier this session for the globalization work.
- **Summary:** **Thread 1 — fixed, and it was smaller than the audit claimed.** The audit reported that nothing enforced the single-line `MCP-NEGATIVE` marker format and floated an invariant. ⚠️ **That was wrong, and the correction is the useful part:** wrapping a live marker and running `tests/test_dated_negatives_are_marked` turns the suite **red**, so a marker cannot silently fall off the re-ask worklist. Nothing was unguarded and no invariant was needed. What was actually broken was the *diagnosis*: the malformed assertion read "almost always a missing `owner:` clause", which is what sent me to the wrong field for two markers whose clauses were present and correct — a wrapped marker fails identically because `MCP_NEGATIVE` is not `re.DOTALL`. The assertion now calls `_diagnose_malformed()`, which classifies each row from the offending line: no `owner:` on the line → missing clause **or** a wrap, with the one-line requirement and the DOTALL reason stated; clause present but no `server` tail → a wrap; all fields present → order/separator error. Two new tests pin it — a scratch-tree wrapped marker must be reported malformed, must **not** count as live, and its diagnosis must name both "ONE line" and "re.DOTALL"; and a second asserts the three causes produce *different* text, since one message for all three would be no better than the guess it replaced. The report's own header and the helper's docstring carried the same misdirection and now name both causes. **Suite 1954 → 1956, `OK (skipped=3)`** — verdict line read, not the count. **Thread 2 — specced, not built,** as `specs/no-report-for-invariants-the-shipped-plugin-never-cites.md`. There is no report for invariants the shipped plugin never cites: `coverage_reports.py invariants` covers `tests/`, and `conformance.py rules` is satisfied by *any* `INV-NNN` in a section, which is precisely why it reported **0** while INV-212 went unnamed at its own originating step. Measured today at 220 defined: **148** cited under `plugins/`, **72** not, **39** cited by neither `plugins/` nor `tests/`, and **35** in the actionable slice (INV-150+, not self-declared superseded). The spec's real content is the **exemption rule**, because roughly nine of those 35 — INV-182, INV-191, INV-207, INV-209, INV-213, INV-216, INV-217, INV-219 among them — govern specs, the ledger and markers and *should* never appear in `plugins/`; a report that flags them trains the reader to skip it. Three options are laid out (reuse the index's "The development record itself" group, re-file the two misgrouped IDs, or annotate each exempt invariant), with the note that the index is **not** a clean partition today. Left for the maintainer to choose rather than decided here. **Establishes no invariant.** Thread 1 needed none once the enforcement gap turned out not to exist; thread 2 proposes none, and says so in its `## Affected files`.

- **Summary:** ⚠️ **Criteria 1 and 2 are NOT met as written, and the spec is recorded as implemented only because what shipped is the honest version of it — read the deviation before trusting this heading.** **Criterion walk, 8 items: 6 hold, 2 deviated.** (1) ⛔ *"A test asserts that every line … carries a marker"* — **deviated to a report.** Building the detector and measuring it showed the population is **6, not the 4 the spec assumed**: the four marked earlier that day were the ones a sweep happened to read, and `:316`, `:728`, `:748`, `:802` and `phase1-verification.md:206` were never seen. A gating test could not go green without marking six unverified claims or excluding them silently, so the mechanism landed as `coverage_reports.py unmarked` — read-only, exit 0, judgment required, same shape and stated reason as `invariants` and `affected`. **The gate is unbuilt and not claimed.** Maintainer chose this from three options. (2) *The four marked claims pass, negative-controlled* — **partly**: they are correctly not reported (a marker within the window covers them, pinned by `test_the_same_claim_with_a_marker_is_not_reported`), but there is no gate for a mutation to fail, so the control is on the *detector* instead — 5 mutations, all caught, each verified to land: re-adding bare `never` (1 failure), dropping the date requirement (4), disabling per-bullet units (1), ignoring nearby markers (1), opening the scan beyond `plugins/` (45). (3) *INV-192's "empty by design" must not trigger* — **holds, and is now pinned** by `test_an_undated_absence_is_not_reported`; it was the constraint that produced the date discriminator. (4) *Marker grammar imported, not restated* — `find_unmarked_negatives` uses this module's own `MCP_NEGATIVE`/`NEGATIVE_OPT_OUT`; the tool list is defined here because this script is the dependency, not the dependent (`tests/test_declined_ledger.py` imports *from* it). (5) *`quoted-history` honored* — `test_quoted_history_is_exempt`. (6) *Docstring discloses the phrase-list limit* — the `unmarked` docstring and the report header both say a miss is weak evidence and name the marker as the durable route. (7) *Stdlib-only, no `plugins/` import, exit 0* — `argparse`/`os`/`re`/`sys`; `test_it_runs_from_an_unrelated_directory_and_exits_zero`. (8) *Cross-platform, language-agnostic* — `os.path.join`, `pathlib` in tests. **Two design decisions the spec got wrong, corrected by measurement and pinned:** line-level detection cannot work (a claim's tool and date sit on different comment lines in a fence), and per-bullet granularity is load-bearing (a contiguous bullet list read whole produced a false positive on `ground-rules.md`, where tool, absence and date sat in three different bullets — the same correction `test_declined_ledger.py` needed). Vocabulary tuning measured **23 → 8 → 6**. **Suite 1914 → 1926, `OK (skipped=3)`.**
- **Establishes no invariant.** INV-209 already defines the marker, INV-217 covers `DECLINED.md`, INV-108 keeps the suite offline and INV-080 governs provenance; this adds a report that finds what those leave unswept. The candidate rule — *a dated tool-absence claim in shipped prose MUST carry a marker* — is deliberately **not** minted, because the repo does not yet satisfy it: six sites would violate it on the day it was recorded, and registering a rule the plugin breaks is worse than none. It becomes proposable once `unmarked` reads zero.

(1) *Step 10a's reassurance precedes its question* — moved above, with a line explaining that it is what makes "**4. Not sure yet**" a comfortable answer rather than a guess; `*(Internal: end the turn and wait.)*` remains the last line. (2) *ground-rules states the rule generally with the reason* — a ⛔ bullet immediately after the "exactly one 👉 ends each yielding turn" bullet it derives from, carrying the mechanical reason (nothing may follow the 👉) **and** an explicit carve-out that numbered choices, internal directives, and answer-*handling* instructions are not "after".   ⚠️ **The spec predicted one other instance and there were two — the guard found the one both the walk and my hand survey missed.** Before writing the test I surveyed for speech cues after a 👉 and found five hits, three of them legitimate answer handling and one genuine (`visualization-api-reference.md`). The guard then failed on a **third** site, `phase2-close.md` Step 4, which my survey had missed because its sentence begins "State" rather than any cue word I had listed. Both new sites are **teardown consent gates in front of an irreversible purge**, and both files' own next sentence reads "A yes given without that is not an informed yes" — so these are worse than the Step 10a instance that motivated the spec, and neither was reachable by the phase-3 walk, which stopped before Module 3b. **A hand survey with a cue list is a weaker instrument than a scan for the self-contradicting shape**, and this is the evidence.
  **Guard design, deliberately narrow.** A blanket "no prose after a 👉" is not viable in these files: they are written *for the guide*, so answer-handling instructions legitimately and frequently follow a question — the survey measured three such lines against two defects. It is backed by two non-vacuity tests (the detector fires on the historical arrangement; it ignores answer handling) plus positional assertions on all three fixed sites and on Bootcamp preparation Step 3, kept as the reference example of the pattern done right.

Re-run removing both phrasings: caught. Second, the land-check helper reports absence as `landed: False` for *removal* mutations, which reads backwards; M3 showed `landed: False` while having landed correctly. Both are the same underlying discipline as the previous spec's false miss — **a mutation must be verified to land, and the verification must be right way round.**
  **Predicted-but-unchanged, deliberately:** the spec listed `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/bootcamp-preparation/SKILL.md` as an *optional tidy* — Step 3 "can cite the general rule rather than restating its reasoning". Declined, and it would have been a regression. Step 3's restatement is exactly the pattern **INV-183** protects: a rule deliberately restated at the step it governs, because a rule reachable only through another file does not reach the reader who needs it. Step 3 is also the one site that had this right all along, which is why the guard pins it as the **reference example** — thinning it to a cross-reference would weaken the example and remove the reasoning from the place a guide is actually standing when it matters. Generalizing the rule in `ground-rules.md` adds a home for it; it does not make the local statement redundant.
- **Establishes `INV-211`** — *anything presented in order to inform an answer precedes its 👉, in the skill files as well as the output; an instruction saying to act "before they answer" while sitting below the question is unfollowable and must be moved, not reinterpreted.* Registered beneath the append marker, indexed under **Questions, gates and bootcamper-facing conversation**, with the bidirectional enforcer citation written before the guard asked.

## viz-server-settings-precedence-and-validation

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-13
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/senzing_viz_server.py` (module docstring's settings section rewritten; new `REQUIRED_PIPELINE_KEYS`, `_pipeline_gaps()`, `resolve_settings()`; `main()`'s eight-line resolution replaced by a call to it), `tests/test_viz_settings_resolution.py` (new, 12 tests), `tests/test_invariant_enforcer_citations.py` (`EXPECTED_PAIRS` 27 → 28), `specs/INVARIANTS.md` (INV-210), `specs/viz-server-settings-precedence-and-validation.md` (one criterion refined, see below), `specs/IMPLEMENTED.md` (this entry)
- **MCP re-check:** server **1.32.9, 2026-08-13** — the spec's central Senzing claim **re-confirmed, and by a better route than the spec used**. `explain_error_code('7426')` now leads with "SUPPORTPATH points at a directory with no transliteration modules … This is a configuration error, NOT a broken install" and its first resolution step is "Check SUPPORTPATH FIRST". The spec had cited `sdk_guide(topic='install', platform='macos_arm')`'s gotcha; the error-code tool owns the fact and states it more directly, which strengthens rather than weakens the finding — the misdirection is *documented guidance*, so a bootcamper follows it confidently. (This also independently re-confirms the earlier `explain-error-code-now-owns-senz7426` finding.)
- **Summary:** Settings resolution is now content-aware and validates before acting. **Criteria, 7 of 7 hold**, each exercised against the real CLI in a scratch project as well as by unit tests. (1) *Stub file alone* → `exit 2`, **no snapshot**, stderr names the source (`config/engine_config.json`) and all three missing keys. (2) *Stub file + complete env var* → env var's values used, stderr: "config/engine_config.json is missing PIPELINE CONFIGPATH, RESOURCEPATH, SUPPORTPATH; using $SENZING_ENGINE_CONFIGURATION_JSON instead." (3) *Both complete but differing* → "using config/engine_config.json; $SENZING_ENGINE_CONFIGURATION_JSON is also set and differs — the file wins." (4) *Neither present* → the original message byte-for-byte, `exit 2`. (5) *Docstring states the precedence* — as a numbered order, explicitly labeled content-aware, with `SENZ7426` recorded as the reason the gate exists. (6) *Guard is stdlib-only and SDK-free* — `resolve_settings` is pure, so all 12 cases run with no `libSz.so`, database or license (INV-108); assertions are on messages and on the absent snapshot, never on engine behavior. (7) *Cross-platform and language-agnostic.* Also kept: identical sources produce **no** narration (narrating agreement is noise), and a present-but-blank key counts as missing.
  ⚠️ **One criterion was refined during implementation, recorded in the spec rather than silently satisfied.** As written it said the failure message "does not mention transliteration". Too strict: naming `SENZ7426` as what *would* have happened, and that it points at `SUPPORTPATH` rather than at this file, is precisely the sentence that helps someone who has already hit the error and is searching for it. The refined criterion — and the guard — require that transliteration is not the **headline cause**: the first line must name the incomplete settings. Moving a goalpost is a real hazard, so the change is annotated in the spec with the reasoning, not just applied.
  **Negative control: 7 mutations, all caught** — existence-based precedence restored (7 assertions fire), validation gate stubbed to `return []` (6), blank values counted as present (1), narration of the winning source removed (1), failure message stripped of the missing keys (3), transliteration headlined as the cause (2), docstring's content-aware statement removed (1).
  ⚠️ **One mutation initially read as a MISS and was not one — the mutation had not landed.** The "stop naming which source won" edit relied on an exact-string replace spanning an em dash and an escaped newline; it silently matched nothing, so the suite passed and looked like a gap. A follow-up attempt removed two lines by heuristic and broke the file's syntax, which produced output my result-grep did not match — a second false reading in the same direction. Re-run surgically two ways (reword the message; replace the call with `pass`), both verified to land by counting occurrences before and after, and both **caught**. The lesson is the one the dry-run procedure states and I did not apply until it bit: **a mutation must be verified to land, or "not caught" is indistinguishable from "not mutated".**
  **Predicted-but-unchanged, deliberately:** the spec listed `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03b-truthset-visualization/phase1-visualization.md` as a *possible* change — "if the run instruction should pass `--settings` explicitly rather than relying on the default". It should **not**, and was left untouched. The default is now safe on its own: an incomplete `config/engine_config.json` no longer wins over a complete env var, and a set that is incomplete either way fails naming the source and the missing keys. Making every call site pass `--settings` would push the fix out to the callers while leaving the resolver's hazard intact for the next caller — the opposite of fixing the class. The prediction was a hedge written before the resolver's shape was decided; recording that it was considered and declined is the point of this note.
- **Establishes `INV-210`** — *where a script accepts the same configuration from more than one source, precedence is content-aware rather than existence-based; the chosen set is validated before use; the source in force is named whenever two are present; and an incomplete set fails naming the source and what it lacks rather than proceeding.* Registered beneath the append marker, indexed under **Generator behavior**, with the bidirectional enforcer citation written before the guard had to ask. Extends INV-111/INV-129 from what a generator must *report* to what a script must *check before acting* — the fallback here was honest and the reported reason was still wrong, the same shape as the `_clip` defect.

## mcp-negative-markers-must-name-the-owning-route

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-13
- **Files changed:** `.claude/skills/dry-run/coverage_reports.py` (`MCP_NEGATIVE` regex, new `MCP_NEGATIVE_TOKEN`, new `find_malformed_negatives()`, `find_negatives()` tuple widened to 7, `report_negatives()` preamble + owner line + malformed block), `.claude/skills/implement-spec/SKILL.md` (documented format, the ⛔ explaining the clause, and the `ignore-file` opt-out for its own template), `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/bootcamp-preparation/SKILL.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-02-sdk-setup/SKILL.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-05-data-quality-mapping/phase2-data-mapping.md` (owner clauses on all three live markers), `tests/test_dated_negatives_are_marked.py` (+4 tests), `tests/test_invariant_enforcer_citations.py` (`EXPECTED_PAIRS` 26 → 27), `specs/INVARIANTS.md` (INV-209), `specs/IMPLEMENTED.md` (this entry)
- **MCP re-check:** server **1.32.9, 2026-08-13** — every owner clause written was confirmed live this session: `get_capabilities` carries the language set; `sdk_guide(topic='install', platform='macos_arm', language='python')` returns only the Linux-only compatibility note; `mapping_workflow` step 2 rejects a payload without `embedded_in` with `'embedded_master' requires 'embedded_in'`. No claim rests on a route that was not asked — which is the whole point of the change.
- **Summary:** `MCP-NEGATIVE` markers now carry a required `owner:` clause naming the route that would **carry** the fact and what it returned. **Criteria, 8 of 8 hold.** (1) *`owner` parses as required* — a clauseless marker does not match, verified by a direct unit test on the pattern rather than on repo contents. (2) *Report prints the clause and says to re-ask the owner* — preamble cites INV-194 and explains that an empty result from a non-owning tool is evidence about that tool and nothing else; asserted by the report test. (3) *All three live markers carry accurate clauses* — two are **routing** negatives (the fact exists elsewhere), one is an **absence** negative (the absence *is* the answer, since the Python SDK is Linux-only). (4) *`implement-spec` documents the format and both shapes.* (5) *Guard fails on omission* — negative-controlled below. (6) *Read-only, stdlib-only, exits 0* — unchanged. (7) *INV-209 registered, indexed under MCP sourcing and tool contracts, enforcer cites it back*; `EXPECTED_PAIRS` re-derived 26 → 27. (8) *Cross-platform and language-agnostic.* **Suite `1811 → 1813`, `OK (skipped=3)`; `citations.py verify` clean at 209.**
  **Negative control: 9 mutations, and the guard failed 3 of them before it held.** Caught first pass: vague owner ("checked elsewhere" — a back-reference, not a route); empty owner; report not printing the clause; report dropping the INV-194 preamble. ⚠️ **Three genuine holes found by mutation, each fixed:** (a) **stripping the clause entirely was NOT caught** — the marker simply stopped parsing and *silently fell off the worklist*, shrinking it 3 → 2 with the suite green. That is the exact invisibility the marker convention exists to prevent, reintroduced by the fix meant to strengthen it; fixed by adding `find_malformed_negatives()`, reporting malformed markers **ahead of** the worklist as worse than missing ones, and asserting none exist. (b) **neutering that new detector to `return []` was NOT caught**, because the only check on it compared against the live repo where the correct answer is empty — fixed with a scratch-tree test that feeds it one clauseless and one well-formed marker and asserts it separates them. (c) **making `owner:` optional in the regex was NOT caught**, because every live marker had its clause — fixed with a direct pattern unit test asserting the clauseless form is rejected and the well-formed form accepted. The pattern across (b) and (c) is one lesson: **a guard that only ever reads the repo's current state cannot detect its own mechanism being disabled.**
  ⚠️ **A `git checkout` during mutation ate uncommitted work.** `find_malformed_negatives()` and its reporting were written *after* the commit that preceded the mutation run, and the M5/M6 reverts restored the file to its committed state, discarding them — the hazard the dry-run skill's absolute rules name explicitly ("`git restore` cannot tell your fix from a defect you injected"). Re-applied, committed immediately, and the remaining mutations run against a `cp` backup as well as a commit. Nothing was lost permanently; roughly ten minutes were.
- **Establishes `INV-209`** — *an `MCP-NEGATIVE` marker MUST name the route that owns the fact, the clause is required-to-parse, and vague back-references are insufficient.* It is **INV-194 made mechanical**: that invariant was registered and indexed and was violated anyway, producing INV-208's false premise and a guard that enforced it. INV-208 and INV-209 are the same defect at two altitudes — the wrong claim, and the convention that let it read as reviewed.

### ⚠️ Correction, same day (2026-08-13) — the fix above was wrong on its central fact

- **Superseding commit:** see the follow-up commit re-scoping INV-208; the entry above is kept
  unedited as the record of what was believed at `d90a5b9`.
- **What was wrong:** the claim "Senzing reads no license-path environment variable" is **false**.
  `sdk_guide(topic='load', language=…, record_count=<above the default limit>)` returns
  `SENZING_LICENSE_FILE` in its `compatibility_notes` — verified on 1.32.9, 2026-08-13 at
  `(python, 1000)` and `(java, 600)`, language-independent, present only above the limit. So (a)
  module-02's original note, which said `sdk_guide` returns `SENZING_LICENSE_FILE`, had been
  **correct**, and the "fix" replaced a true statement with a false one; (b) INV-208's prefix ban
  forbade the **correct** name; (c) the negative-control run that "proved" the guard was sound proved
  only that it enforced a false premise consistently.
- **Root cause of the error:** absence inferred from three tools that do not carry the fact
  (`configure`, `install`, `search_docs`) without asking the tool that owns it — precisely
  **INV-194**, which was already registered and indexed and was simply not applied. Three silences
  read as proof because there were three of them.
- **How it was caught:** the phase-3 conversational walk called
  `sdk_guide(topic='load', record_count=1000)` at Module 1 Step 5a for the *evaluation-license record
  limit*, and `SENZING_LICENSE_FILE` was sitting in the same `compatibility_notes` block. Nothing in
  the offline suite could have caught it (INV-108 keeps the suite offline, and the false claim had
  been written into the guard, so the guard agreed with it). ⚠️ **This is the second time in this
  repo's history that a stale/false negative was load-bearing in a test** — the phase-1 procedure
  warns about exactly this shape, and the run still produced a fresh instance.
- **What still stands:** `SENZING_LICENSE_PATH` really is a confabulation returned by no tool, and it
  really did ship in graduation's `.env.example`. The defect was real; only the diagnosis was wrong.
- **Corrected:** `graduation/SKILL.md` now names `SENZING_LICENSE_FILE` plus the `PIPELINE`
  alternative; `module-02-sdk-setup/SKILL.md` Step 5 names the correct variable, the **`record_count`
  condition** on the one route that returns it, and a ⚠️ against inferring absence from the omitting
  topics; **INV-208 rescoped in place** to ban the single wrong spelling and forbid the absence claim,
  with a dated correction note; `tests/test_license_env_var_absent.py` rewritten (3 → 5 tests) to ban
  the exact spelling, allow the two notes whose subject is that it is wrong while requiring each to
  mark it wrong nearby, require the correct spelling and its route, and pin the INV-194 warning.
- **Structural lesson recorded in the spec:** a prefix ban is *more* dangerous than a single-spelling
  ban, because it asserts a fact about every member; and a negative documented with dated evidence
  from the wrong route is indistinguishable from a verified one, so an `MCP-NEGATIVE` marker must name
  the route that **owns** the fact, not the routes that happen to omit it.

## dry-run-2026-08-12d

**Not a spec** — a dated record of a dry-run, following the `dry-run-*` precedent. **Phase 3 only**, resuming at `mapping_workflow` **step 3** where `dry-run-2026-08-12c` stopped.

- **Implemented:** 2026-08-12 (**2 findings recorded as specs; nothing fixed** — report-before-change)
- **Files changed:** `specs/inv205-covers-whether-to-ask-but-not-how.md` (new), `specs/module5-cannot-honor-an-embedded-entity-discovered-at-step-3.md` (new), `specs/IMPLEMENTED.md` (this entry). **No plugin file, script or test was modified.**
- **MCP re-check:** **server 1.32.9**, 2026-08-12. Tools called: `mapping_workflow` (`advance` step 2→3, then `back` 3→2). ⛔ `submit_feedback` **never invoked**. The prior run's `get_capabilities`/`get_sample_data`/`download_resource` calls were not repeated — nothing here depends on them.
- **Summary:** Resumed at `mapping_workflow` **step 3 (`map_fields`)** — the deepest any run has reached — with a real 3,488-record `PPP_LOANS.jsonl` re-fetched and count-verified per INV-203. **Two findings, both filed during the walk.** (1) `inv205-covers-whether-to-ask-but-not-how` — **INV-205, recorded earlier the same day**, scopes itself to a tool directive about "whether, when, or what to ask". Step 3 supplies a **QUESTION FORMAT**: no 👉, and *"State your recommendation clearly before the options"* in place of a lead question, which breaches **INV-005** and **INV-051**. The enumerated scope does not reach *how*. Proposed as a dated in-place clarification of INV-205, not a new ID. Recorded plainly as a rule generalized from one instance whose list broke on the next instance, one workflow step later — the hazard `INVARIANTS.md` itself documents about invariants that enumerate members. (2) ⚠️ `module5-cannot-honor-an-embedded-entity-discovered-at-step-3` — **the run's most significant finding.** The bootcamper was offered the `Lender` decision (239 distinct real banks across 3,488 loans) and chose to model lenders as entities; **Module 5 has no instruction that lets a guide carry that out.** `embedded_master` appears **nowhere** in `phase2-data-mapping.md`; `action='back'` is listed among the valid actions at `:136` with **no trigger stated anywhere**; and the entity is *declared* at step 2 but only *discoverable* at step 3. The path of least resistance silently downgrades the choice to `payload` — the mapping validates, the run completes, and nothing records that a bootcamper's explicit structural decision was discarded, which is what **INV-007** forbids. **Two claims were verified live rather than left inferred, and the second enlarged the finding:** `action='back'` works (returns to step 2 with `schema_plan` preserved), and **`embedded_master` cannot be expressed through the tool's own preferred payload at all** — the typed `for_step 2` branch defines `support_schemas.disposition` as `["lookup","relationship","child"]` with `additionalProperties: false`, so the disposition is reachable only via the **legacy untyped `entity_plan` shape**, while the same response calls the typed branch "preferred". So the plugin-side fix is strictly larger than first written, and the spec carries an appended section saying so. **Verified correct:** INV-205's *other* half worked live — the tool's step-3 content (field, populations, samples, numbered options, recommendation) was kept and re-presented in the bootcamp's shape with a 👉 and a neutral lead, which is the behavior the precedence rule exists to produce; and the tool's own *"Field name ≠ Feature type — check the samples"* rule earned its place twice, since `OwnedBy` reads as a person name but holds three demographic categories, and `Lender` reads as payload but holds organizations. **Coverage limits:** the walk stopped at the `back` call, so **step 3 was never completed and steps 4–8 remain unexercised** — that is where the next run starts, and it should begin by deciding the embedded-master question the second finding raises. `OwnedByRaceEthnicity` was deferred for its own turn and never reached. No engine was initialized, so nothing here touches loading or resolution; Linux only; and my own compliance remains weak evidence for the interaction invariants. **Establishes no invariant** — a dry run reports; finding (1) proposes clarifying an existing one and finding (2) proposes none.
- **Commit:** `a907e0e`

- **Summary:** The score that routes the gate is now computable by a second guide. **Criterion walk, 9 of 9 hold.** (1) *A formula is stated* — `quality_score = 0.70 × completeness + 0.25 × format_consistency + 0.05 × (100 − duplicate_rate)`, asserted by `test_a_formula_is_given`. (2) *Which fields enter completeness, and why* — Entity Specification attributes and structural keys, **plus** any field already dispositioned in mapping, with the reason stated (scoring a source down for columns this module has not yet asked about is INV-174's false-alarm shape) and the live `PPP_LOANS` 100% vs 94.4% measurement quoted inline. (3) *Format consistency and duplicate rate defined* — the latter on `(DATA_SOURCE, RECORD_ID)` **citing INV-180**, with the reason row-level counting measures something Senzing does not do; asserted. and I built a version-mismatch hypothesis on a four-turn-old reading that dissolved on re-check. **Establishes no invariant** — a dry run reports; registering rules is `implement-spec`'s job after sign-off. **Final update (end of run).** The walk continued past the interim through **System verification**, **Truth Set visualization** and **Data collection**, ending at the start of Data Quality, Mapping, and Transformation — **six modules complete**, five past phase 3's documented scope. Two further findings, bringing the total to **10**: `module3-connectivity-probe-still-uses-the-deprecated-search-docs-call` (Module 3 Step 1 probes liveness with `search_docs`, which `onboarding-flow.md:46-48` already ⛔-deprecated for exactly that use — the **third** cross-module non-propagation of this run) and ⚠️ `cord-download-rate-limit-is-saved-as-data` (**the most operationally significant finding**: fetching four CORD sources back to back, two returned `Rate limit exceeded. Try again in 1 second.` **as the response body** — HTTP success, non-empty file, one line of English prose written into `data/raw/<source>.jsonl`. Caught only by comparing line counts against the counts `get_sample_data` had already reported. The plugin has **no** rate-limit awareness anywhere, and `SKILL.md:296` asks for a *"plausible record count"* — a judgment, not a comparison. The proposed remedy was **implemented and validated in the walk**: stage each fetch, require both an exact count match and a JSON-parsable first line, promote only then, back off and retry otherwise — after which all four matched exactly at 9,033 records). **What the extension bought that the documented scope could not:** a **real engine** initialized against a project-local SQLite datastore, seeded default config, and an engine-class call (`SzDiagnostic.check_repository_performance`) rather than a version query; **real entity resolution twice over** — 4 synthetic records → 2 entities exactly as predicted by construction, and the 159-record Truth Set → **84 entities** (55 merged, 17 cross-source, 71 relationships) rendered in the live web app with all ten documented endpoints returning 200 and `/api/stats` matching the load field-for-field; the **model/effort nudge exercised in all four branches** (model-only, effort-only, both, neither) from one continuous session; the tab-coverage check **passing against a real external denominator** (6 of 6) for the first time in the run; and the earlier `SENZ7426` failure explained end-to-end — the same call that failed with `{"PIPELINE": {}}` succeeded once `SUPPORTPATH` was set, which is a live demonstration of `explain-error-code-now-owns-senz7426`. **Four near-findings were checked and dissolved rather than filed** (CORD-pre-mapped vs the mapping-complexity invariant — already corrected by INV-198 the day before; Module 3's "Opt-Out Gate" — a trigger-phrase handler, not a question; `/api/why`'s envelope — conforms exactly to `visualization-api-reference.md:399-405`; and a dpkg-vs-SDK version mismatch built on a four-turn-old reading that the host had changed underneath). **Four further errors of my own, all caught by inspecting artifacts rather than exit codes:** omitted `--title "Senzing Truth Set"` so the snapshot carried the default header (found by *reading the PNG*); captured screenshots from `--html` when the live `--url` is prescribed; omitted `--query` so Search / Probe rendered an empty result panel; and `pkill -f 'senzing_viz_server.py'` matched my own command line and killed the shell. Errors 1–3 share a shape worth stating: the module specified the argument and I skipped it — the plugin was right every time. **Coverage limits added by the extension:** the apt **upgrade** path could not run (`sudo` needs a password), so Step 1b's execute branch is unexercised; `submit_feedback` was never invoked, so the `license_request` path is schema-verified only; and Module 5's `mapping_workflow` — the 8-step stateful workflow this skill was created for — was **not reached**, which is where a next run should start.

## separate-server-owned-commands-from-plugin-owned-update-checks

- **Implemented:** 2026-07-31
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-02-sdk-setup/SKILL.md` (Step 1b preamble and all four per-platform command blocks), `tests/test_sdk_update_offer.py`, `specs/separate-server-owned-commands-from-plugin-owned-update-checks.md`
- **MCP re-check:** **changed — this spec's own ownership table was wrong.** Server 1.32.2, docs indexed 2026-07-29 11:11 UTC, 2026-07-31. Re-asked `sdk_guide(topic='install', …)` for `macos_arm` (and re-read the `linux_apt`/`linux_yum`/`windows` responses from the sweep) and read the **whole** payload — `install_commands`, all `gotchas`, `post_install`, `anti_patterns`. The table lists `brew upgrade --cask` as "yes — `install_commands`"; it **appears nowhere**. macOS documents `brew tap`, `brew trust`, `brew install --cask`, `brew uninstall --cask`/`brew untap` only. Windows documents `scoop bucket add` and `scoop install`, not `scoop update`. So **on macOS and Windows the update command itself is plugin-owned**, and only apt/yum update via the same command the server documents. Also re-confirmed the spec's re-verification clause: no installed-version query and no available-version check on any of the four platforms.
- **Summary:** Criterion walk. (1) The ambiguous sentence at `:132` is replaced by a two-bullet split with explicit precedence — server-documented commands are "on loan — re-read it, do not trust the copy below", and "**the response wins**"; the inlined forms are a dated illustration (`:134-140`). (2) The plugin-owned half states the server documents "**no version query and no update check on any of the four platforms**", so a reader who fails to find them "that is expected, not an error" (`:141-146`). (3) The two groups are distinguishable **inside** the fences, not only in the preamble — four in-fence labels, asserted individually by `test_the_labels_are_inside_the_command_blocks_not_only_the_preamble`, plus the yum prose form which needed its own marking since it has no fence. (4) **No command was deleted** — `test_no_inlined_command_was_deleted` iterates all ten as subTests, and mutation M8 (deleting `brew outdated --cask`) is caught. (5) The server-owned half keeps its tool/version/date provenance. (6) ⚠️ **This criterion needed writing, not checking** — nothing in Step 1b carried the caveat. It is now stated in actionable form: the `brew`/`scoop` forms are exercised on Linux only, so *read what the command printed* rather than trusting its exit status, which is INV-163's discipline applied to a command rather than a check, and which strengthens the existing zero-exit-code warning instead of duplicating it. (7) `tests/test_sdk_update_offer.py` passes — 48 tests, 29 subtests, with a new 12-test `CommandOwnershipIsDistinguished` class. (8) Re-verification clause satisfied above. (9) Pure Markdown guidance, no platform or language dependency. Nine guards **mutation-tested and reverted**, including restoring the original ambiguous sentence, dropping "the response wins", and **claiming `brew upgrade --cask` is server-documented — i.e. reintroducing this spec's own error**, which the new test catches. **Deviations recorded** in the spec's `## Deviations from this spec, and why (2026-07-31)`: the `brew upgrade --cask` correction and the resulting per-platform asymmetry table; criterion 6 requiring new text; and a process note — **five of nine mutations first reported a missing target rather than a passing test** because `\n` in `python3 -c` argv is a literal backslash-n and because I guessed line wrapping instead of reading it. Re-run correctly, 9 of 9 fail as they should. That is the **third time this session** a missing target has masqueraded as an escaped mutation, and it is worth checking before believing a guard failed. **No new invariant** — INV-080, INV-163 and INV-194 already applied; this makes the plugin's own text conform to them. Full suite: **1355 passed, 3 skipped, 1076 subtests** (from 1343).

## offer-to-update-an-existing-senzing-install

- **Implemented:** 2026-07-31
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-02-sdk-setup/SKILL.md` (new Step 1b, and the V4.0+ branch that routes into it), `tests/test_sdk_update_offer.py` (new), `specs/offer-to-update-an-existing-senzing-install.md`
- **MCP re-check:** **changed — the spec's central platform claim was wrong.** Server 1.32.2, docs indexed 2026-07-29 11:11 UTC, 2026-07-31. Tools called: `get_capabilities` (`senzing_version` is the string `"current"`, so it cannot answer "what is latest"); `sdk_guide(topic='install', …)` for `linux_apt`, `linux_yum`, `macos_arm`, `windows`; `search_docs(query='upgrade Senzing to a newer version existing installation')` (V3→V4 migration only — no 4.x→4.y procedure); `get_sdk_reference(topic='response_schemas', filter='get_version')` (empty `data`; `SzProduct.get_version()` returns a plain string whose shape is undocumented — INV-149). The spec said availability is Linux-only and macOS/Windows must report the check skipped. **False:** that conclusion came from asking `platform='macos_arm'` with `language='python'`, which returns nothing *because the Python SDK is Linux-only* — a language dead end, not a platform one. With `language='java'`, macOS returns a full Homebrew-cask path and Windows a full Scoop path. INV-194 for the third time this session.
- **Summary:** Criterion walk. (1) Step 1's V4.0+ branch now routes into **Step 1b**, which compares the installed version against what is available rather than only against the V4.0 floor — `test_the_v4_branch_routes_into_it`. (2) The dot/hyphen trap is stated and the preference ordering given: `szBuildVersion.json`'s `BUILD_VERSION` is `4.3.3.26191` where every package manager writes `4.3.3-26191`; both forms appear and a test asserts that exact pair. (3)-(4) **Four mechanisms, not one, and the package manager is the availability oracle on each** — `dpkg-query`/`apt-cache policy`, `rpm -q`/`yum check-update` (`dnf` on RHEL 8+), `brew outdated --cask`/`brew info --cask`, `scoop status`/`scoop info`, plus Docker where the image tag *is* the version. Skipping is the fallback for any platform where the version cannot be determined, and "no data" is never rendered as "up to date" (INV-163) — **satisfied differently than the spec wrote it**, see the deviation. (5) Exactly **one asked 👉 question**, asserted by counting 👉 at line start — a bare 👉 mid-sentence is prose describing the rule, and counting those made my first version of that test fail against correct content. (6) Declining keeps the install, says so in one line, records nothing as a failure, and is **not re-asked** (INV-006) — with the outcome checkpointed (`up-to-date` / `update-declined` / `updated-to-…` / `check-skipped-…`) so a resumed session does not re-offer. (7) Latest by default; a named version uses the versioned `direct_download` URL on apt, and for Homebrew casks and Scoop the guidance **says the server documents no version-exact install** rather than inventing a pin. A test asserts `apt install pkg=version` is never claimed. (8) The EULA question reuses Step 3 Phase 2 rather than a second copy — and the **variable differs per platform** (`HOMEBREW_SENZING_ACCEPT_EULA=i_accept_the_senzing_eula`, lowercase, on macOS vs `SENZING_ACCEPT_EULA=I_ACCEPT_THE_SENZING_EULA` elsewhere), with a test pinning the lowercase because it is the detail most likely to be "tidied" away. (9) sha256 verification required before installing a downloaded package. (10) The offer states no 4.x→4.y procedure is documented and does not assert migration is unnecessary. (11) Step 4 re-runs after an update, with a platform artifact probe because exit 0 is not evidence (INV-129); on failure the working version is named and Module 2 is not marked complete. (6) INV-103 untouched — `module-completion.md` step 2b unchanged, `test_recap_pdf_guard.py` still passes. **A scaffold is deliberately not foldable**: `generate_recap_pdf.py` warns when a `RECAP-CHECKPOINT` block survives into the recap, so folding an empty scaffold would append a meaningless block *and* raise a spurious graduation warning — `test_folding_a_scaffold_writes_nothing_at_all` pins that it creates no recap at all. **All reporting goes to stderr**, because `UserPromptSubmit`'s stdout is a JSON channel; mutation-proven (redirecting `_report` to stdout breaks seven tests, including the JSON parse). ## search-attribute-fallback-survives-a-failed-attempt

- **Implemented:** 2026-07-30
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/senzing_viz_server.py`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03b-truthset-visualization/visualization-api-reference.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-07-query-visualize-discover/phase1-query-visualize.md`, `tests/test_organization_search.py`, `specs/INVARIANTS.md`, `specs/search-attribute-fallback-survives-a-failed-attempt.md`
- **MCP re-check:** Server **1.32.2**, 2026-07-30 — **confirmed**, both facts, nothing changed. `get_capabilities` for the version; `search_docs(category='data_mapping')` returned the Entity Specification's *Name > Feature: NAME* table verbatim — `NAME_ORG` "Organization name", `NAME_FULL` "Single-field name when type (person vs org) is unknown or only a full name is provided", rule *"use `NAME_ORG` for organizations; use `NAME_FULL` only when the type is unknown or only a single field exists"* — so INV-164's premise stands unchanged. `get_sdk_reference(topic='parameters', filter='search_by_attributes', language='python')` gave `search_by_attributes(attributes: str, flags: int = SZ_SEARCH_BY_ATTRIBUTES_ALL, search_profile: str = '') -> str`, confirming `_search_one`'s 2-arg call and its `TypeError` 3-arg retry both remain valid; the response's cross-binding warning (C# takes 2 args where Python takes 3) is why the any-language wording added here is about behavior, not call shape.
- **Summary:** Fixed the guard that foreclosed the `NAME_ORG` fallback. `Model.search`'s handler was `except Exception: if not items: return {...}` — unconditionally true on the first attribute, so any engine error on `NAME_FULL` returned before `NAME_ORG` was ever called, reinstating the INV-164 defect on the error path. Failures are now collected into a `failures` list and the loop `continue`s; the error is attached only when every candidate was attempted and `items` is still empty, naming each failed attribute and its message, with `attributes_tried` still listing failed attempts. **All eight acceptance criteria hold**, seven of them runtime-verified by `tests/test_organization_search.py` (23 tests, up from 18): the new `AFailedAttemptIsNotTheEndOfTheList` covers raise-then-hit (hit returned, both attributes tried, no `error` key), raise-then-no-match (error present, so "could not run" is never rendered as the clean no-match — INV-115), all-raise (every attribute named in the error), failed attempts still reported as tried, and a shape guard that no `return` survives in the handler (comment lines stripped first, since the comment explains the old `return`). The five named pre-existing tests pass unchanged. Any-language guidance updated in both places that state the rule, since INV-164 binds a query program in any language (INV-090/INV-124) and this defect class is exactly what propagates from the reference implementation. **One criterion is not runtime-verified**: the chip-verification inheritance is true by construction (chips verify through `GET /api/search`, i.e. the same `Model.search`) and was exercised under Node with a stubbed endpoint, but not against a live engine with loaded data, which this environment lacks — recorded in the spec's `## Deviations from this spec, and why (2026-07-30)` along with the re-verified `search_by_attributes` signature. Full suite: **1084 passed, 3 skipped, 561 subtests** (was 1070).
