## dry-run-2026-07-29-phases-1-and-2

- **Implemented:** 2026-07-29
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/generate_recap_pdf.py`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03b-truthset-visualization/phase1-visualization.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03b-truthset-visualization/SKILL.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03b-truthset-visualization/visualization-api-reference.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-07-query-visualize-discover/phase2b-discover.md`, `specs/INVARIANTS.md`, `tests/test_recap_measure_font_safety.py` (new), `tests/test_truthset_acquisition_call.py` (new), `tests/test_partial_row_and_schema_coverage.py`
- **Not a spec** — a `/dry-run` the maintainer requested directly, phases 1 and 2, then asked to have all four findings fixed. Phase 3 (conversational) deferred to run against the repaired plugin. 909 tests were green before it and none of the four findings was mechanically enforced.
- **MCP re-check:** server **1.32.1**, 2026-07-29. Every `action=`/`topic=`/`category=`/`workflow=` literal in the plugin (24 distinct) validated against the live schemas; `get_sample_data`, `get_sdk_reference`, `find_examples`, `mapping_workflow`, `analyze_record`, `generate_scaffold`, `download_resource`, `reporting_guide` schemas loaded and diffed against every calling file. Two of the four findings came from this: see P1-1 and P1-2.
- **Establishes no new invariant.** P2-1/P2-2 are ordinary defects under INV-143/INV-157; P1-1 is an INV-136 violation; P1-2 is a **correction to INV-149 in place** (dated note, per the dry-run skill's rule 5 — an invariant encoding a false premise is worse than a missing one).
- **P1-1 (High): the Truth Set acquisition step made a call that cannot succeed, and its fallback trigger was stale.** `phase1-visualization.md` Step 1.1 said "Call `get_sample_data` and inspect the response" — but `dataset` is **required** ("schema-respecting clients cannot omit it"), so the call fails and reports nothing about availability (INV-136). The classification compounded it: `unavailable` = "only the CORD collections (Las Vegas, London, Moscow) are present", while `dataset='list'` on 1.32.1 returns **four** datasets, the fourth being `truthset` with `available: true` (159 records across CUSTOMERS/REFERENCE/WATCHLIST — the codes and count the plugin's own example recap cites). `dataset='truthset'` appeared **nowhere in the plugin**. So the module was written to conclude the MCP primary path had failed when it works, dropping to `github_fallback` and recording the wrong provenance — against the step's own declaration that MCP "always takes precedence", and putting INV-077's guarantee on the fallback. Both files now name `dataset='list'` for discovery and `dataset='truthset'` for retrieval, decide availability from `available_datasets`, describe the fallback as exceptional, and take codes and counts **from the response, never from the file** — the counts are deliberately *not* asserted in the test, since hardcoding them is how the old classification went stale.
- **P1-2 (Medium-High): INV-149's first verified claim was false, and a test pinned it.** `get_sdk_reference(topic='response_schemas', filter='find_network')` **now documents the element fields** — `ENTITY_NETWORK_LINKS[].MIN_ENTITY_ID`, `.MAX_ENTITY_ID`, `.MATCH_KEY`, `.MATCH_LEVEL_CODE`, `.ERRULE_CODE`, `.IS_AMBIGUOUS`, `.IS_DISCLOSED`, plus `ENTITIES[].RESOLVED_ENTITY.*` and `ENTITY_PATHS[].*` — where INV-149 recorded "with **no** element fields" as verified 2026-07-26. The contract shipped the negative claim "**NOT in `response_schemas`**", and `test_partial_row_and_schema_coverage.py` *required* it plus that the keys be marked unverified — so the suite held a false premise in place and forced the plugin to understate what MCP confirms. INV-149 corrected in place with a dated note; its **second** half still holds (`get_version` returns `data: []`), and the rule it states is unchanged. The contract and `phase2b-discover.md` now cite `response_schemas` as the authority with the 2026-07-28 dump as corroboration, and **still require the lookup and the dump** — the standing of the names changed, not the discipline. Five assertions in the test were reversed or rewritten, each carrying why.
- **P2-1 (High): the recap PDF fell back to the stdlib renderer on any unfinalized recap.** With fpdf2 2.8.5 installed the generator reported `renderer: stdlib` — a defect, not a fallback — because `fpdf2 render failed: Character "—" … outside the range … "helvetica"`. Traceback: `_render_certificate` → `_cert_module_layout` → `_wrap_to_width` → `_cert_text_width` → `pdf.get_string_width`. **fpdf2's `get_string_width` runs the same `normalize_text` as its text writers**, so measurement raises on exactly the characters `_safe` folds — and every *write* went through `_safe` while **none of the five measurements did**. Cost: the keepsake loses real tables (INV-142) and the branded certificate (INV-156), at exit 0, signaled only by one word. `test_recap_pdf_font_safety.py` passed throughout because it covers writes. Fixed as a **class**, per the skill's rule 1: a single `_width(pdf, text)` helper folds before measuring and all five sites now route through it, so no future call site can reintroduce the hazard — and the folded string is also the *correct* width, since it is what gets drawn.
- **P2-2 (Medium) and P2-1's trigger share one root cause: `_split_title_date`.** It split `## Name — <date>` only when the tail began with four digits, so the `— in progress` suffix the durability hooks leave on a folded-but-unfinalized section (INV-059) stayed glued to the title. That single stale title produced both symptoms: the certificate joins and fits module titles, carrying the em dash into a measurement; and `--check --expect-modules` compares against the title, so a present section read as absent — one run reported the same section as both validated-by-name and *"has no recap section at all"*, which sends graduation to backfill a section that already exists (INV-157 warns against exactly that). Now recognizes the `in progress` marker the plugin itself produces and returns it in the date slot; deliberately narrower than loosening the date test, so a module name legitimately containing " — " is still not mangled.
- **Verification:** every fix negative-controlled by reintroducing the defect and confirming failure, then restoring byte-identically (skill rule 3, not optional). Reverting P2-1+P2-2 together reproduced the **verbatim** original symptom (`renderer: stdlib` plus the em-dash message) and failed 6 tests; P1-1's revert failed 9; P1-2's failed 1. 937 tests pass (from 909): `test_recap_measure_font_safety.py` adds 14, `test_truthset_acquisition_call.py` adds 14.
- **Verified correct (so the next audit need not re-check):** all six hooks silent and exit 0 outside a bootcamp; the write-gate blocks `/tmp`, `~/Downloads`, `C:\Windows\Temp`, PEM, AWS key id and `AQAAAD` blob while allowing project paths **including a project whose own path contains `tmp`**; feedback-capture injects on feedback and verbosity prompts and stays silent otherwise; stop-nudge silent on every bias-to-silence condition and both INV-055 opt-outs; **INV-059's fold is exactly idempotent** (folds on run 1, byte-stable on runs 2 and 3, completed section's four subsections intact); the feedback file is byte-identical through the normalizer (INV-067); the discoveries generator refuses junk and writes no PDF (INV-110); an unknown tab id is rejected by name with no file saved under it (INV-122); `color_for_sources` gives 9 distinct order-independent encodings for 9 non-Truth-Set sources (INV-127); the viz server writes **no** snapshot when the engine is unavailable, in both failure modes (INV-077's blank-page risk); **zero** hits from the server's own `common_confabulations` list; INV-132's in-place correction still accurate; INV-160 reproduces exactly, including the response advertising an undeclared `inline` parameter it forbids adopting; `reporting_guide`'s two unnamed topics omitted deliberately with documented reasons. The live library also reproduced `SENZ7426|Transliteration failed`, corroborating the SUPPORTPATH spec rewritten 2026-07-28.
- **Coverage limits (explicit).** **No records were ever loaded and no SDK-dependent path was exercised.** `libSz.so` loads with `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/senzing/er/lib` and `senzing_core` imports, but engine initialization fails at `SENZ7426` because the support data is not configured — so INV-151 (redo drain termination), INV-152 (factory lifetime), INV-083/INV-089 (register-before-load) and any real resolution remain unverified, exactly as in previous runs. zsh is still absent, so INV-175's zsh branch is again untested. Chrome capture never ran: `capture_screenshots.py` validated tab ids and exited first. **Phase 3 (conversational — INV-005–INV-009, INV-012, INV-029–INV-032 apparatus and gate ordering) was not run** and remains the standing gap; it cannot be self-played.
- **Commit:** `7683d61`

## deep-dive-audit-2026-07-28b

- **Implemented:** 2026-07-28
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/bootcamp-onboarding/module-completion.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03b-truthset-visualization/phase2-close.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/docs/examples/bootcamp_recap.example.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/docs/examples/bootcamp_recap.example.pdf`, `tests/test_recap_pdf_images.py`, `tests/test_example_recap_sync.py`; then for finding 3 (2026-07-29) `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/senzing_viz_server.py`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03b-truthset-visualization/visualization-api-reference.md`, `specs/INVARIANTS.md`, `tests/test_graph_label_distinctness.py`
- **Not a spec** — a fourth full-repo invariant-conformance and coherence audit the maintainer requested directly, then asked to have findings 1, 2 and 4 fixed in place. Distinct from `deep-dive-audit-2026-07-28` earlier the same day (that one established INV-159); recorded separately so the two audits' findings and file sets stay legible. 883 tests were green before it and none of the findings was mechanically enforced.
- **MCP re-check:** n/a (no Senzing fact — every finding is internal consistency between the plugin's own files and its own generator). Server 1.32.1, 2026-07-28.
- **Establishes no new invariant** — findings 1, 2 and 4 are **failures to apply INV-161/INV-162**, recorded the same day, to everything they bind; finding 3 is the same shape against **INV-153**. In every case the rule was already right and its retro-application was incomplete, so INV-153's scope was clarified in place rather than a new invariant recorded.
- **Finding 1 (High, live flow): every screenshot was being lost from every Bootcamper's recap PDF.** INV-161 moved image resolution to the recap document's own directory. The recap is `docs/bootcamp_recap.md` and its screenshots are `docs/visualizations/*.png`, so the only path that resolves is `visualizations/<file>.png`. `graduation/SKILL.md:473` said exactly that and explicitly forbade the alternative — but `module-completion.md:98` and `:199`, which write the recap at **every** module close, instructed `![caption](docs/visualizations/…)`, and `phase2-close.md:125` verified against the same broken form. Confirmed against the live resolver: the instructed path returns `None`, the graduation-documented one resolves. So the resolver was fixed and the instructions that *produce* the paths were updated in one place out of four; graduation's backfill could not recover it, because an embed that exists but points nowhere is not a *missed* embed. All three sites now carry the document-relative form **and the reason** (`docs/`-prefixed resolves to `docs/docs/…`), since a bare corrected example invites being "helpfully" corrected back.
- **Finding 2 (Medium-High, shipped artifact): the example recap was no longer reproducible.** `bootcamp_recap.example.md` referenced its screenshot as `docs/examples/…`, valid only under the pre-INV-161 cwd semantics: a fresh render gave `embedded 0 of 1 images` and 4 image objects against the committed 5, breaking INV-065's "MUST remain regenerable". The HTML comment above the path documented the outlawed behavior as correct and conceded the path would not display in a Markdown reader — exactly what INV-161 forbids. Worse, `tests/test_example_recap_sync.py`'s docstring prescribed `cd plugins/senzing-bootcamp` before regenerating, which INV-161 names as forbidden, and its assertions passed only because they inspected the **committed** PDF whose image was baked in by an older render. Path made document-relative, comment rewritten, PDF regenerated from the repo root (5 images, byte-identical 162,910 bytes, `--check` clean from an unrelated cwd).
- **Finding 4 (Low): a stale claim contradicting INV-162.** `module-completion.md:98` said the PDF "silently skips" missing images; INV-162 requires each drop be named on stderr with an `embedded N of M images` count. Same sentence as Finding 1, corrected with it and now swept for across all three sites.
- **Finding 3 (Low-Medium, fixed 2026-07-29 after the maintainer settled the scope question): INV-153's distinctness rule was implemented for match keys only.** `senzing_viz_server.py:849` cut graph node labels at a fixed 20 characters with no collision check, so two organizations sharing a 19-character prefix — `ACME HOLDINGS INTERNATIONAL LLC` and `…INC` share 27 — rendered as the same string on the one surface whose purpose is telling entities apart, while `drawMatchKeys` compared its fitted labels and disambiguated. The blocker was a scope call only the maintainer could make, because the two answers have different mechanics: "it binds" permits clarifying INV-153 in place (`INVARIANTS.md:33`), while "graph labels are exempt" would be a change of meaning requiring a new ID (`:34`). The maintainer ruled **it binds** (2026-07-29). Fixed in three places, because the contract half is the load-bearing one: **(1)** `visualization-api-reference.md`'s "Defaults at production scale" section now leads with `**1. Every truncated label must stay distinguishable — whatever it labels**` as its own general requirement, with the match-key rule renumbered to 2 as its application and the graph default to 3 — a server generated in another language is built from that contract and never reads the Python, which is exactly how the `NAME_FULL` defect shipped (INV-164); **(2)** the reference now fits labels, compares the **fitted** strings, suffixes only a genuine collision (two entities that really share a name still render alike, per "unless their underlying values are identical"), and gives the label its own `<title>` rather than relying on the group tooltip; **(3)** `tests/test_graph_label_distinctness.py` adds 18 tests. INV-153's wording was clarified in place to state the scope explicitly — no meaning change, since the first clause was always unqualified and the match-key sentence was always an application of it.
- **Verification:** the new guards were proven to catch the defects by reintroducing both original forms — 6 failures — and restoring. 891 tests pass (from 883); `test_recap_pdf_images.py` adds a 6-test class asserting no skill instructs a `docs/`-prefixed embed, that the reason is stated, that a recap written as the skills instruct embeds 6 of 6, and that no site claims silent skipping; `test_example_recap_sync.py` adds a fresh-render class that renders from an unrelated cwd, since INV-065's "regenerable" is a property of a fresh render and cannot be established from committed bytes.
- **Method and its limits:** static analysis (link/anchor resolution, dangling `INV-NNN`, cross-module `Step N` references, layout-tree drift, hook exec form and purposes, tab-set and threshold agreement, model/effort table, MCP-grounding clauses, question forms) plus live execution probes of the recap generator. The conversational invariants — INV-005–INV-009, INV-012, INV-029–INV-032 gate ordering and apparatus — are out of reach of this method and still need a `dry-run`. Thirteen live invariants have no test naming them (INV-094, 101, 118, 144, 145, 150, 151, 152, 153, 157, 172 among them); of those examined, only INV-153 showed an actual gap.
- **Commit:** `a8ee925` (findings 1, 2, 4); `a27684a` (finding 3, 2026-07-29)

## env-script-must-be-shell-portable

- **Implemented:** 2026-07-28
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-02-sdk-setup/SKILL.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03-system-verification/phase1-verification.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/bootcamp-onboarding/ground-rules.md`, `specs/INVARIANTS.md`, `tests/test_env_script_shell_portability.py`, `specs/env-script-must-be-shell-portable.md` (deviation + invariant notes)
- **MCP re-check:** server **1.32.1**, 2026-07-28 — **changed, and the spec's own `n/a (no Senzing fact)` was wrong.** The spec asserts a Senzing fact: that a mis-resolved root surfaces as a JVM *"Unable to get settings"*, *"an error that points at the SDK"*. `search_docs(query='"Unable to get settings"')` finds that string **only** inside Senzing's own official snippets (`senzing/code-snippets-v4` — `java/snippets/information/GetVersion.java`, `GetLicense.java`, the C# `Program.cs` equivalents), in the sample program's *own* guard, which prints it and throws `IllegalArgumentException`/`ArgumentException`. `search_docs(category='troubleshooting')` and `explain_error_code('0058')` return no engine error of that name; the nearest codes, `SENZ0058 EAS_ERR_SZ_INITIALIZATION_FAILURE` and `SENZ0050 EAS_ERR_SZCORE_NOT_INITIALIZED`, are **not** documented as the symptom of an unset environment variable, so neither is cited (INV-169). `SENZING_ENGINE_CONFIGURATION_JSON` re-confirmed as the documented variable via `search_docs(category='configuration')`. Two changes to the fix followed: the guidance tells readers the symptom carries **no SENZ code** and must **not** be routed through `explain_error_code` — the reverse of the spec's framing — and, because the guard tests `settings == null` (*unset*, not empty), the snippet **refuses to export an empty configuration** rather than merely checking the path.
- **Summary:** Module 2's env-script rule now carries the anchored canonical statement (`<a id="env-script-path-resolution"></a>`) that a sourced script MUST resolve its own path in the platform's **default** shell, with a runnable bash/zsh idiom: branch on `${ZSH_VERSION}` to `${(%):-%x}`, else `${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-$0}`; verify the computed root holds `config/engine_config.json`; fail naming the resolved path; refuse an empty configuration; then export. `ground-rules.md` gains a "Sourced scripts and the default shell" section immediately after the Windows/PowerShell one so both supported platforms' shell semantics sit together, and it **links** the anchor rather than restating it. Module 2's Troubleshooting and Module 3's Step 1a both name the symptom and re-attribute it to the snippet guard, and Step 1a checks for a missing SENZ code **before** reaching for `explain_error_code`. **Three things beyond the spec:** (1) `return 1`, never `exit 1` — the spec mandates failing loudly, and the obvious way to fail in a sourced script closes the Bootcamper's terminal while `set -e` leaks into their session, so implementing item 3 literally would have traded a silent wrong root for a killed shell; (2) the shipped snippet is **executed** by the tests — extracted from the fenced block after the anchor, installed in a synthetic project tree and sourced — because a present-but-wrong idiom is precisely this defect; (3) verified by running it that bash **parses** the zsh-only `${(%):-%x}` in the untaken branch without a bad-substitution or syntax error, so no `eval` guard is needed. Scoped to bash and zsh, not POSIX `sh` (`${BASH_SOURCE[0]}` is a bad substitution under dash and no POSIX way exists), and Windows keeps `senzing-env.bat` with `%~dp0`. The same-shell requirement and the `.bat` path are untouched, asserted verbatim by a test. **NOT runtime-verified:** acceptance criterion 2's **zsh** half — zsh is not installed in this environment (`command -v zsh` returns nothing), so it is disclosed rather than ticked; `test_zsh_resolves_the_same_root_as_bash` exists, skips with that reason, and will run wherever zsh is present. The bash half, the fail-loud guard, the empty-config refusal, cwd-independence and shell survival are all runtime-verified by sourcing the snippet. 882 tests pass (from 851); `tests/test_env_script_shell_portability.py` adds 31 plus 1 skip.
- **Invariant:** `INV-175` (sourced scripts resolve their own path in the default shell; verify before exporting; `return`, never `exit`; never export an empty value).
- **Commit:** `32e9c9b`

## default-tab-capture-without-injection

- **Implemented:** 2026-07-28
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/senzing_viz_server.py`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/capture_screenshots.py`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03b-truthset-visualization/visualization-api-reference.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/bootcamp-onboarding/module-completion.md`, `tests/test_snapshot_and_capture_fidelity.py`, `specs/default-tab-capture-without-injection.md` (deviation note)
- **MCP re-check:** n/a (no Senzing fact — the defect is in a bundled capture script and the page it drives). Server 1.32.1, 2026-07-28.
- **Summary:** New invariant established: INV-171 (capture apparatus must not perturb what it captures; a view-switching function must be idempotent and animated content gets longer to settle). **Implemented differently from the spec, deliberately, and the deviation is recorded on the spec file.** The spec said to detect the page's default tab from the markup and skip the `activate()` injection for it. Two findings at implementation time made that wrong: (1) `buildNav()` builds the nav at runtime and marks index 0 active, so the served HTML contains no nav buttons and no active marker — a markup probe cannot work, and the spec's "fall back safely" branch would have been the only branch ever taken; (2) `applyDeepLink()` also calls `activate(tab)`, which is how the **live server** is captured, so a caller-side skip in `capture_screenshots.py` would have left that route still restarting the simulation. The guard therefore went into `activate()` itself — called for the tab already active it returns before `drawFor()` — which covers the injected route, the deep-link route and a user clicking the already-active nav button, and which lives in the any-language contract where a Python-side fix could not reach (INV-090/INV-124). Spec item 3 was implemented as written: `_virtual_time_ms(tab)` returns 30s for the force-directed tabs (`graph`, `network`) against the base 15s for static ones, threaded to the Chrome backend via module state rather than a new backend parameter, because `_BACKENDS` is invoked uniformly and an existing test substitutes two-argument callables for it. `module-completion.md` now tells the reader to open the Entity Graph image and check the nodes are spread, naming a much smaller file size as the tell. **One acceptance criterion is not runtime-verified:** the visual check (spread layout, file-size floor) needs a live server with loaded data this environment lacks — the mechanism is asserted instead (early return precedes `drawFor()`, contract requires idempotence, graph budget exceeds the static one). Full suite 739 passing, including the real-browser capture tests and the JS-executing viz tests.

The `find_network_*` row of the MCP-confirmed paths table now documents the element key set — `MIN_ENTITY_ID` / `MAX_ENTITY_ID` (endpoints, normalized low-to-high), `MATCH_LEVEL_CODE`, `MATCH_KEY`, `ERRULE_CODE`, `IS_DISCLOSED`, `IS_AMBIGUOUS` — marked **dump-confirmed on SDK 4.3.3, 2026-07-28, and explicitly NOT in `response_schemas`**. INV-149's marking discipline is preserved, not relaxed — the existing `NoUnverifiedFieldNameIsShipped` guards ("not MCP-confirmable", "warning about where to look", "use what is actually there") all still pass **unchanged**, so this added the record without weakening the guard. (2) **The `JSON_DATA` trap is recorded**, re-verified against the live server 2026-07-28: `get_sdk_reference(topic='response_schemas', filter='getEntity')` lists `RESOLVED_ENTITY.RECORDS[].JSON_DATA.*` source-value paths, while `SZ_ENTITY_INCLUDE_RECORD_JSON_DATA` reports `applies_to: ["get_record"]` and is a member of `SZ_RECORD_DEFAULT_FLAGS` — so **no** entity-family flag produces those paths and a viewer built on them renders blank for every record against a loaded database. `JSON_DATA` appeared nowhere in the plugin before this, so the failure was fully re-derivable; the contract now states it, names the flag and its `applies_to`, and says plainly that this is the one place the authoritative reference is itself what misleads. **The spec's open question about a cheaper path was resolved affirmatively:** `SZ_ENTITY_INCLUDE_RECORD_FEATURE_DETAILS` ("include full feature details at the record level of an entity response") lists `get_entity_by_entity_id`, `get_entity_by_record_id`, `search_by_attributes`, `why_*`, `find_path_*` and `find_network_*` in its `applies_to` (verified 2026-07-28), and the get_entity schema documents `RECORDS[].FEATURES.<TYPE>[].ATTRIBUTES.*` plus `RECORDS[].UNMAPPED_DATA.*` — so per-record source values are reachable from the entity family in **one** call. The guidance states this without overclaiming: those are the *mapped* attributes per feature, not the raw record as loaded, so `get_record` + `SZ_RECORD_DEFAULT_FLAGS` remains the route when the raw `JSON_DATA` document is genuinely needed, at one extra SDK call per record. Module 7's discover step carries both findings as short pointers with its dump-first and partial-row rules intact. **One acceptance criterion is not runtime-verified:** "a relationship-network rendering built from this guidance shows both endpoint ids populated" needs a live engine with loaded data, which this environment does not have — the guidance content is in place and asserted by tests, but the rendering itself awaits a bootcamp run. `tests/test_partial_row_and_schema_coverage.py` grew from 9 to 22 tests (its stale "these tests deliberately do NOT assert any specific endpoint field name" docstring was updated to describe the new state, and its `__main__` guard moved to the end of the file, where it had been leaving the appended classes uncollected on a direct run). ## export-related-entities-is-flag-conditional

- **Implemented:** 2026-07-28
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-06-data-processing/phaseD-validation.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03b-truthset-visualization/visualization-api-reference.md`, `tests/test_related_entities_guidance.py`, `specs/IMPLEMENTED.md` (annotation on the reversed entry)
- **Summary:** New invariant established: INV-169 (a single observation of SDK behavior must not be generalized into an absolute about a method; record the flag set, version and binding, and route through a per-installation check). **This reverses an absolute a previously-implemented spec shipped** — `match-key-audit-cannot-read-related-entities-from-export`, whose ledger entry is annotated in place to record the correction, since it sits in the guard test's `GRANDFATHERED` set and nothing would otherwise link the two. Phase D's ⛔ "Do not expect `RELATED_ENTITIES` from `export_json_entity_report`" is gone from both files, replaced by the flag-conditional truth plus a routing instruction: dump one export row, print its top-level keys and a `carries RELATED_ENTITIES` boolean, then route — present → do both reads in one export pass; absent → keep the per-record read on the export and use a per-entity reader or `find_network_by_entity_id` for the relationship half. **Verified against the live MCP server rather than the field report:** `reporting_guide(topic='evaluation')` documents each row of an export taken with `SZ_EXPORT_DEFAULT_FLAGS` as carrying `RESOLVED_ENTITY` **and** `RELATED_ENTITIES[]` (with `ENTITY_ID`, `MATCH_LEVEL_CODE`, `MATCH_KEY`, `ERRULE_CODE`, `RECORD_SUMMARY[]`), and its worked `export_with_stats` pattern computes relationship categories in a single export pass. **Deviation from the spec, and an improvement on it:** acceptance criterion 6 asked for the flag's relationship behavior to be "confirmed by a dumped row at implementation time"; no live engine is available in this environment, so it is instead carried by an MCP citation marked verified-2026-07-28 — a stronger source than a dump under INV-080, with the per-installation dump retained as the routing check. The rewrite also explains why *both* field observations were real (the earlier session composed its flags from `SZ_ENTITY_INCLUDE_*` members, which do not list the export methods in `applies_to`; `SZ_EXPORT_DEFAULT_FLAGS` is an export-family flag documented as matching "the normal entity defaults", which include the relationship-inclusion members), so neither report is written off. It additionally fixes a defect the old absolute was masking: `reporting_guide` warns that each relationship appears in **both** entities' `RELATED_ENTITIES`, so a single-pass read must deduplicate `(min_id, max_id)` pairs — both files now require it, since without it the audit double-counts every relationship and *inflates* a suppressor share rather than emptying it, a wrong number that still looks plausible. Every guarantee the reversed spec established survives and is still test-enforced: the reader-capability check (now cheaper, since the row dump answers it for the whole pass), the three-outcome iterate-vs-proceed gate, the never-"no suppressors"-on-a-failed-read rule (INV-115), and no direct SQL against `database/G2C.db` (INV-117). `tests/test_related_entities_guidance.py` was rewritten — it had pinned the reversed absolute in three places — and now asserts across **both** files that neither absolute is stated, that the answer is conditioned on the flag set, that one row is dumped before a reader is chosen, that the export case carries its `reporting_guide` citation, and that pair deduplication is required; 15 tests, full suite 673 passing.

## windows-headless-browser-discovery-for-screenshots

- **Implemented:** 2026-07-28
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/capture_screenshots.py`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/bootcamp-onboarding/module-completion.md`, `tests/test_windows_browser_discovery.py`
- **Summary:** New invariant established: INV-168 (executable discovery must cover each supported platform's conventional install locations, must never report a present capability as absent, and must name what it searched). `_chrome_exe()` probed only bare command names via `shutil.which()` and hard-coded macOS `/Applications/...` paths, so on Windows — which places neither browser on `PATH` — a workstation carrying **both** Edge and Chrome was told "No headless screenshot capability available" and lost the screenshots from two recap sections, while `C:\Program Files\...` was never examined. `_chrome_exe()` now delegates to a new `_chrome_search_paths()` that appends Windows candidates when `os.name == "nt"`: Chrome and Edge under `%ProgramFiles%`, `%ProgramFiles(x86)%` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%`, expanded from the environment at call time so a non-C: drive or a localized `Program Files` still resolves, followed by an `App Paths` registry probe wrapped so an absent `winreg`, missing key or permission error yields nothing rather than raising. The single conflated failure message became two: "no browser found", which now enumerates every location searched, and "a browser was found (<path>) but every capture attempt failed", which states plainly that this is **not** a missing install — the old wording's real damage was sending the reader to install software they already had. `module-completion.md`'s exit-2 handling now says the three reasons are not interchangeable and that only one concerns a missing install. Per the spec, browser auto-installation was deliberately **not** added: nothing was missing on the reporting machine, capture is dependency-optional by contract (INV-122), and any install belongs behind a consent gate outside this probe path. The second gap the feedback reported — blank tab bodies from a missing `--virtual-time-budget` — was already fixed in the tree at `capture_screenshots.py:327` (`_CHROME_VIRTUAL_TIME_MS = 15000`) after the 0.4.1 release the bootcamper ran; it is now pinned by a test so a future edit cannot drop it. `tests/test_windows_browser_discovery.py` (23 tests) resolves Chrome, Edge and Chrome-preferred-over-both from a faked Windows layout with an empty `PATH`, proves environment expansion via a `D:\Programme` fixture, proves the registry probe degrades rather than raises, asserts the POSIX lookup and backend order are untouched, and asserts both failure messages are distinguishable and neither suggests an install. The fixture asks `_windows_browser_candidates()` for the paths rather than restating them, so it cannot drift from the implementation and silently stop testing it. Verified with the full suite at 670 passing and no skips — a real Chrome is present on the verifying machine, so `test_capture_tabs.py`'s end-to-end capture tests ran rather than skipping.
- **Commit:** `600511f`

## windows-powershell-encoding-and-syntax

- **Implemented:** 2026-07-28
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/bootcamp-onboarding/ground-rules.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/normalize_docs_markdown.py`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-05-data-quality-mapping/phase3-test-load.md`, `tests/test_windows_powershell_guidance.py`
- **Summary:** New invariant established: INV-166 (byte-correct BOM-free UTF-8, no PowerShell redirection for generated files, mojibake detected and reported not repaired) and INV-167 (a PowerShell counterpart uses PowerShell syntax; quote-heavy code goes in a script file). Windows is a supported platform and several modules ship PowerShell blocks, but nothing documented PowerShell 5.1's semantics — so two silent corruptions and a recurring parser-error tax went unaddressed. Added a "Windows and PowerShell" section to `ground-rules.md` covering both encoding traps with their fixes (`-Encoding utf8` writes a BOM on 5.1 → `[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText` with `UTF8Encoding($false)`; `Get-Content` decodes as the system ANSI codepage → pass `-Encoding utf8` or use `[System.IO.File]::ReadAllText`), the five 5.1 syntax traps as a table with PowerShell-correct forms (`&&`/`||` → `A; if ($?) { B }`; `if` is not an expression; inline `python -c` quoting; `Start-Process -ArgumentList` splitting; here-strings are not heredocs), the `powershell.exe` 5.1 vs `pwsh` 7+ assumption, and the general rule that generated files go through Python or the file tools and quote-heavy code goes in a script file under `src/`. `phase3-test-load.md`'s input-BOM note now cross-references the section and names the far more damaging write-side case. `normalize_docs_markdown.py` gained `mojibake_lines()`, which warns on stderr per file before the recap renders, naming the affected line numbers. **Deviation from the spec, deliberate:** the spec proposed detecting the `Â`–`Ã` + C1 signature; the shipped detector instead round-trips any non-ASCII line through cp1252→UTF-8 and reports only lines that decode to something different and non-replacement. That is strictly stronger and produces no false positives on ordinary accented prose — `café`, `£20`, `João`, `© 2026`, `20°C ± 2`, CJK and emoji are all asserted clean. Detection is report-only (the spec permitted this): a repair would be a content change, which the normalizer's own `_signatures_compatible` guard forbids. One real limit is pinned as a test rather than left implicit: a corruption whose bytes land on cp1252-undefined slots (a right curly quote, `E2 80 9D` → `0x9D`) cannot round-trip and is undetectable this way; the reported failure — 25 em dashes — is in the detectable class. `tests/test_windows_powershell_guidance.py` (21 tests) covers the detector, the false-positive set, the guidance, and a repo-wide sweep asserting no PowerShell block chains with `&&`/`||` (there were none — it is a regression guard, with a second test guarding that the sweep actually inspects PowerShell blocks).
- **Commit:** `fbaaf3f`

## organization-search-requires-name-org

- **Implemented:** 2026-07-28
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/senzing_viz_server.py`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03b-truthset-visualization/visualization-api-reference.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03b-truthset-visualization/phase1-visualization.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-07-query-visualize-discover/phase1-query-visualize.md`, `tests/test_organization_search.py`, `tests/test_tab_set_is_singular.py`
- **Summary:** New invariant established: INV-164 (a name search must try `NAME_ORG`, not `NAME_FULL` alone, and must report the attributes tried) and INV-165 (an example or hint must be verified by actually running it). `senzing_viz_server.py:436` built its attribute document as `{"NAME_FULL": query}`; re-confirmed against the MCP server at implementation time (`search_docs`, category `data_mapping` → Senzing Entity Specification, "Name > Feature: NAME") that `NAME_ORG` is the organization name attribute and `NAME_FULL` is for a single-field name of unknown type, so an organization name sent as `NAME_FULL` matches nothing and raises no error — on a roughly half-organization dataset, half the population was silently unsearchable. `Model.search()` now iterates a `SEARCH_NAME_ATTRS = ("NAME_FULL", "NAME_ORG")` tuple through a `_search_one()` helper, stopping at the first attribute that matches (so the person case still costs one engine call), and an engine error on a later attribute can no longer discard a hit an earlier one produced. The response carries `attributes_tried`, and the UI renders an empty result as "No entity matched a NAME_FULL then NAME_ORG search for X" rather than "No matching entities found." (INV-115). The chips contract was being satisfied only nominally — chips were derived from real merged entities but never run, which is exactly why organization chips found nothing — so live chips are now verified through the same search path the click takes and dropped with a `console.warn`, and snapshot examples that return no match are dropped with a stderr line instead of silently falling back to merge data and rendering a card with an empty match key. The rule is stated in the any-language contract (`/api/search` and the chips section of `visualization-api-reference.md`), in `phase1-visualization.md`, and in Module 7's query step, since the defect propagated into a generated query program precisely because it lived only in the Python reference (INV-090/INV-124). `tests/test_organization_search.py` (18 tests) drives the real `search()` against a fake engine that matches a name only under the attribute it was mapped with — the behavior that makes the failure silent — and covers attribute order, fall-through, the empty-result wording, error handling, and the legacy three-argument binding signature. One pre-existing test was modified: `test_tab_set_is_singular.py::test_chips_are_suppressed_without_a_search_box` pinned the old chip one-liner's exact syntax; the behavior it guards (chips built only inside the `live` guard, so the snapshot ships no dead controls) is preserved and is now asserted structurally instead.
- **Commit:** `fbaaf3f`

## pdf-layout-verification-without-poppler

- **Implemented:** 2026-07-28

- **Summary:** Graduation Step 1b named `pdftoppm` / `pdfimages` as the tools for the two checks text extraction cannot substitute for, and poppler is absent on Windows by default — so on a Windows run the page raster and the honest image count silently did not run, the count fell back to the `/Subtype /Image` grep the skill itself warns overcounts, and the recap was reported verified with its layout never inspected. Fixed as guidance, since these checks are agent-performed: the image count now has a four-step preference order whose first two rungs need no external tool at all — the generator's own `embedded N of M images` line, then **Pillow**, which `fpdf2` already pulls into the Step 1b venv (so it is *already importable*, not a new install) — with `pdfimages -list` third and the grep fourth, explicitly labeled as overcounting. Added a ⛔ "Say what you could not verify" rule requiring any check skipped for a missing tool to be recorded as skipped, and requiring the mandatory closing announcement to state in one plain sentence what was not verified — with an example line — so "verified" never silently means "verified except for the two strongest checks". The feedback's suggested `scoop install poppler` was **not** adopted: INV-129 forbids a verification step installing a tool to satisfy itself, so the skill now names that prohibition explicitly and a test asserts the three package-manager install commands can appear only as things not to do. Non-blocking (INV-048/INV-052/INV-066) and agent-side (INV-012) framing preserved throughout. `tests/test_pdf_verification_toolchain.py` (11 tests) pins the poppler-free count route, the Windows naming, the skip-reporting requirement, and the no-install rule.

## recap-pdf-images-resolve-against-recap-directory

- **Implemented:** 2026-07-28
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/generate_recap_pdf.py`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/graduation/SKILL.md`, `tests/test_recap_pdf_images.py`
- **Summary:** `_render_image()` resolved a relative `![alt](path)` against `Path.cwd()`, so the document-relative paths graduation Step 1a instructs (`visualizations/x.png`, relative to `docs/bootcamp_recap.md`) were looked for at `<project>/visualizations/…` when Step 1b ran the generator from the project root — every screenshot was dropped, silently, while the success line reported ~99% of characters rendered because the characters did render. Relative paths now resolve against the **input recap's own directory** first (`set_image_context()`, called from `main()`), with `Path.cwd()` retained as a second candidate so invocations that already worked keep working; an absolute path is still used as given. Each image's outcome is recorded once — keyed by the path as written, because the fpdf2 renderer builds the document twice for TOC page numbers and so reaches every image twice — and anything other than success is reported on stderr, distinguishing "not found" (naming the directories searched), "remote URL, never fetched" (INV-081 preserved) and "unreadable (<ExceptionName>)", since those need different remedies (INV-111). The render stays non-fatal: exit 0 and a valid PDF regardless (INV-048). The success line now carries `embedded N of M images` alongside the character figure — the count retention structurally cannot see (INV-110) — with an explicit note when the stdlib fallback is used, since it embeds no images and a bare `embedded 0 of 6` would read as a lookup failure. `--check` now also flags any `![](…)` target that resolves to no file, so a lost screenshot surfaces where it can still be fixed, and still writes no PDF. Step 1b's guidance states that image paths are document-relative and resolved that way, tells the reader not to "fix" a path to `docs/visualizations/…` (which breaks the Markdown recap) nor to `cd docs` before rendering, and tells them to read the new image count rather than treating retention as covering it. Verified end-to-end on a fixture reproducing the original failure: rendering from the project root embeds 6 of 6 (6 image XObjects at the fixture's 160px width, plus the logos), byte-identical to rendering from `docs/`, and identical again via an absolute `--input` from `/`. Coverage lives in a new `tests/test_recap_pdf_images.py` (13 tests) rather than as an extension of `test_recap_pdf_guard.py`, which continues to pass unchanged.
- **Commit:** `1fe3252`

## deep-dive-audit-2026-07-28

- **Not a spec** — a third full-repo invariant-conformance and coherence audit the maintainer requested

  Static analysis plus execution probes and page rasterization; the conversational invariants
  (INV-005–INV-009, gate ordering) are out of reach of this method and still need a `dry-run`.
- **Invariant established:** **INV-159** — no generator may reduce a Bootcamper-authored character to
  `?`; unprintable characters are folded to ASCII where possible (including atomic Latin letters) or
  dropped, never encoded; a name in a non-Latin script is not transliterated by the plugin but warned
  about, placeholder-substituted, and routed to INV-113's question; the font-safety inventory covers
  names.
- **Findings fixed:**
  1. **INV-143 violated on the certificate (HIGH, verified by rasterizing).** `_safe()` ended in
     `.encode("latin-1", "replace")`, so a name in any non-Latin script printed as `?` — a Bootcamper
     named 李明 got **`?? (Li Ming)`** at 34 pt on the page they frame, at exit 0 with no warning.
     INV-134 detects the name from `git config user.name`, so this is the ordinary path, not an edge
     case, and it affects CJK, Cyrillic, Arabic, Hebrew, Greek, Devanagari and Thai names alike.
     `_safe` now folds (NFKD + `_LATIN_FOLD` for `Ł Đ Œ …`, which have no decomposition — "ukasz" is
     not a lesser rendering of "Łukasz") and drops the rest; `_unrepresentable()` reports what was
     lost; `_cert_fields` substitutes the placeholder rather than a blank recipient line; `main()`
     warns naming the characters; graduation's INV-113 test gains "a name the recap PDF cannot print"
     with an explicit instruction *not* to transliterate it for them. The font-safety inventory
     covered punctuation and symbols only — it now covers names (8 scripts + 4 folding cases).
  2. **The INV-157 guard shipped that morning misfired (MEDIUM).** `_summary_block_label` required a
     colon, so `**Files produced**` above a bullet list — or `#### Files produced` — read as absent:
     `--check` failed a complete recap, the PDF printed "Files produced: (not recorded)" *beneath the
     files that were there*, and graduation was directed to backfill content it already had (INV-085).
     Colon-less lines are now matched exactly against the canonical labels, so an arbitrary bold
     phrase still cannot pass for one.
  3. **INV-050 misattributed `config/license.json` to Module 2 (LOW-MED).** It is written in Module 4
     Step 7, where `single-license-gate-at-data-processing` moved license detection; Module 2 only
     reads the limit. Same stale-enumeration class as INV-104's tab list. Corrected in place with a
     note; the file and its purpose are unchanged.
  4. **Two of three shipped slash commands were undocumented (LOW-MED, INV-003).** `/start-bootcamp`

     table and `README.md` points at it.
  5. **The certificate name had no final clip (LOW).** Shrinking stops at 12 pt, so a ~78-character
     name drew from x = −18 mm — off the card and off the page, the INV-121 class, on the one page

  6. **INV-063 and INV-120 still described the nudge in pre-INV-158 vocabulary (LOW, coherence).**

## name-the-claude-interface

- **Summary:** Retired "the Claude app" and made every interface reference say which interface. Canonical names: **Claude Desktop**, **Claude Code CLI**, **the Claude web app**, **a Claude IDE extension**, with "Claude Code" reserved for the product — the distinction that was missing, since Claude Desktop runs Claude Code too, which is why `README.md` could offer "Claude Desktop (desktop)" against "Claude Code (command line)" as if they were rival products. **Maintainer-decided before the sweep** (asked because both answers changed ~30 strings): the terminal is "Claude Code CLI" rather than "Claude CLI", and the web/IDE interfaces are kept and named rather than collapsed into two — collapsing would have narrowed INV-098's coverage for a Bootcamper in claude.ai/code or VS Code. Swept the nudge in `ground-rules.md` and its copy in `graduation/SKILL.md`: both pinned question forms (the non-CLI one now substitutes the single interface the Bootcamper is on, `{Claude Desktop | the Claude web app | your Claude IDE extension}`), both "how to change it" lines, and the per-stage table note in `ground-rules.md` and its INV-114 twin `docs/model-selection.md`. Added a **Naming the Claude interface** section to `ground-rules.md` so the rule governs all output and not just the nudge, including the product-vs-interface split and the one sanctioned vague form ("in your Claude interface", allowed only where the interface genuinely cannot be determined). Install docs rewritten: `README.md` now leads "This is a Claude Code plugin, and Claude Code has two interfaces you can run it in", heads its walkthrough "Using Claude Desktop", and renames the troubleshooting section "Claude code inoperative" → "Claude Desktop inoperative" (its body was already entirely about Desktop); `docs/README.md` becomes "Using the Claude Code CLI", drops its stray "Claude CLI", and links back to the Desktop path. Both sides' anchors were updated together and are now pinned by a test, because a renamed heading breaks a Markdown anchor with nothing failing. `Claude app`/`Claude application` is registered in the retired-vocabulary registry (mutation-verified: it catches a re-introduction in `README.md`), and that registry now also scans the repo-root install docs `propagate-to-public` mirrors as user-facing — their exclusion is how the phrase survived there. INV-098's own text was clarified in place ("surface" → "interface", the vague controls phrasing replaced) with a no-meaning-change note; its four interfaces and INV-069's pinned gate are untouched. 12 new tests; 573 green.
- **Invariant established:** **INV-158** — every Claude-interface reference names which one from a fixed set of four; "Claude Code" is the product, never an interface; "the Claude app" is retired; vague wording only where the interface cannot be determined; both install docs name their interface and cross-link with resolving anchors.

## end-of-module-summary-blocks-guaranteed

- **Implemented:** 2026-07-28
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/generate_recap_pdf.py`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/bootcamp-onboarding/module-completion.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/graduation/SKILL.md`, `tests/test_recap_summary_blocks.py` (new), `tests/test_recap_pdf_guard.py`, `specs/INVARIANTS.md`
- **Summary:** Fixes a reported silent content loss in the terminal deliverable: a bootcamp's recap PDF rendered its End-of-Module Summary with none of What you accomplished / Files produced / Why it matters. Root cause was an unenforced clause of INV-103 — it has required those blocks since 2026-07-23 *and* said `--check` must validate them, but `missing_required()` compares H3 headings only, so nothing looked below the heading. Every signal reported success (`Recap complete`, `PDF generated:`, ~100% retention) because the prose that was written did reach the page. Closed at three layers, since any one alone leaves the hole: **detect** — `END_SUMMARY_BLOCKS` plus `ModuleSection.missing_summary_blocks()` feed `verify_recap`, so `--check` fails naming each missing block and the pre-render audit warns (non-blocking per INV-110/INV-048); **render** — both renderers now draw every required block, `(not recorded)` where the recap has none, including when the whole subsection is absent, so an omission can no longer look like a finished page; **author** — `module-completion.md` requires the three labels explicitly ("never as one prose paragraph") and verifies them in the Step 2c re-read it already performs, and graduation Step 1a backfills them from the module's own recorded content before rendering, with an explicit prohibition on inventing content to fill a label (INV-065's principle). Detection is deliberately tolerant (`**Label:**`, `**Label**:`, `- **Label:**`, bare `Label:`) via a separate `_summary_block_label` — `_block_label` keeps its narrower spacing job and its `- **Q:**` exclusion — because a false "missing" would send graduation to rewrite a finished section (INV-085); legacy `### Journal` sections are exempt through `_is_legacy_journal`, as INV-103 tolerates them, and are neither reported nor annotated. A wholly missing summary is still reported once, as a missing subsection. Verified by rasterizing the module page (INV-129) for the prose, labeled, absent-subsection and legacy cases, in both renderers. Notably `test_recap_pdf_guard.py`'s own `GOOD_RECAP` fixture was an instance of the defect — its summary was a single prose line — which is how the gap survived a 500-test suite; fixed. 20 new tests; 561 green.
- **Invariant established:** **INV-157** — the blocks INV-103 requires inside the End-of-Module Summary are validated by `--check`, reported by the audit, and rendered by both renderers (as `(not recorded)` when unrecorded), with tolerant detection, the legacy-Journal exemption, and no invented backfill.
- **Commit:** `381ec40`

## certificate-of-completion-from-template

- **Implemented:** 2026-07-28
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/generate_recap_pdf.py`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/docs/examples/bootcamp_recap.example.pdf`, `tests/test_recap_pdf_certificate.py` (new), `tests/test_recap_pdf_guard.py`, `specs/INVARIANTS.md`
- **Summary:** The recap's final page now follows `resources/certificate-of-completion.pdf`, discharging the last open acceptance criterion of `landscape-certificate-of-completion` ("If/when a `resources/` certificate template exists, the certificate layout is driven from it"), which had been deferred because no template existed. Both renderers were rebuilt on one shared set of millimeter constants measured off the template at 150 dpi — band, card, per-line baselines, signature blocks, seal — replacing two independently hard-coded designs; `_cert_line`, `_cert_wrap`, `_wrap_to_width`, `_cert_module_layout` and `_cert_seal_paths` are shared, so the stdlib fallback is now a plainer rendering of the same page (verified positionally: every shared line matches within 0.5 pt) instead of a second layout. Palette additions are brand-derived, not sampled: `AMBER` is `EMBER_GRAD_END` (the band mirrors the brand's own gradient pair) and `MUTED` is blended from body ink toward the warm off-white the way `TABLE_HEAD_FILL` is derived — `_FALLBACK_RGB` extended in step (INV-107). Only the *light* wordmark ships, so it is repainted in dark ink at render time for the white card (RGB only, original alpha re-attached — an opaque paste printed the whole canvas as a dark block, which extraction cannot see), cropped to its ink and downsampled to 1000 px (2500 dpi → 600 dpi at 41 mm, ~40 KB rather than ~80 KB in a keepsake PDF); Pillow or asset absent falls back to drawn text with the ember "z". Content honesty: the template's "all 10 modules" became the recap's real count, its arc description was reattached to *the bootcamp* rather than to what the bootcamper completed, and the modules completed are still named on the page (INV-100). The module list — the one variable-length block on a fixed page with the auto page-break off — is now fitted (narrow measure → full card width → type size → truncation last), and an over-long recipient name shrinks to fit instead of running off the card. Letterspacing is real (`set_char_spacing` / `Tc`), so the name and small caps still extract as words. Verified by rasterizing at 110–150 dpi against the template, both renderers; example PDF re-rendered from `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/` (5 image objects, screenshot intact). `tests/test_recap_pdf_guard.py` gained `drawn_runs_by_page` and its off-page bound is now per page — the portrait bound it used was never right for a landscape certificate and only passed while every certificate line happened to be centered; its border-clearance test now derives the bound from the card constants. 541 tests green, plus 16 new certificate tests.
- **Invariant established:** **INV-156** — the certificate is laid out from the template through one shared set of geometry constants both renderers read; the citation counts only the modules actually completed; the module list is fitted rather than allowed to overrun; letterspacing goes through the text state; colors are `brand_tokens` or derived from it.
- **Commit:** `09cb722`

- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-03b-truthset-visualization/visualization-api-reference.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-07-query-visualize-discover/phase2b-discover.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-04-data-collection/SKILL.md`, `specs/INVARIANTS.md`, `tests/test_partial_row_and_schema_coverage.py`
- **Summary:** The contract and the Discover call site now state that `response_schemas` for the
  graph methods **stops at the top-level arrays**, require dumping one raw link element before
  writing the parser, and carry the new partial-row rule: when some fields of a row populate and
  others are blank, the blanks are a wrong field name, not thin data. `get_version` / `get_license`
  are named as methods with an empty entry, at the contract and at Module 4's license parse.
  **Two of this spec's claims were wrong and were corrected by querying the server:** `find_network`
  *does* have a `response_schemas` entry (it just documents only `ENTITY_PATHS[]`, `ENTITIES[]`,
  `ENTITY_NETWORK_LINKS[]`), while `get_license`'s empty result is confirmed.
  **⚠️ Deliberately unmet criterion:** documenting the `MIN_ENTITY_ID` / `MAX_ENTITY_ID` endpoint
  keys "verified from a dumped raw response". Verification needs a live loaded engine, unavailable
  here, and the keys are in no MCP source — writing them would assert an unverified Senzing fact
  (INV-080), the error this repo already retracted once for `SZ_EXPORT_ALL_FLAGS`. The defense
  shipped instead of the datum: the divergence is recorded as a caution marked *not MCP-confirmable*
  and *never the names to code against*, and the tests assert **no** specific field name. To close
  it, dump one link element on a loaded engine and promote the caution to a verified field list.
  Tests **481 → 490**; all seven new assertions confirmed to fail against the pre-change files. One
  test-helper fix: the guidance lives in a Markdown blockquote, so whitespace collapsing alone left
  `>` markers mid-phrase — the helper now strips them.
- **Invariants:** INV-148, INV-149.
- **Commit:** `a2e4363`

## analyzer-legacy-sublist-format-false-errors

- **Implemented:** 2026-07-26
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-05-data-quality-mapping/phase1-quality-assessment.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-05-data-quality-mapping/phase2-data-mapping.md`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-05-data-quality-mapping/phase3-test-load.md`, `specs/INVARIANTS.md`, `tests/test_legacy_sublist_format_is_supported.py`
- **Summary:** Split the analyzer's output into **structural invalidity** (blocking) and
  **conformance to the recommended schema** (informational) in `phase2`, with the exit code removed
  as a gate, the Entity Specification's "While we still support that" quoted and marked for
  per-session MCP re-confirmation (INV-080), `No NAME features found` explained as an artifact of
  where the analyzer looks, a one-record load probe made the arbiter with its conclusion recorded
  (INV-125), and hand-writing a mapper to clear a conformance finding forbidden outright.
  **The defect was in three files, not the one the spec named.** `phase3-test-load.md` instructed
  "Fix the structural errors ... in the transformation program" for the flat format — literally the
  five-mapper rewrite the spec exists to prevent — and `phase1-quality-assessment.md`'s CORD
  fast-path readiness check required a `FEATURES` array, classifying every legacy-shaped CORD source
  as not-ready at the earliest gate and routing loadable data into a mapping phase it did not need.
  Both fixed. **Two claims in the spec were corrected by verifying against the MCP server rather
  than trusting it:** (1) the legacy shape is not "the sub-list format" but "a flat JSON structure
  *with* a separate sub-list for each feature that had multiple values" — sampling showed London/
  `GLOBALDATA` returns a `FEATURES` array while Las Vegas/`PPP_LOANS` returns flat root attributes
  with **no** sub-lists, so a sub-list-keyed check would still have misjudged it, and CORD is now
  documented as shipping both forms; (2) the analyzer does not contradict the specification — the
  same section's validation rules do say `FEATURES (required, array)`, so the analyzer applies the
  *recommended* schema's rules while the prose grants continued support for the *legacy* shape.
  Both true, answering different questions; the guidance says so instead of calling the analyzer
  wrong. Tests **457 → 471**; all nine new guidance assertions were confirmed to **fail against the
  pre-change files**. Not verifiable here: the end-to-end criterion "a CORD run reaches the test
  load without a hand-written conversion" — verified instead by removing every instruction that
  would cause one (grep across the plugin plus the new tests), not by running a bootcamp.
- **Invariants:** INV-144, INV-145.
- **Commit:** `9d2c43f`

## discoveries-pdf-real-tables-and-paragraph-spacing

- **Implemented:** 2026-07-26
- **Files changed:** `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/generate_discoveries_pdf.py`, `plugins/senzing-bootcamp/scripts/generate_recap_pdf.py`, `specs/INVARIANTS.md`, `tests/test_discoveries_pdf.py`, `tests/test_recap_pdf_font_safety.py`
- **Summary:** Reviewed and landed the uncommitted generator work (tables as a real grid, generalized
  block spacing, `_UNICODE_MAP` additions), then closed the gaps it left. Verified by **rasterizing**
  pages, not by exit code or retention (INV-129): raw pipe lines **55 → 0** on a stress fixture,
  grids draw with shaded headers, the header repeats across a page break with the following body row
  in the **body font** (the regression stays fixed), ragged rows pad/truncate without shifting a
  column origin, the stdlib fallback emits aligned columns and still announces itself on stderr
  (INV-111), and the INV-110 guard is unchanged. **Three defects found during verification, all
  fixed:** (1) two adjacent tables shared an edge and read as one grid with a bold middle row —
  `_needs_item_gap` gapped a table before prose but not before another table; (2) thirteen further
  characters still corrupted to `?` (`≈ ≤ ≥ ≠ ∞ € ™ ⇒ ↑ ↓ ←`, non-breaking hyphen, zero-width space)
  — `↔`/`⚠️` were not the whole gap, and the widened inventory found them immediately; (3) the
  label-continuation split is now fixed **at the cause** — the parser absorbs continuation lines into
  the label block, so the paragraph reflows and the gap-suppression carve-out was removed. The empty
  leading table column is **accepted, not fixed**, reasoned in `parse_table`'s docstring: dropping it
  would delete a real row-label column's values. Tests **437 → 457**; the new pipe-count,
  table-structure, adjacent-table, page-break-font, paragraph-gap and font-safety probes were each
  confirmed to **fail against the pre-change scripts** (rendered from `HEAD`, 55 pipe lines, no grid,
  paragraph gap identical to the line advance at 15.6 pt). Paragraph-spacing assertions are
  self-calibrating — comparing a paragraph break against a plain line advance measured from the same
  document — rather than hardcoded thresholds that a type change would silently invalidate.
- **Invariants:** INV-142, INV-143.
- **Commit:** `a53f865`
